1:2.notes: Al-hamd formula triggers 'praise'. Ar-Rahman/Ar-Rahim triggers 'mercy'. 'Lord of the Worlds' asserts sovereignty. 'Master of the Day of Judgment' triggers 'day-of-judgment'.

1:5.notes: 'It is You alone we worship' is a tawhid declaration. 'Guide us to the straight path' is an uttered supplication triggering dua-guidance. The section is itself recited in every prayer, and 'we worship / we call for help' frames it as an act of prayer.

1:7.notes: Continuation of the supplication for guidance from 1:5 — dua-guidance straddles both sections per rule 1. 'Those You have blessed' vs. 'those against whom there is anger / those who are misguided': per Ibn Kathir and the labeling instructions §10, the two negative descriptions map to Jews and Christians respectively, warranting 'people-of-the-book'. Confidence medium on 'people-of-the-book' because the verse uses descriptive categories rather than naming the groups explicitly; tafsir is the tie-breaker here.

19:1.notes: Section opens with Kaf-Ha-Ya-Ayn-Sad (disjoined letters). Zechariah's uttered supplication asking for an heir (Rabbi inna wahana...) qualifies as dua-family-offspring. John's name announced ('a name We have never given before'). 'I created you before, when you were nothing' asserts power. 'Never disappointed in my prayer to you' asserts nearness-and-response. Miraculous birth announced to an elderly man with a barren wife = miracles.

19:10.notes: Zechariah is given the sign of three nights of speechlessness — a miracle. He signals his people to 'praise morning and evening' — the act of praising is uttered/commanded by gesture; tagging praise for the explicit content of his signal (tasbihu). Confidence adjusted from high since the praise is indirect (signaled rather than uttered in text), but the Arabic 'sabbihoo' is explicit.

19:12.notes: 'Hold on to the Scripture firmly' — this refers to the Torah/previous scriptures, so previous-scriptures applies. 'He was devout' (taqiyyan) — taqwa is named explicitly. 'Tenderness from Us' = mercy. 'Day he was born... day he dies... Day he is raised alive' = death-and-dying and resurrection. prophethood-general for John's character as a prophet-child.

19:16.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Mary's uttered 'I take refuge... in the Most Merciful' = dua-protection. 'It is easy for Me' = power. 'A sign for humanity' = mankind. 'A matter already decided' = divine-decree. Stream and dates = provision. Virgin birth = miracles and human-creation. Unmarried pregnancy context = marriage-and-family. Angel/Spirit appearing = angels.

19:27.notes: 'O sister of Aaron' names Aaron explicitly. The accusation against Mary = slander-and-backbiting (per Ibn Kathir and §11 of instructions). Jesus speaking in the cradle = miracles. 'Made me a prophet' = prophethood-general. 'Enjoined on me prayer and charity' = prayer and zakat-and-charity. 'Day I was born... day I die... Day I get resurrected' = death-and-dying and resurrection.

19:34.notes: 'It is not for Allah to have a child — glory be to Him' = tawhid refuting shirk; 'subhanahu' = praise uttered. 'Be and it becomes' = power. 'Woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a tremendous Day' = disbelievers + day-of-judgment. 'Day of Regret' = day-of-judgment. 'We will inherit the earth' = divine-decree / sovereignty — tagging divine-decree for the decreed return. Mary named as mother of Jesus in verse 34.

19:41.notes: Abraham named as subject; Isaac and Jacob explicitly granted in v.49. Iblis named ('the devil is disobedient to the Most Gracious'; 'do not worship the devil'). Father's idol-worship = shirk. 'I will guide you along a straight way' = guidance named explicitly. 'Out of Our mercy' = mercy. All three are made prophets = prophethood-general.

19:51.notes: Four prophets named: Moses, Aaron, Ishmael, Idris. 'Brought him near in communion' = nearness-and-response. 'Out of Our mercy' (twice) = mercy. 'Enjoin prayer and charity' = prayer + zakat-and-charity. 'He was dedicated/chosen' (mukhlas) = sincerity named explicitly.

19:58.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Adam, Noah, Abraham named; 'Israel' (Jacob) referenced as ancestor of the prophets; 'descendants of Adam...those We carried with Noah...descendants of Abraham and Israel' = adam, noah, abraham, children-of-israel. Prostrating and weeping at revelations = the-quran. 'Lost the prayers' = prayer (negatively). 'Those who repent' = repentance named explicitly. 'Enter Paradise' = paradise. 'Those who are devout' (taqiyyan) = taqwa. 'Those We guided' = guidance considered but guidance label is about God as source; covered by prophethood-general context. Believers implied for the righteous remnant.

19:64.notes: Angels speaking ('We do not descend except by command of your Lord') — angel speech addressing the Prophet. 'Your Lord is never forgetful' = knowledge. 'Lord of the heavens and the earth' = sovereignty + creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Persevere in His service' = patience named explicitly (istabar).

19:66.notes: 'The human being says, when I am dead will I be brought back alive?' = mankind + resurrection. 'We created him before when he was nothing' = human-creation. 'Round them up and the devils' = iblis. 'Bring them around Hell on their knees' = hell. 'This has been an unavoidable decree of your Lord' = divine-decree. 'Those who were devout' (ittaqaw) = taqwa. 'Wrongdoers' = disbelievers. Day of gathering = day-of-judgment.

19:73.notes: Disbelievers address believers in a taunt = both groups. 'How many a generation have We destroyed' = punishment-of-past-nations. 'Say, whoever is in error the Most Merciful will lead him on' = qul-statements. 'Allah increases in guidance those who accept guidance' = guidance named explicitly. 'When they see the punishment or the Hour' = day-of-judgment. 'Extending the agony' + 'comes to Us alone' = hell context. 'Denied Our revelations' = denial-of-revelation.

19:81.notes: Taking gods besides Allah = shirk. 'We dispatch the devils against the disbelievers' = iblis. 'Gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as guests' = paradise + mercy + taqwa (implied by 'righteous/muttaqin' — but taqwa: 'righteous' here is al-muttaqin, explicitly naming the muttaqin). 'Herd the sinners into hell' = hell. 'No power of intercession' = intercession. Day of gathering = day-of-judgment.

19:88.notes: 'The Most Merciful has begotten a son' = shirk being refuted = tawhid. 'It is not fitting for the Most Merciful to have a son' = tawhid. 'The heavens almost rupture, the earth splits' = creation-of-heavens-earth (invoked as witness to the gravity). 'None in the heavens and the earth but will come as a servant' = sovereignty + mankind (all creation addressed). 'He has enumerated them and counted them one by one' = knowledge. 'Day of Resurrection alone' = day-of-judgment.

19:96.notes: 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will give them love' = believers + mercy. 'We made it easy in your tongue' = direct address to the Prophet (second person 'your tongue') = muhammad + the-quran. 'Deliver good news to the righteous' = taqwa (muttaqin named explicitly).

19:98.notes: 'How many a generation have We destroyed before them?' = punishment-of-past-nations. The implied audience is the disbelieving Quraysh / opponents = disbelievers.

67:1.notes: tabaraka opens the surah — tag praise. 'Almighty, the Forgiving' → power + mercy. Seven heavens in layers → creation-of-heavens-earth. Flawless creation argument → wisdom. 'Created death and life' → creation + death-and-dying.

67:5.notes: Stars as missiles against devils → cosmic-bodies + iblis. Hell torment for disbelievers (vv.6–11) → hell + disbelievers. Keepers ask 'Has no warner come?' → prophethood-general + denial-of-revelation. 'Those who fear their Lord in secret… forgiveness and great reward' → taqwa + mercy + believers (implicit at close, per §5.2 generous tagging policy).

67:13.notes: 'He is Aware of inner thoughts' / 'Would He not know, He Who created? He is the Refined, the Expert' → knowledge. 'Eat of His provisions' → provision. Earth made manageable, travel its regions → natural-signs. Verses 16–17 warn of earth collapsing / violent storm — divine power over nature → power. Verse 18 references past nations who denied → punishment-of-past-nations. The address 'you' is universal humanity throughout → mankind.

67:19.notes: Birds held aloft only by the Compassionate → natural-signs + mercy + power. 'Who will provide for you if He withholds His provision?' → provision. Disbelievers in delusion / defiance → disbelievers. Straight path vs. bent walker metaphor → guidance (explicitly named as 'better guided' / 'straight path', meeting rule-5 trigger).

67:23.notes: Three 'Say:' (qul) commands in vv.23, 24, 26 → qul-statements. 'He produced you and made for you hearing, vision, organs' → human-creation + mankind. 'To Him you will be rounded up' → day-of-judgment. 'Knowledge is with Allah, I am only a clear warner' → knowledge + prophethood-general. 'Rarely do you give thanks' — shukr explicitly named → gratitude (concrete trigger met per rule 5). Disbelievers' faces turning gloomy → disbelievers.

67:28.notes: Two 'Say:' commands in vv.28 and 29 → qul-statements. 'He bestows His mercy on us' → mercy. 'Who will protect the disbelievers from an agonizing torment?' → hell + disbelievers. 'We have faith in Him, and in Him we trust' — tawakkul explicitly stated → trust-in-god.

67:30.notes: Single verse with 'Say:' → qul-statements. Water draining away / pure running water → provision + natural-signs. The rhetorical challenge implies God's exclusive power over sustenance → power.

112:4.notes: Continuation of the Qul declaration from 112:1; qul-statements held back because the imperative itself is in §1 only — pending §1 straddling rule call.

2:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Mim disjoined letters. Section describes the muttaqin who believe in the unseen, pray, give, and believe in prior revelation.

2:6.notes: Allah seals the hearts of disbelievers; severe torment awaits. Divine-decree tagged because Allah actively seals their hearing and sight.

2:8.notes: Classic munafiqun passage — they say 'we believe' but do not; painful punishment mentioned.

2:11.notes: Hypocrites deny making fasad while being the fasad-makers; they mock believers as 'fools'; they barter error for guidance.

2:17.notes: Parable of fire extinguished — simile for loss of divine light/guidance. No named figures, no du'a, no eschatology directly invoked.

2:19.notes: Storm/thunderbolt parable for disbelievers; 'Allah is capable of everything' — power attribute. Rain/thunder are natural-signs imagery.

2:21.notes: Direct address 'O people' (ya ayyuha al-nas). Creator who made earth, sky, sends rain for provision; ends with prohibition against assigning rivals (shirk). 'That you may attain piety' names taqwa.

2:23.notes: Classic tahaddi passage; fire prepared for disbelievers if they cannot produce a surah like it.

2:25.notes: Good news to believers of gardens with rivers; pure spouses; eternal abode. Provision label applies to the fruits described.

2:26.notes: Verse 26 addresses believers vs disbelievers on parables; verse 27 describes those who break Allah's covenant and corrupt the earth — covenant and corruption-on-earth explicitly named.

2:28.notes: How can you deny when He gave you life, will cause death, then revive you? Creation of seven heavens; 'He is aware of all things' — knowledge attribute.

2:30.notes: Angels ask about placing successor who will cause corruption (corruption-on-earth explicitly invoked by angels' question). Allah teaches Adam names — knowledge. Angels say 'You are the Knowledgeable, the Wise' — knowledge + wisdom closing formula.

2:34.notes: Iblis refuses to bow — arrogance explicitly noted ('was arrogant'). Adam and spouse in Garden; Satan causes them to slip; 'He is the Relenting, the Merciful' — mercy. Guidance promised to those who follow it.

2:40.notes: Direct address to Bani Israel. Covenant with God to fulfill pledge. Commands to pray, give zakat, and seek help through patience and prayer (v.45). 'Seek help through patience and prayer' names patience explicitly. Previous scriptures referenced. Prophethood implied via 'what was revealed to you' and what preceded.

2:47.notes: Reminders to Bani Israel of favors; warning of a Day when no intercession accepted; Pharaoh's persecution; parting of sea (miracle); 40-night appointment of Moses; calf worship (shirk).

2:53.notes: Moses given Scripture and Criterion; calf-worship, repentance commanded; 'He is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful'; thunderbolt and revival (miracle); manna and quails (provision). Repentance explicitly named ('repent to your Maker').

2:58.notes: Entry into town, command to say 'pardon'; wrongdoers substituted and a plague came — punishment of past nations pattern. Mercy promised to the virtuous.

2:60.notes: Moses strikes rock — twelve springs (miracle); 'eat and drink from Allah's provision'; 'do not corrupt the earth' (corruption-on-earth explicitly commanded against); struck with humiliation for disbelief, killing prophets — punishment of past nations. Prophethood-general: killing of prophets mentioned.

2:62.notes: Jews, Christians, Sabeans, believers — all named. Covenant (pledge raised over them). Allah will judge on Day of Resurrection. His mercy/grace saves them from loss.

2:67.notes: Moses commands sacrifice of heifer; the murder-victim struck with it to reveal killer (miracle: dead brought back to life). 'Allah is not unaware' — knowledge. Murder (anger-and-violence) is the underlying trigger.

2:75.notes: Some of them distort scripture knowingly (hypocrisy/denial); follow what devils recited about Solomon's kingdom — sorcery (Harut and Marut context is here but that label is separate); fire/hell for buyers of evil; 'If they believed and were righteous, reward would be better.' Harut and Marut named in v.102 — see 2:101 section.

2:83.notes: Covenant with Bani Israel: worship Allah, good to parents, orphans, needy, pray, give zakat (explicit). Then killing own people, expelling them (war/violence), ransoming captives (manumission-and-captives). Day of Resurrection — severe torment. Righteous-conduct: 'speak nicely to people' / comprehensive righteousness list. 10 labels — within ceiling.

2:87.notes: Moses given Scripture; messengers sent; Jesus son of Mary given clear proofs supported with Holy Spirit (miracle); arrogance of Bani Israel killing prophets explicitly stated ('you grew arrogant'); calf worship; denial of scripture. 9 labels.

2:93.notes: Covenant and Mount; 'We hear and disobey'; hearts filled with love of calf (shirk). Two qul imperatives ('Say, Wretched is what...' and 'Say, If the Final Home is yours...'). If they die disbelievers, their deeds come to nothing on Day of Judgment. Death/hell implied.

2:97.notes: Gabriel named (angel); Michael named; 'Say, whoever is hostile to Gabriel' — qul-statement. The Quran revealed by Gabriel. Covenant broken repeatedly. Knowledge: 'Allah knows what they conceal.' Disbelief: Allah is enemy to the faithless.

2:101.notes: People of the Book threw the Book behind their backs; followed what devils taught during Solomon's reign; Harut and Marut (named angels) in Babylon teaching witchcraft (sorcery); sorcery causes separation between man and wife (marriage-and-family). Angels label covers Harut and Marut.

2:104.notes: Address to believers ('O you who believe'). People of the Book and polytheists referenced. 'Allah chooses for His mercy whomever He wills' — mercy. Qul: 'Say, Produce your proof.'

2:106.notes: Abrogation of verses — the-quran. Sovereignty of heavens and earth. Power: 'Allah is capable of all things.' People of the Book wish to turn believers away — envy explicitly stated ('out of envy on their part'). Prayer and zakat commanded (v.110). Knowledge: 'Allah is Seeing of everything.' 10 labels.

2:111.notes: Jews say only Jews enter heaven; Christians say only Christians. 'Say, Produce your proof' — qul. Allah will judge on Day of Resurrection. Whoever submits to Allah — tawhid underpinning.

2:114.notes: Forbidding remembrance of Allah's name in mosques — remembrance. 'To Allah belongs the East and the West' — sovereignty. 'Allah is Omnipresent and Omniscient' — knowledge. Punishment in this world and hereafter (hell implied).

2:116.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. 'Allah has begotten a son — be He glorified' (Subhanahu) = praise + tawhid + shirk refutation. Originator of heavens and earth (creation). 'Be and it becomes' (power). Muhammad sent with truth (prophethood-general). 'Say, Allah's guidance is the guidance' (qul-statements + guidance). People of the Book referenced. The-quran: discusses revelation given. Sovereignty: His is everything in heavens/earth.

2:122.notes: Reminder to Bani Israel of favors; warning of Day when no intercession/ransom. Abraham tested and made imam of humanity (covenant/pledge theme). Abraham's prayer for descendants and covenant not to include wrongdoers.

2:125.notes: The House as focal point — sacred-mosque. Prayer: 'Use shrine of Abraham as place of prayer.' Abraham and Ishmael commissioned to sanctify the House for those who circle/pray. Abraham's du'a: 'O My Lord, make this a peaceful land and provide its people with fruits' — dua-family-offspring (for his descendants) and provision. Hell: those who disbelieve consigned to Fire.

2:127.notes: Abraham and Ishmael raise foundations — both named. Multiple uttered du'as: 'Our Lord, accept it from us' (dua-gratitude borderline, but primarily asking acceptance); 'make us submissive... show us our rites... accept our repentance' (dua-forgiveness); 'raise up among them a messenger' (dua-family-offspring for descendants/community). 'You are the Acceptor of Repentance, the Merciful' — mercy. 'The Hearer, the Knower' — knowledge. 'The Almighty, the Wise' — wisdom. Prophethood: du'a for a messenger.

2:130.notes: Who would forsake Abraham's religion? Abraham chosen in this world and hereafter. 'Submit to the Lord of the Worlds' — tawhid. Abraham exhorts his sons and Jacob — both Jacob and the patriarchal lineage (Isaac and Ishmael implied by context of 'his sons'). Jacob explicitly named. Prophethood: Abraham as chosen prophet.

2:133.notes: Jacob at deathbed — death-and-dying. His sons declare worship of One God (tawhid) — the God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac (all named). 'That was a community that has passed' — each soul responsible for its own deeds.

2:135.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: knowledge (lowest priority, only from closing 'Hearer, the Knower' formula).

2:139.notes: Two qul imperatives. 'We are sincere to Him' — sincerity explicitly named. Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Patriarchs all named. Tawhid: 'He is our Lord and your Lord.' People of the Book addressed. Knowledge: 'Allah is not unaware of what you do.'

2:142.notes: Qiblah change passage — sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. 'Say, To Allah belong the East and West' — qul. Direct address to Prophet ('We have seen your face turned towards the heaven... turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque') — muhammad (substantive about him personally). 'Allah is Kind towards the people, Merciful' — mercy. Guidance. 'Allah is capable of everything' — power. Knowledge: 'Allah is not unaware.' People of the Book: they know it is truth. Believers addressed. 10 labels.

2:149.notes: Continued qiblah instruction — sacred-mosque. Direct address to Prophet (substantive about his turning, his role) — muhammad. 'We sent to you a messenger from among you' — prophethood-general. 'Remember Me and I will remember you' — remembrance explicitly commanded. 'Thank Me and do not be ungrateful' — gratitude (shukr explicitly named). Mercy implied by 'complete My blessings.' Guidance: 'that you may be guided.'

2:153.notes: Address to believers ('O you who believe'). Patience and prayer commanded — patience explicitly named ('Allah is with the steadfast'). Those killed in Allah's cause are alive — death-and-dying. Testing with fear, hunger, loss — trials context. 'Blessings and mercy from their Lord' — mercy.

2:158.notes: Angels label applied because v.161 explicitly says 'curse of Allah, and of the angels' — confirming angels tag.

2:163.notes: 11 labels. 'Your God is one God' — tawhid. 'Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim' — mercy. Creation of heavens/earth, night/day cycle (cosmic-bodies), rain, winds, ships, creatures (natural-signs). Those who take equals to Allah — shirk. Fire and severe punishment — hell/day-of-judgment. 'All power is Allah's' — power. Sovereignty implicit in 'al-Qadir.' Mankind addressed in v.164 context.

2:168.notes: Address 'O people' (ya ayyuha al-nas) — mankind. Food and dietary law: eat what is lawful and good; forbidden items listed (carrion, blood, pork, v.173). Iblis as open enemy — iblis. Disbelievers as parable. Believers addressed in v.172 ('O you who believe, eat of the good things').

2:174.notes: Those who conceal what Allah revealed, buy it for small price — swallow fire. Allah will not speak to them on Day of Resurrection. They exchanged guidance for error. The-quran: 'Allah has revealed the Book in truth.' People of the Book implied as those concealing scripture.

2:177.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. The famous birr verse: defines righteousness comprehensively. Believes in Allah, Last Day, angels, Scripture, prophets (prophethood-general + previous-scriptures + angels). Gives to orphans (orphan-care), needy, homeless, frees slaves (manumission-and-captives), prays (prayer), gives zakat (zakat-and-charity), fulfills covenant (covenant), patient (patience explicitly named — 'patiently persevere'). 'These are the sincere; these are the pious' — taqwa explicitly. Righteous-conduct: the whole verse defines it ('righteousness does not consist of...').

2:178.notes: Address to believers. Retaliation for murder — justice-and-witness + war context. 'A concession from your Lord, and a mercy' — mercy. Death: 'when death approaches one of you.' Testament for parents and relatives (inheritance/bequest). 'Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing' — knowledge.

2:183.notes: Address to believers ('O you who believe'). Fasting prescribed. Ramadan: month in which Quran was revealed (the-quran). 'Allah desires ease for you' — mercy/wisdom. 'Celebrate Allah... that you may be thankful' — gratitude commanded. 'I am near; I answer the call of the caller' (v.186) — nearness-and-response (explicit divine name/attribute). Guidance: 'that you may be rightly guided.' Knowledge: implicit. Taqwa: 'that you may become righteous' (the explicit purpose of fasting).

2:187.notes: Fasting rules and permitted intercourse with wives during nights of Ramadan — fasting + marriage-and-family. Ritual purity: conduct rules for retreat in mosques. Trade/corruption of wealth by bribery (v.188) — trade-and-debt. 'Allah thus clarifies His revelations... that they may attain piety' — taqwa.

2:189.notes: Crescents as timetables for people and Hajj — hajj. Fighting in Allah's cause (vv.190–195) — war-and-treaties. Sacred Mosque referenced (v.191). Mercy: 'But if they cease, then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.' Zakat-and-charity: 'spend in the cause of Allah' (v.195). Taqwa named multiple times. Qul: 'Say, they are timetables.'

2:196.notes: Hajj and Umrah completion rules; offerings; shaving heads; fasting as substitute if lacking means; Sacred Mosque referenced. Taqwa: 'Be conscious of Allah' (twice).

2:197.notes: Hajj months; conduct rules; 'remember Allah at the Sacred Landmark' — remembrance. 'Ask Allah for forgiveness' — could be du'a-forgiveness but it is commanded not uttered. 'Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful' — mercy. Uttered du'a in v.201: 'Our Lord, give us goodness in this world and the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire' — dua-protection. Reckoning: 'Allah is swift in reckoning' (v.202). Taqwa named.

2:203.notes: Designated days of remembrance — remembrance. Hypocritical man who corrupts earth and destroys harvest — corruption-on-earth. His pride leads to more sin — arrogance ('his pride leads him to more sin' explicit). 'Allah is kind towards the servants' — mercy. 'To Him you will be gathered' — day-of-judgment. Mankind as one community; prophets sent — prophethood-general. 'Allah guides whom He wills' — guidance. Address to believers (v.208 'O you who believe').

2:210.notes: Waiting for Allah and angels to come — day-of-judgment + angels. Ask Bani Israel about signs given — children-of-israel. Disbelievers mock believers (v.212 — 'they ridicule those who believe') — mockery. 'Allah provides to whomever He wills' — provision. Prophets sent as bearers of good news — prophethood-general. Guidance: 'Allah guides whom He wills.' 'Allah is Gracious towards the people' — mercy borderline but guidance is explicit.

2:214.notes: 'Do you expect to enter Paradise before...' — paradise. Adversity and hardship — patience context ('the steadfast' referenced). Those who believed migrated and fought hope for Allah's mercy. 'Say, Whatever charity you give...' — qul-statements + zakat-and-charity. Trust-in-god: 'Allah's victory is near' — believers placing trust in Allah.

2:216.notes: Fighting ordained — war-and-treaties. Sacred month fighting / Sacred Mosque expulsion — sacred-mosque. Those who believed, migrated, and fought — migration. Whoever dies a disbeliever — disbelief + hell. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' (v.218) — mercy. Knowledge: 'Allah knows and you do not know.' Qul: 'Say, Fighting during it is deplorable.' 10 labels.

2:219.notes: Intoxicants and gambling — explicit. Qul (twice): 'Say, There is gross sin in them' and 'Say, The surplus.' Charity: how much to spend. Orphans: care for them. Knowledge: 'Allah knows the dishonest from the honest.' Wisdom: 'Allah is Mighty and Wise.'

2:221.notes: Do not marry idolatresses/idolaters until they believe — marriage-and-family + polytheists + shirk. 'Allah calls to the Garden and to forgiveness' — paradise + mercy. Guidance: 'He makes clear His communications.'

2:222.notes: Menstruation rules — ritual-purity. Marital relations — marriage-and-family. 'Allah loves the repentant' — repentance. Qul: 'say, It is harmful.'

2:224.notes: Do not make Allah an excuse in oaths — oaths-and-vows. Four-month vow of abstinence from wives; divorce if resolved — divorce + marriage-and-family. Waiting period (iddah) rules (v.228) — divorce. 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' — wisdom. 'Allah is Listener and Knower' — knowledge. Justice: rights of women stated fairly.

2:229.notes: Divorce twice rule; honorable retention or release; khul' (wife's ransom); 'Allah's limits' repeated — divorce + marriage-and-family. Justice-and-witness: fair treatment obligations. 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' — wisdom + knowledge.

2:231.notes: When you divorce women — divorce. Do not retain to hurt them — marriage-and-family. 'Do not take Allah's revelations for a joke' — the-quran. 'Allah revealed to you the Scripture and Wisdom' — the-quran + wisdom. 'Allah is aware of everything' — knowledge.

2:233.notes: Nursing period rules (two years) — marriage-and-family. Father's obligation to provide — marriage-and-family. Heir's duty — inheritance borderline but it's about nursing period obligations. Justice: 'No soul shall be burdened beyond its capacity.' Knowledge: 'Allah is Seeing of what you do.'

2:234.notes: Widows' waiting period (four months and ten days) after husband's death — marriage-and-family + death-and-dying. Engagement rules. 'Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing' — mercy (closing). Knowledge: 'Allah knows what is in your souls.'

2:236.notes: Divorce before consummation — divorce + marriage-and-family. Compensation rules. 'Guard your prayers, and the middle prayer' (v.238) — prayer explicitly. 'Remember Allah' (v.239) — remembrance. Knowledge: 'Allah taught you what you did not know.'

2:240.notes: Will for wives for one year after husband's death — marriage-and-family + death-and-dying + inheritance (bequest). Divorced women to be provided for. 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' — wisdom. Knowledge: 'Allah is fully acquainted.'

2:243.notes: Those who fled homes — died and were revived (miracle: mass resurrection). 'Fight in the cause of Allah.' 'Who will offer Allah a generous loan' — zakat-and-charity. 'Allah receives and amplifies' — provision. Knowledge: 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing.' Death and resurrection explicitly depicted.

2:246.notes: Bani Israel after Moses ask for a king — saul (Talut). Saul chosen; 'Allah bestows His sovereignty upon whomever He wills' — sovereignty. Ark containing relics of Moses and Aaron's family carried by angels — angels + miracles. Moses and Aaron named (relics). Knowledge: 'Allah is Embracing and Knowing.'

2:249.notes: Saul, Goliath, David all named. River test of faith. 'Allah is with the steadfast' — patience named. Uttered du'a: 'Our Lord, pour down patience on us, and strengthen our foothold, and support us against the faithless people' (v.250) — dua-distress. David kills Goliath; given sovereignty and wisdom (sovereignty + wisdom). War context throughout.

2:252.notes: 'These are Allah's revelations which We recite to you... You are one of the messengers' — direct address to Muhammad — muhammad + the-quran. Jesus son of Mary given clear miracles, supported by Holy Spirit — jesus + miracles (prophethood-general covers this). 'Had Allah willed, they would not have fought' — divine-decree. Disbelief: some disbelieved after clear signs.

2:254.notes: Address to believers: spend before a Day of no trading, friendship, or intercession — day-of-judgment + intercession. Ayat al-Kursi (v.255): 'There is no god except He' — tawhid. 'To Him belongs everything in heavens and earth' — sovereignty. 'He knows what is before them' — knowledge. 'His Throne extends over heavens and earth' — sovereignty/power. 'He is the Most High, the Great' — sovereignty + power.

2:256.notes: 'No compulsion in religion' — guidance (right way distinct from wrong). Whoever rejects evil and believes — tawhid. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' — knowledge. 'Allah brings them out of darkness into light' — guidance. Disbelievers' lords (taghut) take them to darkness — disbelievers + hell.

2:258.notes: Abraham argues with the king (Nimrod) about his Lord — abraham. Abraham: 'My Lord gives life and causes death' — death-and-dying. The sun from the East argument — sovereignty (Allah controls cosmic order). 'Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people' — guidance withheld. Tawhid: Abraham's argument for the one God. Power: life-giving and death as divine power.

2:259.notes: Man dead for 100 years then revived — miracle + death-and-dying + resurrection. 'We will make you a wonder for mankind' — mankind. Bones arranged then clothed with flesh (resurrection imagery). 'I know that Allah has power over all things' — power (explicitly stated).

2:260.notes: Abraham asks 'show me how You give life to the dead' — dua-knowledge-wisdom (asking to see/understand). Four birds brought back to life — miracles + resurrection. 'Allah is Powerful and Wise' — power + wisdom.

2:261.notes: Parable of grain yielding 700-fold — zakat-and-charity + natural-signs (agricultural imagery as parable). 'Allah multiplies for whom He wills' — provision. 'Allah is Bounteous and Knowing' — provision + knowledge. Sincerity: 'do not nullify charitable deeds with reminders and hurtful words' (v.264 — 'like him who spends to be seen by people' — sincerity is the implicit positive counter; but 'spends to be seen' is absence of sincerity). Wisdom: v.269 'He gives wisdom to whomever He wills.' 'Allah is Rich and Clement' — provision/power.

2:267.notes: Spend of good things earned — zakat-and-charity. Satan promises poverty — iblis. 'Allah promises forgiveness and grace' — mercy. Wisdom: 'He gives wisdom to whomever He wills.' Knowledge: 'Allah is cognizant.' Oaths/vows: 'or a pledge you fulfill, Allah knows it.' Guidance: 'Their guidance is not your responsibility, but Allah guides whom He wills.'

2:274.notes: Spending by night and day (charity). Interest (riba) explicitly forbidden — interest. 'Allah condemns usury, and He blesses charities' — zakat-and-charity. Prayer and zakat in v.277 (believing + praying + zakat). 'Fear Allah and forgo what remains of usury' — interest. Day of Judgment: 'guard against a Day when you will be returned to Allah.' Knowledge: 'Allah is aware of everything.' Power: 'Allah is Able to do all things' (v.284). Justice: recording debt fairly. 10 labels.

2:282.notes: Longest verse — detailed debt-writing and witnessing rules — trade-and-debt + justice-and-witness. 'Fear Allah, and Allah teaches you' — knowledge. 'To Allah belongs everything in the heavens and the earth' — sovereignty. 'He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills' — mercy + power.

2:285.notes: The Messenger believed in what was revealed — muhammad (direct about him). Believers affirm faith in Allah, angels, scriptures, messengers — angels + previous-scriptures + prophethood-general + the-quran. 'Your forgiveness, our Lord' — uttered du'a — dua-forgiveness.

2:286.notes: Allah does not burden beyond capacity — mercy + justice. Multiple uttered du'as: 'Do not condemn us if we forget or make a mistake' (dua-forgiveness); 'do not burden us as You burdened those before us' (dua-distress); 'pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us' (dua-forgiveness); 'help us against the disbelieving people' (dua-protection). Disbelievers mentioned. Power: 'You are our Lord and Master.'

3:1.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: dua-protection (the du'a is primarily for guidance/steadfastness; dua-guidance covers it better); human-creation (forming in the womb is present in v6 but not the section's primary subject). The section opens with Alif-Lam-Mim (disjoined-letters), asserts tawhid (v2), introduces the Quran and Torah/Gospel (previous-scriptures, the-quran), asserts God's knowledge (v5), wisdom and power (v6), contains a uttered du'a for guidance and steadfastness (v8, Rabbana la tuzigh — dua-guidance) and a du'a about gathering on the Day (v9 — day-of-judgment), and warns disbelievers of punishment (v4).

3:10.notes: Section covers the fate of disbelievers (v10), references Pharaoh's people as a precedent (v11), contains 'Say' (qul) in v12, and describes the sign of the two armies at Badr (v13). War-and-treaties is appropriate for the battle-sign passage.

3:14.notes: V14 addresses humanity about worldly desires (mankind). V15 opens with 'Say' (qul-statements) and describes paradise for the muttaqin (paradise, taqwa). V16 contains an uttered supplication 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins' (dua-forgiveness). V17 names patience (patience) and charitable spending (zakat-and-charity). The section is addressed to believers implicitly (believers).

3:18.notes: V18 asserts tawhid with angels and those of knowledge as witnesses; names justice, wisdom. V19 states Islam is the religion with Allah and rebukes People of the Book who differed out of envy (people-of-the-book, disbelief). V20 contains two 'Say' commands (qul-statements) addressing People of the Book and the unlearned; guidance is the explicit subject ('they are guided').

3:21.notes: V21 warns those who kill prophets and advocates of justice — contextually children-of-israel / people-of-the-book. V22 mentions deeds coming to nothing. V23-24 address those given scripture who turn from Allah's book. V25 describes the Day of gathering and full reckoning. The section straddles people-of-the-book and children-of-israel as subjects.

3:26.notes: V26 opens with 'Say: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty' — a uttered glorification/praise of God's sovereignty (qul-statements, sovereignty, power, praise). The du'a-like address 'Allahumma' qualifies as an uttered supplication of praise/gratitude toward God's dominion (dua-gratitude is borderline; the address is laudatory rather than petitionary — keeping it at medium for that label). V27 mentions merging of night/day (cosmic-bodies) and provision (provision) and creation of life from death (creation). Confidence adjusted to high overall as labels are well-grounded.

3:28.notes: V28 instructs believers not to take disbelievers as allies. V29 contains 'Say' (qul) asserting God's knowledge of hearts (knowledge, power). V30 describes the Day when every soul finds its deeds (day-of-judgment, reckoning). V31 has 'Say: if you love Allah, follow me — Allah will forgive you' (qul-statements, mercy). V32 has another 'Say: obey Allah and the Messenger' (qul-statements). Taqwa is triggered by the piety theme in v28 (explicit 'taqah' — protecting yourselves).

3:33.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: miracles (the supernatural provision for Mary is present but not the section's focus; it is more a sign of provision), angels (they call to Zechariah in v39 — keep). V33 names Adam, Noah, family of Abraham, family of Imran. V35-36 introduce Mary's mother's vow (dua-family-offspring — uttered 'Rabbi inni nadhartu'), and names Mary. V37 names Zechariah and provision. V38 uttered du'a for offspring (dua-family-offspring confirmed). V39 names John (Yahya) and angels. V40-41 describe the miracle sign of Zechariah's muteness.

3:42.notes: V42-43 recount the angels addressing Mary — her chosenness, purification, and command to pray (prayer). V44 frames this as revealed knowledge from the unseen (the-quran — Quranic revelation context; prophethood-general). Knowledge is implicit in God's revelation of the unseen.

3:45.notes: V45 names Jesus (the Messiah, son of Mary) — annunciation by angels. V47 contains Mary's question and God's response 'Allah creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter He only says Be and it is' (divine-decree, power, human-creation). V48 mentions teaching him Torah and Gospel (previous-scriptures). V49 details Jesus's miracles to Children of Israel (miracles, children-of-israel). V50 references the Torah. V51 asserts tawhid ('Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him').

3:52.notes: V52 names Jesus and the Hawariyyun (disciples) who profess belief. V53 contains their uttered supplication 'Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed… count us among the witnesses' — this is a du'a of commitment/guidance (dua-guidance). V54 mentions the plotting against Jesus and God's counter-plan (plotting). Disbelief is explicit ('Jesus sensed disbelief on their part').

3:55.notes: V55 recounts Allah's direct address to Jesus — terminating his life, raising him, and the division between his followers and disbelievers until the Day. V56 describes punishment of disbelievers (hell). V57 describes reward of believers who do good (paradise). Justice is implicit in 'He will judge between you'; power in 'I am terminating your life and raising you.'

3:58.notes: V58 identifies this as the Wise Reminder (the-quran). V59 explicitly compares Jesus to Adam — both created by divine decree (human-creation, power). V60 asserts truth from the Lord. V61 instructs 'say' (qul-statements) about mutual imprecation (mubahala). V62 asserts tawhid ('there is no god but Allah', wisdom). V63 references the corrupt (knowledge of God). V64 has another 'Say: O People of the Book' (qul-statements, people-of-the-book) calling to tawhid and rejecting shirk.

3:65.notes: V65 addresses People of the Book disputing about Abraham; notes Torah and Gospel came after him (previous-scriptures). V66 rebukes arguing without knowledge (knowledge). V67 declares Abraham was a hanif Muslim, not a Jew or Christian, and not of the polytheists (tawhid). V68 states those most deserving of Abraham are those who followed him and the believers (believers).

3:69.notes: V69 describes a party of People of the Book seeking to lead believers astray (people-of-the-book, disbelief). V70-71 directly address People of the Book rejecting revelations and concealing truth (denial-of-revelation). V72 describes their scheme of feigned belief (plotting is borderline — not explicitly named, so not tagged). V73-74 contain 'Say' (qul-statements) asserting guidance belongs to Allah (guidance), and His mercy going to whom He wills (mercy, knowledge).

3:75.notes: V75 discusses trustworthiness of different individuals among People of the Book regarding financial deposits (trade-and-debt, people-of-the-book). V76 states whoever fulfills his covenant and is pious — Allah loves the pious (covenant, taqwa). V77 warns those who sell Allah's covenant and oaths for a small price — punishment on Day of Resurrection (day-of-judgment, covenant). V78 describes twisting scripture with tongues (previous-scriptures, disbelief, justice-and-witness).

3:79.notes: V79 states no prophet would tell people to worship him instead of Allah (prophethood-general, tawhid). V80 adds that a prophet would not command taking angels and prophets as lords (angels, shirk) — that would be disbelief (disbelief). The section addresses the proper role of prophethood and refutes exaggerated veneration.

3:81.notes: V81 describes the covenant Allah took from all prophets to believe in and support any subsequent messenger (prophethood-general, covenant, previous-scriptures). This is widely understood as the covenant to support Muhammad (muhammad). V83 asserts that everything in heavens and earth submits to Allah willingly or unwillingly (sovereignty, tawhid).

3:84.notes: 15 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: repentance (v89 opens the door but it is one verse among many); believers (implicit rather than direct address). V84 opens with 'Say' listing all prophets (qul-statements, abraham, ishmael, isaac, jacob, patriarchs, moses, jesus, prophethood-general, previous-scriptures, tawhid). V85 warns whoever seeks other than Islam (disbelief). V86-88 discuss those who disbelieve after faith — curse of Allah (hell is borderline — not described in detail). V89 opens the door for repentance (repentance, mercy). V90-91 further discuss apostasy. V92 mentions spending what you love for righteous conduct (zakat-and-charity is borderline).

3:93.notes: V93 addresses food permissibility for Children of Israel and what Jacob (Israel) forbade himself — food law (food-and-dietary, children-of-israel, previous-scriptures). Contains 'Say' (qul-statements). V95 says 'Say: Allah has spoken the truth; follow the religion of Abraham the Monotheist' (qul-statements, abraham, tawhid). V96-97 describe the first House at Bekka (Mecca) — pilgrimage is a duty (hajj-and-pilgrimage, sacred-mosque-and-qiblah). V98-99 have 'Say: O People of the Book' (people-of-the-book, qul-statements).

3:100.notes: V100 addresses believers warning against following People of the Book into disbelief (believers, people-of-the-book, disbelief). V101 asks how can you disbelieve while Allah's revelations are recited (the-quran, guidance). V102 calls believers to proper taqwa (taqwa). V103 commands holding to Allah's rope, remembering His blessings (remembrance), avoiding division. V104-105 call for a community advocating virtue, warning against division and punishment. V106-107 describe the Day of whitened/blackened faces (day-of-judgment). V107 mentions Allah's mercy (mercy). V108-109 assert Allah's sovereignty (sovereignty).

3:110.notes: V110 addresses believers as the best community — advocating good, forbidding evil (righteous-conduct explicitly named). References People of the Book (people-of-the-book) and notes most are sinners. V111 mentions if they fight you (war-and-treaties). V112 details their humiliation for killing prophets and rejecting signs (disbelief). V113-115 note a righteous subset among People of the Book who are among the righteous (righteous-conduct).

3:116.notes: V116 warns disbelievers that wealth and children will not avail — they are inhabitants of the Fire (hell, disbelievers, disbelief). V117 uses the parable of a frosty wind destroying a harvest (natural-signs as an illustrative parable).

3:118.notes: V118 addresses believers warning against taking outsiders (non-believers) as confidants who wish them harm (believers, disbelievers). V119 describes their hypocrisy — saying 'we believe' but biting fingers in rage (hypocrisy). Contains 'Say: die in your rage' (qul-statements). V119 also invokes God's knowledge of hearts (knowledge). V120 mentions if you persevere and maintain taqwa (patience — 'if you persevere', taqwa). The section contextually involves People of the Book (people-of-the-book) and their plotting (plotting).

3:121.notes: V121 directly addresses the Prophet in second person ('when you left your home') — muhammad. V122 mentions believers' near faltering and God as Protector — trust-in-god. V123 references Allah's victory at Badr (war-and-treaties). V124-125 mention angels reinforcing believers (angels, war-and-treaties). V126 states victory comes from Allah the Almighty, the Wise (power, wisdom, mercy). V127-129 discuss God's plan (knowledge, mercy, taqwa implied). God is Forgiving and Merciful at close (mercy).

3:130.notes: V130 directly addresses believers commanding avoidance of riba (interest, believers). V131 warns about the Fire prepared for disbelievers (hell). V133-134 call believers to race to forgiveness and paradise (paradise), describing those who spend in charity (zakat-and-charity), restrain anger, forgive (righteous-conduct). V135 describes those who remember Allah, seek forgiveness for sins (repentance, remembrance — remembrance is borderline as it is named in action). V136 promises forgiveness and paradise (paradise, mercy). Taqwa is explicitly named ('fear Allah so you may prosper', v130). Patience named in 'those who restrain anger' — borderline, but 'perseverance' appears in context.

3:137.notes: V137 references passed-away societies and their fate — punishment of past nations, travel the earth (previous-creations-destroyed). V138 calls this proclamation to humanity with guidance and advice for the righteous (guidance, taqwa). V139 addresses believers — 'you are the superior ones if you are believers' (believers). V140 discusses wounds and alternating days of conflict (war-and-treaties), God knowing the believers. V141-142 mention proving believers and distinguishing the steadfast (patience named explicitly in v142). V143 references facing death (death-and-dying borderline). Paradise referenced in v142.

3:144.notes: V144 explicitly names Muhammad — 'Muhammad is no more than a messenger' (muhammad, prophethood-general). The verse addresses the possibility of his death (death-and-dying). V145 states no soul can die except by Allah's leave at a predetermined time (divine-decree, death-and-dying). 'Allah will reward the appreciative' (gratitude — shukr named explicitly). V146 describes prophets with armies who did not waver — 'Allah loves the patient' (patience explicitly named). V147 contains an uttered du'a of warriors: 'Our Lord, forgive us our offences… help us against the disbelieving people' (dua-forgiveness, dua-distress — but classified as war context). V148 rewards in this world and next (paradise). War context throughout (war-and-treaties).

3:149.notes: V149 addresses believers warning against obeying disbelievers (believers, disbelievers). V151 mentions terror thrown into hearts of disbelievers because they associate partners with Allah (shirk, polytheists). V151 mentions the Fire as their lodging (hell). V152 describes the battle and God's promise fulfilled — believers pardoned for disobedience (war-and-treaties, mercy, divine-decree). V153-154 detail the battle aftermath including a 'Say' (qul-statements — but the explicit command is within a longer passage). V154 references Satan causing backsliding (iblis). V155 states Allah forgave them, is Forgiving and Prudent (mercy). Trust in Allah urged implicitly — 'Allah is your Master, He is the Best of Helpers' v150 (trust-in-god).

3:156.notes: V156 addresses believers — do not be like disbelievers who said of their brethren who marched or were killed 'had they stayed they would not have died' (believers, disbelievers, war-and-treaties, death-and-dying, migration). God gives life and causes death (divine-decree). V157-158 state that dying in the cause of Allah — forgiveness and mercy from Allah are better (mercy). 'To Allah you will be gathered up' (death-and-dying).

3:159.notes: V159 directly addresses the Prophet in second person — 'it is by grace from Allah that you were gentle with them' (muhammad, mercy). Commands: pardon them, seek forgiveness for them, consult them, and put trust in Allah (trust-in-god). 'Allah loves the trusting.' V160 states if Allah supports you none can overcome you — let believers put their trust in Allah (trust-in-god, power). War context (war-and-treaties) as this follows Uhud narrative.

3:161.notes: V161 states it is not for a prophet to act dishonestly — any dishonesty will be brought on the Day of Resurrection (prophethood-general, day-of-judgment, reckoning). Every soul will be paid fully and not wronged (justice). V162 contrasts one seeking Allah's approval with one incurring wrath whose refuge is Hell (hell, disbelievers). V163 states they have different ranks with Allah (reckoning).

3:164.notes: V164 states Allah blessed the believers by raising a messenger from among themselves (believers, muhammad, prophethood-general, the-quran). V165 contains 'Say: it is from your own selves' (qul-statements, power). V166 states what befell at the battle of the two armies was by Allah's permission (war-and-treaties, knowledge). V167 identifies the hypocrites who refused to fight (hypocrites).

3:168.notes: V168 describes hypocrites who stayed behind saying their brethren would not have been killed — contains 'Say' (qul-statements, hypocrites, war-and-treaties). V169 states those killed in Allah's cause are not dead but alive at their Lord, provided for (paradise, provision, death-and-dying). V170-171 describe their joy in Allah's grace and bounty (mercy). V172 praises those who responded to Allah and the Messenger despite injury (believers). V173 recounts their faith increasing when warned of enemy mobilization. V174-175 mention Satan frightening his partisans (iblis — borderline; mentioned as Satan frightening, keeping it medium).

3:176.notes: V176 addresses the Prophet not to be saddened by those rushing into disbelief — terrible torment awaits (disbelievers, disbelief, hell). V177 warns those exchanging faith for blasphemy (disbelief). V178 warns disbelievers not to think their respite is good (disbelief, day-of-judgment). V179 states Allah will not leave believers without distinguishing wicked from sincere — believes in messengers (prophethood-general, believers, knowledge, taqwa). V180 warns those who withhold what Allah gave them of His bounty — they will be encircled by their hoardings on Day of Resurrection (greed-and-miserliness, day-of-judgment).

3:181.notes: V181 records People of the Book saying 'Allah is poor and we are rich' — their killing of prophets (people-of-the-book, prophethood-general, punishment-of-past-nations). V182 asserts God's justice (justice). V183-184 contain 'Say' (qul-statements) about messengers coming with proofs and Psalms (previous-scriptures). V185 states every soul will taste death (death-and-dying) and be rewarded on the Day — whoever avoids the Fire and enters Paradise has won (day-of-judgment, paradise, hell). V186 addresses believers being tested — patience and taqwa named explicitly (patience, taqwa).

3:187.notes: V187 describes the covenant Allah took from those given Scripture to proclaim it — they disregarded it (people-of-the-book, previous-scriptures, covenant, disbelief). V188 warns those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done — punishment awaits them. This is a general warning applicable to the People of the Book in context.

3:189.notes: 15 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: natural-signs (the night/day alternation is more cosmic-bodies than natural-signs strictly; trim natural-signs), dua-guidance (the supplications in v193-194 are primarily for forgiveness and protection from Fire; trim dua-guidance). V189 asserts sovereignty and power. V190 invites reflection on creation of heavens/earth and alternation of night/day (creation-of-heavens-earth, cosmic-bodies). V191 depicts those who remember Allah and utter 'Subhanaka, protect us from the Fire' (remembrance, praise, dua-protection). V192-194 contain multiple uttered du'as: protection from Fire (dua-protection), forgiveness of sins (dua-forgiveness). V195 promises rewards for those who migrated and were expelled (migration, paradise, believers).

3:196.notes: V196-197 warn against being impressed by disbelievers' movements — their abode is Hell (disbelievers, hell). V198 contrasts with those who feared their Lord — for them are gardens (paradise, taqwa). Short section with clear, minimal labeling.

3:199.notes: V199 singles out among People of the Book those who believe in Allah and both revelations — humble before Allah, not selling His signs for a small price (people-of-the-book, believers, humility). Taqwa is implicit in their humble, God-conscious behavior; explicitly triggered by 'humble before Allah' (khashi'in). Knowledge is invoked through 'swift in reckoning'.

3:200.notes: V200 directly addresses believers: 'Be patient, and advocate patience, and be united, and revere Allah' — patience (sabr) named explicitly twice, taqwa named explicitly. Short closing verse with clean labeling.

4:1.notes: yā ayyuhā an-nās opens v.1 → mankind. taqwa named explicitly twice ('fear your Lord', 'revere Allah'). Creation from a single soul → human-creation. Orphan property rules vv.2-3 → orphan-care. Marriage (up to four wives) v.3 → marriage-and-family. 'Allah is Watchful over you' → knowledge (Al-Raqīb).

4:5.notes: Managing wealth of the immature and orphans until maturity; witnessing the handover. 'Allah suffices as a Reckoner' → knowledge.

4:7.notes: vv.7-9 establish inheritance shares for men and women; v.8 mentions orphans and the needy at distribution. v.10 warns that those who consume orphan wealth unjustly will 'roast in a Blaze' → hell. v.9 instructs taqwa, but in the context of fairness in inheritance rather than naming taqwa as the section's subject; justice is the explicit frame.

4:11.notes: Detailed inheritance shares vv.11-12. v.13 paradise for obedient; v.14 hell for disobedient. Closing 'Allah is Knowing and Judicious/Clement' → knowledge + wisdom. mercy also possible for 'Clement' (Halīm) but wisdom cluster is the primary pair here.

4:15.notes: vv.15-16 legislate punishment for lewdness, requiring four witnesses → justice-and-witness. v.16 'if they repent and reform' → repentance named explicitly. v.16 closing 'Redeemer, Full of Mercy' → mercy. v.17 'Knowing and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. v.18 death-bed repentance not accepted → death-and-dying; dying as disbelievers → disbelief implied but 'kuffār' appears explicitly.

4:19.notes: yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū → believers. Instructions on not inheriting women against their will, coercing them, and dealing with them kindly → marriage-and-family. Replacing one wife with another and the dowry issue → also touches divorce context.

4:22.notes: Prohibited degrees of marriage in detail (mothers, daughters, sisters, foster-mothers, wives' mothers, stepdaughters, sons' wives, two sisters simultaneously) → marriage-and-family. Closing v.23 'Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful' → mercy. v.24 closing 'All-Knowing, Most Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

4:25.notes: Marrying believing maids when unable to afford free women → marriage-and-family + manumission-and-captives (captive/slave-girl marriage context). v.26 'guide you in the ways of those before you, and to redeem you' → guidance + repentance (tawba). 'Knowing and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. v.25 closing 'Most Forgiving, Most Merciful' → mercy.

4:29.notes: yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū → believers. v.29 prohibits consuming wealth illicitly, permits trade by mutual consent → trade-and-debt. v.29 'do not kill yourselves' → anger-and-violence borderline but not the section's named subject; skipping per rule 5. v.30 hell for transgressors. v.32 'do not covet what Allah has given to some of you' → envy explicitly named ('do not covet/tatamannaw'). v.33 inheritance-adjacent (beneficiaries of what parents leave) → inheritance. v.29 'Allah is Merciful' → mercy. v.32 'Allah has knowledge of everything' / v.33 'Allah is Witness' → knowledge.

4:34.notes: Men as maintainers/protectors of women; rules for dealing with marital discord; arbitration → marriage-and-family. v.34 closing 'Allah is Sublime, Great' (ʿAlī, Kabīr) → sovereignty/power cluster; tagging knowledge for v.35 closing 'Knowledgeable, Expert' (ʿAlīm, Khabīr). wisdom covers the wise ordering implicit in 'Knowledgeable, Expert'. Power/sovereignty could also be added for 'Sublime, Great' but section is primarily domestic law.

4:36.notes: v.36 'Worship Allah, and ascribe no partners to Him' → tawhid + shirk. Broad righteous-conduct list (parents, relatives, orphans, poor, neighbors, travelers, servants) → orphan-care prominent; zakat-and-charity for spending on poor. v.36 'Allah does not love the arrogant showoff' → arrogance named. v.37 stinginess, concealing Allah's bounty → greed-and-miserliness. v.38 spending to be seen by people → hypocrisy borderline but not named; skipping. v.41-42 Day of Resurrection witness scene → day-of-judgment. v.40 'Allah does not commit an atom's weight of injustice' → justice. v.39 'Allah knows them very well' → knowledge. v.37/42 disbelievers addressed → disbelievers. 11 labels — within ceiling.

4:43.notes: yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū → believers. Prohibition on approaching prayer while drunk → prayer + intoxicants-and-gambling. Rules on ritual purity (ghusl, tayammum) → ritual-purity. Closing 'Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving' → mercy.

4:44.notes: vv.44-45 address those given a share of the Book who buy error → people-of-the-book. v.46 Jews specifically distorting words → children-of-israel (they are among the Jews/Yahud). v.46 'Allah has cursed them for their disbelief' → disbelief. v.45 'Allah knows your enemies best' → knowledge. Adding children-of-israel for v.46 'Among the Jews'.

4:47.notes: v.47 address to those given the Book → people-of-the-book; reference to Sabbath-breakers → children-of-israel. v.48 'Allah does not forgive shirk' → shirk. v.51 believing in superstition/evil powers → shirk/disbelief. v.54 envy of people for Allah's grace; family of Abraham given Book and wisdom → abraham (named). v.55 hell. v.56 hell described vividly → hell. v.56 closing 'Most Powerful, Most Wise' → power + wisdom. Abraham named in v.54 → adding abraham. envy named in v.54 → envy. 12 labels at ceiling.

4:57.notes: Believers who do good deeds enter Gardens with purified spouses → paradise. Short single-theme section.

4:58.notes: v.58 command to give back trusts and judge with justice → justice-and-witness. v.59 obey Allah, Messenger, and those in authority → believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū v.59). vv.60-63 those who claim belief but seek Satanic arbitration, and the hypocrites who shun the Messenger → hypocrites. v.58 'Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing' → knowledge. v.63 Allah knows what is in their hearts → knowledge. covenant implicit in 'trusts' (amanāt) but justice-and-witness covers the explicit frame.

4:64.notes: v.64 messengers sent to be obeyed; had they come seeking forgiveness → prophethood-general + repentance. v.64 'Allah Relenting and Merciful' → mercy. v.68 'guided them on a straight path' → guidance. v.69 those who obey are with prophets, truthful, martyrs → prophethood-general reinforced. v.70 'Allah suffices as Knower' → knowledge.

4:71.notes: yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū v.71 → believers. Military mobilization instructions → war-and-treaties. vv.72-73 hypocrite-like laggards (though not named munafiqun, behavior described). v.74 fighting in the cause of Allah. v.75 uttered supplication: 'Our Lord, deliver us from this town... appoint for us a Protector and Victor' (Rabbanā...) → dua-distress (calling on God in oppression). v.76 those who disbelieve fight for evil/Taghut; 'the strategy of the Devil is weak' → iblis + disbelievers.

4:77.notes: v.77 those told to restrain hands, perform prayers, give zakat → prayer + zakat-and-charity. Fighting ordained → war-and-treaties. Uttered words: 'Our Lord, why did You ordain fighting for us?' — this is a du'a-like utterance but it is a complaint/question rather than a supplication; not tagging dua-*. v.77 contains 'Qul' (Say) → qul-statements. v.78 'Wherever you may be, death will catch up with you' → death-and-dying. v.78 all is from Allah → divine-decree. v.77 'better for the righteous (man ittaqā)' → taqwa named.

4:82.notes: v.82 'Do they not ponder the Quran? Had it been from other than Allah...' → the-quran. v.83 'Were it not for Allah's blessing and mercy upon you' → mercy.

4:84.notes: v.84 fight in the cause of Allah; rouse believers → war-and-treaties + believers. v.85 whoever intercedes for a good/evil cause shares in it → intercession. v.86 return greetings kindly → righteous-conduct borderline; not naming the concept explicitly enough; skipping. v.87 'Allah—there is no god except He' → tawhid. v.87 'He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment. v.87 'who speaks more truly than Allah' → knowledge. v.84 'Allah is Stronger in Might' → power.

4:88.notes: vv.88-91 deal with the hypocrites and those who are neither fully aligned → hypocrites. Instructions on seizing/executing those who turn away unless they emigrate → migration (hijrah) + war-and-treaties. v.90 those with whom you have a treaty → covenant. disbelievers as opposing party → disbelievers.

4:92.notes: Rules on unintentional killing of a believer → war-and-treaties. Expiation: freeing a believing slave → manumission-and-captives. Fasting two consecutive months → fasting. 'By way of repentance to Allah' → repentance named. v.93 deliberate killing → hell. v.94 yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū → believers. v.92 closing 'All-Knowing, Most Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

4:95.notes: Distinction between inactive believers and those who strive with their possessions and persons → war-and-treaties. Both promised goodness but strivers favored → believers. v.96 closing 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy.

4:97.notes: Angels taking the souls of those who wronged themselves → angels + death-and-dying. Question about not emigrating → migration. Those who fail to emigrate without excuse: hell → hell. v.99 'Allah may well pardon them' → mercy. v.100 emigrating to Allah and Messenger → migration reinforced.

4:101.notes: Shortening prayers in travel when fearing disbelievers → prayer + war-and-treaties. 'The disbelievers are your manifest enemies' → disbelievers. Prayer in danger (salat al-khawf) detailed in v.102 → prayer reinforced. v.103 'remember Allah... the prayer is obligatory at specific times' → prayer. v.104 'Allah is Knowledgeable and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

4:105.notes: v.105 'We revealed to you the Scripture... so that you judge between people' → the-quran + justice-and-witness. v.106 'ask Allah for forgiveness; Allah is Forgiver and Merciful' → mercy. v.107 not arguing for those who deceive → plotting. v.108 they plot by night → plotting reinforced. v.109 who will argue with Allah on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment borderline (mentioned in passing); not tagging. v.111 'Allah is Aware and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. v.112 blaming an innocent person → slander-and-backbiting.

4:113.notes: v.113 direct address to the Prophet ('towards you', 'revealed to you the Scripture') → muhammad. 'Allah has revealed to you the Scripture and wisdom' → the-quran. 'Were it not for Allah's grace and mercy' → mercy. v.114 advocating charity (sadaqah) or reconciliation → zakat-and-charity. v.115 hell for those who breach with the Messenger → hell borderline; the section's focus is counsel to the Prophet and ethics of private counsel; not tagging hell to keep count manageable. 'Allah is Aware and Wise' implied throughout → knowledge + wisdom.

4:116.notes: v.116 Allah will not forgive shirk → shirk. v.117 invoking females and rebellious devil → iblis. vv.118-120 Iblis's plot to mislead → iblis reinforced. v.121 hell for followers of Iblis. v.122 paradise for believers. v.123 'it is not according to wishes of People of the Scripture' → people-of-the-book. v.125 'follows the faith of Abraham the Monotheist; Allah has chosen Abraham for a friend' → abraham. v.116/122 disbelief implicit → disbelief. v.116 'Allah will forgive what is less than shirk to whom He wills' → mercy. v.126 'To Allah belongs what is in the heavens and earth' → sovereignty. 9 labels.

4:127.notes: v.127 contains 'Qul' → qul-statements. Ruling about women, orphan women's rights, helpless children, treating orphans fairly → orphan-care + marriage-and-family + justice-and-witness. 'Allah knows it' → knowledge.

4:128.notes: Wife fearing maltreatment/desertion; reconciliation; polygamy fairness → marriage-and-family. v.128 'if you do what is good, and practice piety (tattaqū)' → taqwa named. v.129 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. v.130 'Allah is Bounteous and Wise' → knowledge (closing attribute).

4:131.notes: v.131 'We instructed those who were given the Book before you... to be conscious of Allah (ittaqū)' → people-of-the-book + taqwa named. v.133 'O people (ayyuhā an-nās)' → mankind. 'If He wills, He can do away with you... and bring others' → power. 'To Allah belongs everything in the heavens and earth' (3×) → sovereignty. v.134 'Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing' → knowledge.

4:135.notes: v.135 yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū; 'stand firmly for justice, as witnesses to Allah' → believers + justice-and-witness. v.136 yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū; believe in the Book revealed to messenger and previous Books, in Allah, His angels, His Books → the-quran + angels + previous-scriptures. v.136 'Whoever rejects... has strayed far in error' → disbelief. v.137 those who believe then disbelieve repeatedly → disbelief reinforced. v.138 'inform the hypocrites of painful punishment' → hypocrisy. 'Allah is Aware of what you do' → knowledge. Adding previous-scriptures for v.136.

4:139.notes: vv.139-141 hypocrites taking disbelievers as allies → hypocrites + disbelievers. v.139 'All glory belongs to Allah' → sovereignty borderline; not tagging (passing mention). v.140 when revelations are rejected or ridiculed → mockery + the-quran. v.140 'Allah will gather hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell' → hell. v.141 'Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment. believers addressed v.144 (next section) so not tagging here, but v.141 implicitly contrasts with believers → keeping believers for the explicit address.

4:142.notes: v.142 hypocrites try to deceive Allah; stand lazily for prayer → hypocrites + prayer. v.143 wavering between believers and disbelievers → hypocrites reinforced. v.144 yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū; do not befriend disbelievers → believers + disbelievers. v.145 hypocrites in lowest level of Fire → hell. v.146 those who repent and hold fast to Allah, sincerely dedicating their religion → repentance + sincerity (ikhlas named: 'dedicate their religion to Allah alone'). v.147 'what would Allah accomplish by your punishment if you have given thanks and believed' → mercy. v.148-149 Allah does not like public utterance of bad language except for the wronged; pardon → mercy reinforced. v.147 'Allah is Appreciative and Cognizant' → knowledge. 9 labels.

4:150.notes: vv.150-151 those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, separating between Allah and messengers → disbelievers + prophethood-general. v.151 hell for the unbelievers. v.152 those who believe in all messengers rewarded; 'Allah is Forgiver and Merciful' → mercy. Context implies people-of-the-book (those who accept some prophets but not others) → people-of-the-book.

4:153.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: punishment-of-past-nations (subsumed by the narrative of Israel's crimes and consequences, already covered by children-of-israel), slander-and-backbiting (single verse), interest (single verse v.161).

4:163.notes: 20 labels — significantly over ceiling. All named prophets must be tagged per rule 3. Trim candidates (if forced): knowledge, wisdom, power are closing-attribute tags on v.165 ('Powerful and Wise') and v.166 (knowledge). previous-scriptures (Psalms given to David, v.163) is highly specific and valuable. Retaining all — this section is a prophet-list by design and the overflow is justified.

4:170.notes: v.170 yā ayyuhā an-nās → mankind. v.171 yā ahl al-kitāb → people-of-the-book. Jesus son of Mary addressed → jesus + mary. 'Do not say Three; Allah is only one God' → tawhid + shirk. 'Glory be to Him that He should have a son' → tawhid/praise; praise not uttered as a formula here but rather refuted. v.171 'To Him belongs everything in heavens and earth' → sovereignty. v.170 'Allah is Omniscient and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. v.172 Jesus does not disdain to be a servant; favored angels → angels. v.172-173 those who are too arrogant → arrogance named ('yastakbir'). 11 labels.

4:174.notes: v.174 yā ayyuhā an-nās; 'a proof has come from your Lord; a clear light' → mankind + the-quran. v.175 'He will admit them into mercy and grace... guide them to a straight path' → mercy + guidance.

4:176.notes: v.176 contains 'Qul' → qul-statements. Detailed inheritance rules for a person with no parents or children (kalāla) → inheritance. 'Allah is Aware of everything' → knowledge.

112:3.notes: Added to match theme_breaks.json [1,3,4]; pilot Markdown grouped 112:1-3, but machine assignments need the 112:3 start key.

91:11.notes: salih is inferred from the she-camel episode; the translation says messenger but does not name him.

105:1.notes: quraysh is contextually implied by the attack on the House in Mecca; the translation names People of the Elephant, not Quraysh.

111:4.notes: slander-and-backbiting reflects the traditional reading of the firewood carrier as carrying harm/slander; review if sticking only to surface translation.

114:4.notes: iblis is used for Satanic whispering even though the translation says the sneaky whisperer rather than naming Iblis.

62:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with glorification (tasbih) of Allah with four names — Sovereign, Holy, Almighty, Wise — triggering praise, sovereignty, wisdom, power. Verses 2–4 describe the sending of the unlettered messenger (Muhammad ﷺ), reciting revelations, teaching Scripture and wisdom — prophethood-general, the-quran, muhammad (substantively about him and his role, not just a 'Say:' command). Verse 5 compares those entrusted with the Torah to a donkey carrying books — people-of-the-book, previous-scriptures, denial-of-revelation, disbelief. 'Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people' → guidance (divine attribute, negated form still invokes it). 12 labels — at the ceiling; all independently justified.

62:6.notes: Two 'Say:' (qul) commands in verses 6 and 8 → qul-statements. Addressed explicitly to 'those who follow Judaism' → people-of-the-book and children-of-israel. The challenge to wish for death if they are sincere → death-and-dying. 'Allah knows well the wrongdoers' → knowledge. 'You will be returned … and He will inform you of what you used to do' → reckoning. Their failure to act on their claim and their hypocrisy toward death → disbelief. 'To the exclusion of the rest of mankind' references mankind as a contrasted group → mankind.

62:9.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe' (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū) → believers. Commands hastening to prayer on Jumu'ah (Friday) → prayer. 'Remembrance of Allah' explicitly named → remembrance. 'Drop all business' and 'seek Allah's bounty' → trade-and-debt and provision.

62:11.notes: Contains 'Say:' (qul) command → qul-statements. The incident described involves the Prophet ﷺ being left standing during a sermon — this is substantively about him personally (his domestic/community context), warranting muhammad alongside qul-statements. 'What is with Allah is better than entertainment and business' → trade-and-debt. 'Allah is the Best of providers' → provision (divine attribute closing formula).

63:1.notes: Direct address to Muhammad ('when they come to you'); Allah bears witness He knows — tags knowledge. Verse 3 explicitly names disbelief ('they believed, then disbelieved'). Oaths used as cover aligns with hypocrisy as the section's explicit subject.

63:5.notes: 'Turning away arrogantly' (mustakbirun) is the explicit Arabic trigger for arrogance. 'Allah does not guide the sinful people' names guidance (negated). 'To Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth' invokes sovereignty and provision. 'Power belongs to Allah, and His Messenger, and the believers' tags believers and sovereignty.

63:9.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe' — tags believers. Explicit command not to let wealth distract from dhikr — tags remembrance. 'Spend from what We have provided' is explicit charity instruction — tags zakat-and-charity. Death approaching is the concrete subject of verse 10 — tags death-and-dying. The uttered words 'My Lord, if only You would delay me' are a near-du'a but are presented as the hypothetical speech of a dying person regretting inaction, not an uttered supplication in the du'a sense; therefore no dua-* label applied. divine-decree is tagged because the deferred death scenario is framed around God's appointed term (ajal).

63:11.notes: Single verse. 'Allah will not delay a soul when its time has come' — explicit divine decree over the appointed term (ajal) and death. 'Allah is Informed of what you do' — closing attribute invoking knowledge.

73:1.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('O you Enwrapped one') with instructions on night vigil, Quran recitation, and remembrance. 'There is no god but He, so take Him as a Trustee' triggers both tawhid and trust-in-god. Sovereignty implicit in 'Lord of the East and the West.' No uttered du'a so no dua-* label. No qul so no qul-statements.

73:10.notes: Direct address to the Prophet instructing patience and withdrawal from deniers. 'Endure patiently' explicitly names patience as the commanded virtue — rule-5 trigger met. Shackles, Fierce Fire, choking food describe hell. The trembling earth and mountains on a Day described = day-of-judgment imagery. 'Those who deny the truth, those of luxury' = disbelievers. Punishment-of-past-nations not explicitly named here — removed on reflection; the deniers described are contemporary not historical. Hell and day-of-judgment are directly described.

73:15.notes: Messenger sent as witness — prophethood-general. Pharaoh explicitly named and his defiance/seizure recounted — pharaoh + punishment-of-past-nations. The Day turning children gray = day-of-judgment. Heaven shattering = day-of-judgment (signs-of-the-hour borderline, but the section frames it as the Day itself rather than a preceding sign). 'Whoever wills, let him take a path to his Lord' — guidance as explicit theme. Disbelief named explicitly ('if you persist in unbelief'). Direct address context connects to muhammad.

73:20.notes: Allah knows the Prophet and companions' night vigil — knowledge. He has pardoned them — mercy and repentance (tawbah accepted). Recite what is possible of the Quran — the-quran. Observe prayers — prayer. Give zakat and lend generously — zakat-and-charity. Fighting in Allah's cause mentioned — war-and-treaties. 'Allah designed/measures the night and day' — divine-decree. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' closing formula — mercy confirmed. Believers addressed collectively alongside the Prophet.

81:1.notes: Verses 1–14 enumerate the cosmic upheavals of the Last Hour and culminate in souls knowing their deeds. 'Sun rolled up', 'stars dimmed' → cosmic-bodies; 'mountains set in motion', 'beasts gathered', 'oceans set ablaze' → natural-signs and signs-of-the-hour; 'Fire set ablaze' → hell; 'Paradise brought near' → paradise; 'records made public' → reckoning; 'girl buried alive' is a justice motif supporting the justice label; 'each soul will know what it has readied' → day-of-judgment.

81:15.notes: Oath by the galaxies and the night/dawn → cosmic-bodies. 'Noble messenger endowed with power, eminent with the Lord of the Throne, obeyed and honest' refers to Gabriel delivering revelation → angels. 'Your friend is not possessed' and 'he saw him on the luminous horizon' is direct second-person address defending the Prophet and his vision of Gabriel → muhammad. 'Not the word of an accursed devil' → denial-of-revelation. 'Does not withhold knowledge of the Unseen' → knowledge. The passage defends the authenticity of the Qur'anic revelation → the-quran and prophethood-general.

81:27.notes: 'A Reminder to all mankind' → the-quran and mankind. 'To whoever wills to go straight' names guidance (istaqāma — going straight) as the explicit subject of the Qur'an's purpose → guidance. Rule-5 trigger met: guidance is the stated function of the reminder here.

81:29.notes: 'You cannot will unless Allah wills — the Lord of the Worlds' is a direct assertion of divine decree and sovereignty over human will. 'Lord of the Worlds' frames His absolute sovereignty → sovereignty. The verse implicitly reinforces tawhid by subordinating all created will to the single divine will → tawhid.

85:1.notes: The oath by the sky with constellations triggers cosmic-bodies. The Promised Day is the Day of Judgment. The People of the Trench narrative involves persecution of believers by disbelievers. 'The Almighty, the Praiseworthy' and 'sovereignty of the heavens and the earth' trigger power and sovereignty. The persecution/burning is anger-and-violence.

85:10.notes: Verse 10 contrasts those who do not repent (hell) with verse 11's believers doing righteous deeds (paradise). Repentance is explicitly named ('then do not repent'). Righteous deeds are explicitly named ('do righteous deeds').

85:12.notes: God's severe onslaught → power. 'Forgiving, the Loving' → mercy. 'Possessor of the Glorious Throne' + 'Doer of whatever He wills' → sovereignty and divine-decree. Pharaoh named → pharaoh. Thamud named → thamud. 'Those who disbelieve are in denial' → disbelievers + denial-of-revelation. 'It is a Glorious Quran' → the-quran. Pharaoh and Thamud as cautionary examples → punishment-of-past-nations.

85:22.notes: The Preserved Tablet (lawh mahfuz) directly references the Quran's preservation (the-quran) and God's written decree (divine-decree). Short single-verse section.

90:1.notes: sacred-mosque-and-qiblah is inferred from 'this land' as the sacred city; review if using only surface translation.

92:21.notes: paradise is inferred from the promised satisfaction of the devout in context.

95:1.notes: moses is inferred from Mount Sinai; sacred-mosque-and-qiblah from the safe land as Mecca.

100:1.notes: war-and-treaties reflects the raiding cavalry scene; natural-signs tags the animal imagery.

98:1.notes: The 'Clear Evidence' (al-bayyinah) is identified in verse 2 as a messenger reciting purified scriptures — tagging prophethood-general and the-quran. Denial-of-revelation is implicit in their prior state of not being apart (i.e. persisting in disbelief until the evidence came); verse 4 explicitly notes they splintered after the evidence arrived, suggesting willful rejection.

98:5.notes: Verse 5 states they were commanded to worship Allah with sincere devotion (mukhlisina — sincerity explicitly named), to establish prayer, and to give zakat. Tawhid is asserted via 'devoting their faith to Him alone' (hunafa'). People-of-the-book is carried forward from the immediate context. prophethood-general applies as this describes the universal command sent via all messengers.
