98:6.notes: Verse 6 names disbelievers from People of the Book and Polytheists condemned to Hell eternally — hell label applies. Verse 7 contrasts with believers who do righteous deeds and are 'best of creatures' — believers and righteous-conduct (explicitly named as doing righteous deeds) apply. paradise is strongly implied for the best of creatures though verse 8 makes it explicit; tagging it here is borderline — keeping it off and leaving it to 98:8. reckoning is implied in the comparative judgment ('worst' vs 'best' of creatures).

98:8.notes: Verse 8 describes the reward of the believers: Gardens of Eternity, rivers, eternal abiding, Allah's pleasure. paradise is the primary label. taqwa is explicitly triggered: 'That is for whoever fears his Lord' (man khashiya rabbahu). Divine pleasure (Allah is pleased with them) — justice label applies as this is the fair recompense. believers carried forward as the subject.

86:1.notes: An oath by the sky and the piercing star. cosmic-bodies covers the star and sky as celestial signs. No named figures, no divine attributes invoked, no du'a.

86:4.notes: The protector/guardian over every soul is understood per Ibn Kathir as a recording angel. human-creation is triggered by the explicit description of man being created from gushing liquid issuing from backbone and breastbones. knowledge is tagged because God's awareness of every soul's deeds is implied by the guardian-over-it framing, though not named by a closing formula — medium confidence on knowledge.

86:8.notes: Verse 8 asserts God's ability to return him (resurrection) → power + resurrection. Verse 9 names the Day when secrets are disclosed → day-of-judgment + reckoning. Verse 10 — no strength, no supporter on that Day — reinforces the reckoning theme.

86:11.notes: Oath by the sky that returns (rain cycle → natural-signs; sky as cosmic element → cosmic-bodies) and the earth that cracks open (natural-signs). Verses 13–14 declare it a Decisive Word, no joke — explicit statement that the Qur'an/revelation is serious truth → the-quran.

86:15.notes: Explicit reference to 'they plot and scheme' and God counter-plotting → plotting. The schemers are the disbelievers/opponents of the Prophet → disbelievers.

86:17.notes: Direct command addressed to the Prophet to give the disbelievers respite → disbelievers. This is an imperative command (famahhil) directed at the Prophet, functioning similarly to a qul-statement pattern; however, the imperative here is not literally 'qul' — medium confidence on qul-statements. The command is directed at Muhammad implicitly but is not a direct 'O Prophet' address, so muhammad label is not applied per §5.2.

87:1.notes: sabbih = 'Glorify/Praise' — uttered command to praise, so `praise` applies per §5.6b. Creation and regulation → `creation`. 'Measures and guides' → `guidance` (God as source of guidance, named explicitly). 'Produces the pasture / turns it to debris' → `natural-signs`.

87:6.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('We will make you read… We will ease you') → `muhammad`. Subject is revelation/recitation of the Qur'an → `the-quran`. 'He knows what is declared and what is hidden' → `knowledge`. 'The Easy Way' → `guidance`. 'Except what Allah wills' → `divine-decree`. 'Remind' (dhikr imperative) → `remembrance`.

87:10.notes: 'The reverent will remember' — man yakhsha (those who fear/revere God) → `taqwa` explicitly named as the section's subject. 'The wretched will avoid it… enter the Gigantic Fire… neither die nor live' → `hell` and `disbelievers`.

87:14.notes: 'Purifies himself, mentions the name of his Lord, and prays' → `prayer` (salah explicitly named) and `remembrance` (dhikr of Lord's name). 'The Hereafter is better and more lasting' → `day-of-judgment`. 'This is in the former scriptures' → `previous-scriptures`. 'Successful is he who purifies himself' — purification/righteous conduct named explicitly as the section's subject → `righteous-conduct`.

87:19.notes: Single verse naming the Scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Both figures named → `abraham`, `moses`. Subject is prior revealed books → `previous-scriptures`.

88:1.notes: Section opens with 'the overwhelming' (al-ghashiyah), a name for the Day of Judgment, then describes the faces of the damned roasting in fire and given thorns to eat — squarely eschatological, focused on hell.

88:8.notes: Contrasting section describing joyful faces in a lofty Garden with flowing springs, raised beds, and cushions — classic paradise imagery. 'Satisfied with their endeavor' implies the believers' righteous deeds; tagging believers generously per §5.2.

88:17.notes: Four rhetorical questions directing attention to camels (natural-signs), the sky (creation-of-heavens-earth), mountains (natural-signs / creation-of-heavens-earth), and the spread earth (creation-of-heavens-earth). The address is implicitly to those who do not reflect — disbelievers per context. 'Creation' tagged because the passage invokes God as Creator via the passive 'how they are created / raised / installed / spread.'

88:21.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('You are only a reminder', 'You have no control over them') — tags both `muhammad` (direct address) and `prophethood-general` (the role of a reminder/messenger). 'Whoever turns away and disbelieves' tags `disbelief`. 'Remind' (dhakkir) explicitly names the act of remembrance/dhikr as the Prophet's function, triggering `remembrance`.

88:24.notes: 'The greatest punishment' for those who disbelieve → connects back to disbelievers from 88:23. 'To Us is their return / upon Us rests their reckoning' invokes divine justice and the reckoning on the Day of Judgment.

89:1.notes: An oath by natural phenomena: the daybreak, ten nights, the even and odd, and the receding night. No named figures, no divine attributes claimed, no du'a. 'The even and the odd' is ambiguous in tafsir (some read as ritual; most read as cosmological/temporal) — tagged under natural-signs as the dominant reading.

89:5.notes: 'Spread much corruption therein' triggers corruption-on-earth explicitly (v12: 'fa-aktharū fīhā al-fasād'). 'Your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment' → punishment-of-past-nations and justice. 'Your Lord is on the lookout' (v14) asserts God's all-seeing vigilance → knowledge (God's complete awareness).

89:15.notes: 'Al-insān' (man/mankind) is the explicit subject throughout. 'He restricts his livelihood' invokes provision/rizq and divine-decree. Orphan-care is explicitly named (v17: 'you do not honor the orphan'). Greed and hoarding of wealth are the explicit subjects of vv19–20 → greed-and-miserliness. The inheritance verse (v19) is a moral critique of how inheritance is devoured, not a legal ruling — greed-and-miserliness captures it; no separate inheritance label warranted.

89:21.notes: The earth being leveled and crushed → resurrection/day-of-judgment. Angels arriving row after row named explicitly → angels. Hell brought forward → hell. Man's regret and remembrance → reckoning. 'None will punish as He punishes' is a justice assertion about God's unmatched judgment.

89:27.notes: 'O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, pleased and accepted, enter among My servants' — the address to the satisfied soul implies the believing soul; tagged believers generously. 'Return to your Lord' is a nearness-and-response motif — God accepting and welcoming the soul back. Paradise is implied but not yet named (it comes in v30); however 'enter among My servants' is the gateway address to it — paradise tag held for 89:30 which names it explicitly. Confidence remains high.

89:30.notes: Single verse: 'Enter My Paradise' — direct, unambiguous statement of Jannah. Minimal section; paradise is the sole relevant label.

96:1.notes: The command 'Read' (Iqra) is the first revelation addressed directly to the Prophet — justifies `muhammad`. 'Created man from a clot' → `human-creation`. 'Your Lord who created' → `creation`. 'Taught by the pen / taught man what he never knew' → `knowledge`. The revelatory context of the first command also warrants `prophethood-general`.

96:6.notes: 'Man oversteps all bounds when he considers himself exempt' → `arrogance` (explicit transgression/self-sufficiency). 'To your Lord is the return' → `day-of-judgment`. The address is about mankind in general → `mankind`. The attitude of considering oneself exempt from God is a form of `disbelief`.

96:9.notes: 'A servant when he prays' — explicit mention of prayer → `prayer`. 'Disbelieved and turned away' → `disbelief`. 'Does he not know that Allah sees' → `knowledge` (God's knowledge invoked). 'Advocates righteousness / upon guidance' — taqwa is explicitly named ('advocates righteousness' translates أَمَرَ بِٱلتَّقْوَىٰ) → `taqwa`. Verses 8-9 describe the scales of justice (mizan) — reckoning and justice labels both apply. 'We were never absent' asserts God's knowledge.

7:10.notes: Verse 10 addresses mankind regarding livelihood/provision on earth. Verses 11-19 cover the full Adam-Iblis narrative: creation of Adam, angels commanded to bow, Iblis refuses citing arrogance ('I am better'), is expelled, requests respite until resurrection, vows to waylay mankind, and God threatens to fill Hell with Iblis and his followers. Adam and wife are told to dwell in the Garden. Arrogance is explicit ('it is not for you to act arrogantly'). Hell mentioned explicitly in v.18.

7:20.notes: Satan whispers to Adam and his wife, they eat from the tree. In v.23 they utter 'Rabbana zalamna anfusana wa-in lam taghfir lana wa-tarhamna' — a clear uttered supplication asking for forgiveness and mercy → dua-forgiveness. Mercy invoked explicitly. Their repentance/turning to God is the explicit subject of v.23. Divine decree implied in v.24-25 ('in it you will live and die and be brought out').

7:26.notes: Addressed to 'O Children of Adam' (Bani Adam — mankind as descendants of Adam). Clothing as provision from God. 'The clothing of piety (taqwa) — that is best' — taqwa is explicitly named as the subject. Warning about Satan as he drove their parents from the Garden. Adam label applies because Adam's parents narrative is referenced and Bani Adam is addressed.

7:28.notes: V.28: 'Qul: Allah does not command indecencies' — qul-statement. V.29: 'Qul: My Lord commands justice' — second qul-statement. Both trigger qul-statements label. V.29 explicitly names justice ('al-qist'). V.29 also commands calling upon God with sincere devotion ('mukhlisina lahu al-din') — sincerity is explicitly named. V.30: guidance/misguidance as subject. Shirk implied in 'adopted the devils for patrons'. V.32: two more 'Qul' occurrences.

7:33.notes: V.33 opens with 'Qul' — qul-statement. Explicitly forbids shirk ('associate with Allah anything for which He revealed no sanction'). V.34 states every nation has an appointed time (ajal) that cannot be advanced or delayed — divine decree. Short section (2 verses).

7:35.notes: Addressed to 'O Children of Adam' (Bani Adam). V.35: messengers from among you come with revelations — prophethood-general. Those who practice piety (taqwa) — explicit. V.36: those who reject and are arrogant → hell — arrogance and hell explicit. V.37: denial of revelation explicit. V.38: Hell filled with crowds of jinn and humans → jinn label. V.38 contains a uttered du'a within Hell ('Rabbana ha'ula' adalloona') — borderline; this is speech in hell not a proper supplication seeking God's response, so dua-* not applied. Paradise implied for the pious in v.35 but not explicitly described — not tagging paradise.

7:40.notes: V.40-41: arrogant rejectors forbidden from paradise, assigned hell — arrogance, denial-of-revelation, hell, paradise all explicit. V.42: believers who do righteous works inherit the Garden — paradise, believers. V.43: inhabitants of Garden say 'al-hamdu lillahi alladhi hadana' — uttered praise formula → praise label. V.43 also references guidance ('had Allah not guided us'). V.44-45: exchange between paradise and hell dwellers; curse upon wrongdoers who hindered from Allah's path.

7:46.notes: The Al-A'raf (the Elevations/Heights) passage. V.46: men on the Elevations between paradise and hell. V.47: they utter 'Rabbana la taj'alna ma'a al-qawm al-zalimin' — uttered supplication seeking protection from being placed with wrongdoers → dua-protection. V.48: arrogance of the condemned referenced ('your arrogance'). V.49: mercy of Allah mentioned ('Allah will not touch with mercy'). Day of Judgment setting throughout.

7:50.notes: Inmates of Fire call on inhabitants of Garden for water/provision — refused as God has forbidden it to disbelievers. V.51: those who took religion lightly, deceived by worldly life, God ignores them as they ignored the Day. Denial of revelations explicit in v.51. Day of Judgment setting.

7:52.notes: V.52: Scripture detailed with knowledge, guidance and mercy — the-quran, mercy, knowledge. V.53: awaiting the fulfillment (ta'wil) of the Scripture; on that Day those who ignored it ask 'have we any intercessors?' — intercession explicitly raised. Prophethood-general: messengers of the Lord referenced. Disbelievers: those who ruined their souls.

7:54.notes: V.54: Creation of heavens and earth in six days, the Throne, night/day cycle, sun, moon, stars subservient by His command — creation-of-heavens-earth, cosmic-bodies, sovereignty, power, creation. 'Tabaraka Allahu' — uttered praise formula → praise. V.55: call upon Lord humbly (prayer instruction, not uttered du'a). V.56: 'do not corrupt on earth' — corruption-on-earth explicitly named. 'Allah's mercy is close' — mercy. V.57-58: wind, clouds, rain, dead land revived, fruits — natural-signs. Analogy to resurrection of the dead. 9 labels — within ceiling.

7:59.notes: Noah sent to his people; calls them to worship Allah alone (tawhid) and warns of punishment of a tremendous Day. People call him in error. Noah declares himself a messenger (prophethood-general). They reject him → Noah and believers saved in the Ark; rejectors drowned. Punishment of past nations, denial of revelation.

7:65.notes: Hud sent to 'Ad; calls to worship Allah alone (tawhid). People mock him as foolish and a liar. He declares himself a messenger. V.69 references the people of Noah as predecessors — noah label applies per rule 3. V.71: condemnation and wrath upon them. V.72: God saves Hud and believers by mercy ('bi-rahmatin minna') — mercy. 'Ad destroyed — punishment of past nations, denial of revelation.

7:73.notes: Salih sent to Thamud; calls to worship Allah alone (tawhid). The she-camel as a miracle sign from God (miracles). V.74 references 'Ad as predecessors. V.75-76: arrogant elite vs. believers — arrogance explicit ('alladhina istakbaru'). V.77: they hamstring the she-camel, defy God. V.78: quake destroys them — punishment of past nations. V.74 warns against corruption on earth ('la ta'thaw fi al-ard mufsidina') — corruption-on-earth explicitly named.

7:80.notes: Lot rebukes his people for lewdness unprecedented among any people. People respond by threatening to expel Lot and his followers. God saves Lot and his family (except his wife). Rain of destruction poured on the sinners. Punishment of past nations, denial of revelation.

7:85.notes: Shuayb sent to Madyan; calls to worship Allah alone (tawhid). Explicitly commands full measure and weight, not cheating people — trade-and-debt, justice. 'Do not corrupt the land' — corruption-on-earth explicitly named. V.86: warns against blocking path of God. V.87: 'be patient until Allah judges' — patience is the explicit instruction ('fasibru').

7:88.notes: Arrogant elite threaten to expel Shuayb and believers unless they return to their religion — arrogance explicit. V.89: Shuayb's response: 'In Allah we place our trust' — trust-in-god explicit ('tawakkalna'). 'Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge' — knowledge. 'Rabbana iftah baynana wa-bayna qawmina bi-l-haqq' — uttered supplication in distress → dua-distress. V.90-91: disbelievers' warning, quake strikes them — punishment of past nations. V.92-93: those who rejected Shuayb are the losers.

7:94.notes: General principle: every prophet sent to a town was accompanied by affliction of its people (misery and adversity) so they humble themselves. Then prosperity, then sudden seizure. V.96: had towns believed and been righteous, blessings of heaven and earth opened — guidance implicit. Divine decree in the appointed pattern. Punishment of past nations as the overarching theme.

7:97.notes: V.97-99: rhetorical questions about towns feeling secure from God's might — punishment-of-past-nations theme. V.99: 'Do they feel safe from Allah's plan?' V.100: guidance for those who inherit the land — those who came after could have been struck for their sins; God seals their hearts. V.101: these towns — their messengers came with clear signs but they would not believe — denial-of-revelation. V.102: most untrue to their covenants — covenant label applies.

7:103.notes: Moses sent with God's miracles to Pharaoh and his establishment. Moses declares himself messenger from Lord of the Worlds; asks Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel. Pharaoh demands a miracle — Moses throws his staff (serpent) and shows his white hand — miracles. Pharaoh's notables accuse Moses of being a 'skilled magician' — sorcery label (accusation of sihr). V.103 notes the evildoers/corrupters — corruption-on-earth.

7:113.notes: Magicians contest with Moses; throw their staffs. Moses's staff swallows their sorcery — miracles. 'The truth came to pass and what they were producing came to nothing.' Magicians fall prostrate, profess belief in the Lord of Moses and Aaron — aaron label (v.122). Pharaoh threatens crucifixion. Magicians say 'Rabbana afrigh 'alayna sabran wa-tawaffana muslimin' — uttered supplication in distress → dua-distress. 'Pour out patience upon us' — patience is explicitly requested in the supplication.

7:127.notes: Pharaoh's chiefs ask him to deal with Moses and his people — Pharaoh threatens to kill their sons and spare their women. Moses tells his people: 'Seek help in Allah and be patient (wasibru)' — patience is the explicit command. 'The earth belongs to Allah, He gives it in inheritance to whomever He wills' — sovereignty. 'The future belongs to the righteous.' V.129: Moses's reassurance that God may destroy the enemy — trust-in-god implicit in context but patience and sovereignty are the explicit triggers.

7:130.notes: God afflicts Pharaoh's people with barren years and shortage of crops — natural-signs. V.131: they blame Moses for bad omens. V.132: they refuse to believe no matter what sign is shown — denial of revelation / disbelievers. V.133: the five plagues (flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood) — miracles (explicit miraculous signs). V.133: 'they were too arrogant' — arrogance explicit. V.134-135: they ask Moses to pray to lift the plague, promise to believe and release Children of Israel — covenant. V.135: they break their promise — covenant broken. V.136-137: God drowns them; Children of Israel inherit the land — punishment of past nations.

7:138.notes: Children of Israel cross the sea and see idol-worshippers. They ask Moses to make them a god like theirs — shirk. Moses rebukes them: 'You are truly an ignorant people.' V.139: those idolaters are in perdition. V.140: 'Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah?' — tawhid assertion. V.141: reminder of rescue from Pharaoh's people, who killed their sons — Pharaoh label applies.

7:142.notes: Moses's appointment of 40 nights; tells Aaron to lead the people. Moses asks to see God — refused; mountain crumbles, Moses falls unconscious. Upon recovery: 'Subhanaka tubtu ilayk' — uttered praise/glorification formula → praise. 'I repent to You' — repentance is the explicit act. 'You spoke to him' — nearness-and-response (God speaking directly to Moses). V.144: 'I have chosen you over all people for My messages and My Words' — prophethood-general. The Tablets are previous-scriptures (Torah content).

7:145.notes: V.145: God inscribes the Tablets (Torah) — previous-scriptures. V.146: God will turn away from His revelations those who act arrogantly ('yatakabbaruna') — arrogance explicitly named. They will not believe in any sign — denial-of-revelation. They follow the path of error rather than rectitude — guidance as subject. V.147: those who deny revelations and the Hereafter — denial-of-revelation.

7:148.notes: People of Moses adopt the golden calf in his absence — shirk. V.149: they regret and realize they erred; say 'Unless our Lord extends His mercy to us and forgives us' — uttered plea for mercy/forgiveness → dua-forgiveness. V.150: Moses returns angry, confronts Aaron — aaron label. V.151: Moses utters 'Rabbi ighfir li wa-li akhi wa-adkhilna fi rahmatika' — uttered supplication for forgiveness and mercy → dua-forgiveness confirmed. 'You are the Most Merciful of the merciful' — mercy. V.152: those who idolized the calf incur wrath. V.153: those who repent and believe — repentance explicit.

7:154.notes: V.154: Moses takes up the Tablets — previous-scriptures; 'guidance and mercy for those in awe of their Lord' — guidance, mercy. V.155: Moses selects 70 men; tremor shakes them; Moses utters 'Rabbi law shi'ta ahlaktahum min qablu wa-iyyay... anta waliyyuna faghfir lana wa-irhamna wa-anta khayr al-ghafirin' — uttered supplication for forgiveness and mercy → dua-forgiveness. 'This is but Your test, with it You misguide whomever You will and guide whomever You will' — divine decree. 'Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge' — knowledge.

7:156.notes: 13 labels — over 12 ceiling. V.156: continuation of Moses's supplication: 'wa-uktub lana fi hadhihi al-dunya hasanatan wa-fi al-akhira inna hudna ilayk' — uttered supplication asking for goodness → this is a du'a for worldly and next-life good; closest to dua-gratitude or general petition — applying dua-family-offspring is not right; this is a general supplication. Reconsidering: the du'a asks for 'goodness (hasana) in this world and the next' — most fitting is dua-distress or general — none of the 7 dua labels perfectly fits a request for 'goodness'. Dropping specific dua label; noting in suggestedNewLabels. God's response: 'My mercy encompasses all things' — mercy. 'Those who act righteously and pay zakat' — taqwa, zakat-and-charity explicit. V.157: the Unlettered Prophet found in Torah and Gospel — muhammad (substantive description of the Prophet), people-of-the-book (Torah/Gospel holders), previous-scriptures, prophethood-general. V.158: 'Qul ya ayyuha al-nas inni rasul Allah ilaykum jami'an' — qul-statement; 'O people' — mankind; 'He to Whom belongs the kingdom of heavens and earth' — sovereignty; 'There is no god but He' — tawhid. Trim candidates: dua label (removed), previous-scriptures (borderline — kept because Torah/Gospel explicitly named).

7:159.notes: V.159: among Moses's people a community that guides by truth and does justice. V.160: 12 tribes divided; Moses strikes rock — 12 springs gush (miracle); manna and quails sent down — provision, miracles. V.161: told to settle the town, enter gate in humility, sins forgiven — previous-scriptures context (covenant of entry). V.162: wicked substitute words given to them; plague sent from sky — punishment of past nations, covenant broken.

7:163.notes: The Sabbath-breaking town narrative — addressed to people of the Book context per tafsir. V.163: town by the sea violating the Sabbath (covenant). V.164: group among them advises; answered 'as excuse to your Lord.' V.165: God saves those who prohibited evil; punishes wrongdoers — punishment of past nations. V.166: those who rebelled turned into apes. V.167: God announces He will send those who inflict suffering upon them until Day of Resurrection; 'Your Lord is swift in retribution, yet He is Forgiving and Merciful' — mercy (closing formula).

7:168.notes: V.168: Children of Israel scattered into communities; tested with good and bad. V.169: succeeding generations inherited Scripture ('al-kitab'), took worldly goods, said 'We will be forgiven' — covenant of the Scripture. 'Did they not make a covenant to uphold the Scripture?' — covenant, previous-scriptures. V.170: those who adhere to the Scripture and establish prayer — prayer explicit. 'The Home of the Hereafter is better for the cautious (al-muttaqin)' — taqwa explicit. V.171: mountain suspended over them as covenant-taking moment.

7:172.notes: The primordial covenant (mithaq): God summoned all descendants of Adam and made them testify 'Am I not your Lord?' — tawhid. V.172: 'so you cannot say on the Day of Resurrection we were unaware' — day-of-judgment. V.173: 'nor can you say our ancestors practiced idolatry (shirk) before' — shirk. V.174: God elaborates revelations so they may return. Divine decree in the primordial witnessing.

7:175.notes: V.175-176: story of one given God's signs who detached himself; Satan went after him — iblis. 'His metaphor is that of a dog' — denial-of-revelation. V.177: evil metaphor of those who reject signs. V.178: 'Whoever Allah guides is the guided one; whoever He sends astray are the losers' — guidance (explicit subject), divine-decree. V.179: 'We have destined for Hell multitudes of jinn and humans' — hell, jinn explicitly named.

7:180.notes: V.180: 'To Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call Him by them' — tawhid (names assert oneness). V.181: a community that guides by truth. V.182-183: God will gradually lead rejectors astray; 'My plan is firm.' V.184: 'He is but a plain warner' — prophethood-general. V.185: 'Have they not observed the government of the heavens and the earth and all things Allah created?' — creation-of-heavens-earth, knowledge. V.186: 'Whoever Allah misguides has no guide' — guidance as explicit subject.

7:187.notes: V.187: 'They ask you about the Hour, when will it come?' — signs-of-the-hour. Two 'Qul' commands → qul-statements. 'Knowledge of it rests with my Lord / with Allah' — knowledge. This section is directly about a question put to the Prophet and his reply — substantively about him and his role — muhammad label applies (direct address context: 'they ask you'). 'I am only a warner and herald' — prophethood-general. V.188: another 'Qul' — 'I have no control over benefit or harm except as Allah wills' — prophethood-general.

7:189.notes: V.189: God created you from a single person, made from it its mate — human-creation, marriage-and-family (spouse/companionship). When the wife grows heavy they pray: 'if You give us a good child, we will be among the thankful' — uttered supplication for offspring → dua-family-offspring. V.190: when given the good child, they attribute partners to God — shirk. V.191: rhetorical refutation of shirk — tawhid by implication. 'Mankind' is the universal subject of this passage about human creation from a single soul.

7:193.notes: V.193-198: refutation of idols — they cannot follow guidance, they are servants like you, they cannot hear or help — shirk. V.195: 'Qul: call upon your partners' — qul-statement. V.196: 'My Master is Allah who sent down the Book.' V.199: 'Be tolerant, and command decency' — righteous-conduct is borderline; 'command decency' (amr bil-'urf) is explicit instruction but not named as a concept label. V.200: 'when a suggestion from Satan assails you, take refuge with Allah' — iblis (Satan named). 'He is Hearing and Knowing' — knowledge (closing formula). V.201: 'those who are righteous (ittaqaw)' when Satan strikes them — taqwa explicit. V.201: 'they remind themselves (tadhakkaruu)' — remembrance explicit.

7:203.notes: V.203: disbelievers demand a miracle; 'Qul: I only follow what is inspired to me' — qul-statement, prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation (they deny without miracle). 'These are insights from your Lord, and guidance, and mercy' — the-quran (scripture described), guidance, mercy. V.204: 'When the Quran is recited, listen to it' — the-quran. V.205: 'Remember your Lord within yourself (udhkur rabbaka)' — remembrance explicitly commanded.

7:206.notes: V.206: those in the presence of God (angels) are not too proud to worship Him; 'they recite His praises (yusabbihunahu)' — praise (subhan formula). 'They bow down' — worship. Short single-verse section.

8:1.notes: The 'Say' (qul) command in v1 triggers qul-statements. Taqwa is explicitly named ('be mindful of Allah'). Provision appears in v4 ('generous provision'). Mercy is implicit in 'forgiveness' in v4 — tagging mercy for the forgiveness + provision pairing. Trust-in-god is present in v2 ('upon their Lord they rely'). Prayer is mentioned in v3 explicitly but the section is about the broader identity of believers, with prayer as one marker; tagging prayer as well.

8:5.notes: Verses 5–14 cover the Battle of Badr context. Angels sent as reinforcement (v9). 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' (v10) → power + wisdom. 'Hearing and Knowing' (v17 belongs to next section but v10 closes with 'Mighty and Wise') → wisdom and power. Hell mentioned in v14 ('the suffering of the Fire'). Divine decree implicit in God's plan overriding human preference (v7). Trust-in-god: 'victory comes only from Allah' (v10). Knowledge: 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' (v17 is next section, but within this range v10 asserts 'Allah is Mighty and Wise'). Note: v17 is in section 8:15, not here.

8:15.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe' (v15) → believers. War conduct instructions throughout. Hell in v16 ('his abode is Hell'). 'It was not you who killed them, but Allah' (v17) → divine-decree and power. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' (v17) → knowledge. Section includes 'you' (second person singular) references to the Prophet in v17 ('it was not you who launched when you launched') which is substantively about his role at Badr → muhammad.

8:20.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe' (v20, v24) → believers. Taqwa: v25 'be mindful' (ittaqu) explicitly names the concept. 'Allah stands between a man and his heart' → nearness-and-response and knowledge. 'Allah is severe in retribution' → power/justice. Disbelievers addressed as those who do not reason (v22). Tagging knowledge for 'Allah knows what is in hearts' and power for 'severe in retribution'.

8:26.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe' (v27, v29) → believers. Gratitude explicitly named in v26 ('so that you may be thankful' — shukr trigger). Provision in v26 ('provided you with good things'). Taqwa explicitly in v29 ('if you remain conscious of Allah'). Mercy via forgiveness in v29 ('will forgive you'). Trust-in-god implicit in v29 context. War/trust context from v26 (sheltered from enemies).

8:30.notes: Plotting explicitly named in v30 ('they plotted, and Allah plotted') → plotting. Direct address to Muhammad implied throughout; v30 'plotted against you' is about him personally → muhammad. Qul in v38 → qul-statements. Sacred Mosque in v34 ('turning others away from the Sacred Mosque') → sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. Hell in v36, v37 → hell. 'Allah is Powerful, Severe in punishment' is in next section (8:49), but v39 references God's sight → knowledge. Denial of revelation in v31 ('these are nothing but myths of the ancients') → denial-of-revelation. 11 labels — within ceiling.

8:41.notes: War spoils legislation (khums) in v41 → war-and-treaties. Orphans explicitly mentioned as recipients in v41 → orphan-care. Distribution to poor and wayfarers → zakat-and-charity. 'Allah is Capable of everything' → power. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' (v42) → knowledge. 'Allah was to carry out a predetermined matter' (v42) → divine-decree.

8:43.notes: God showing the enemy as few in the Prophet's dream → divine management of battle. 'He knows what the hearts contain' (v43) → knowledge. 'Allah may conclude a predetermined matter' (v44) → divine-decree. Power implicit in God's direct manipulation of perceptions. War-and-treaties context throughout.

8:45.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe' (v45) → believers. Remembrance explicitly named: 'remember Allah much' (v45) → remembrance. Patience explicitly named: 'be steadfast; Allah is with the steadfast' (v46) → patience. Iblis named in v48 → iblis. Arrogance in v47: 'boastfully, showing off' — the Arabic is batarar (arrogance/insolence), explicit enough → arrogance. 'Allah is severe in punishment' (v48) → power. War conduct instructions throughout.

8:49.notes: Hypocrites explicitly named in v49 → hypocrites. Trust-in-god: 'whoever puts his trust in Allah' (v49) → trust-in-god. Angels taking souls of disbelievers (v50) → angels. 'Allah is not unjust to the servants' (v51) → justice. Pharaoh's people named in v52, v54 → pharaoh. Punishment-of-past-nations: people of Pharaoh destroyed (v54) → punishment-of-past-nations. 'Allah is Powerful, Severe in punishment' (v52) → power. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' (v53) → knowledge. 10 labels — within ceiling.

8:55.notes: Disbelievers as 'worst of creatures' (v55) → disbelievers. Covenant breaking in v56 → covenant. War instructions in v57–60 → war-and-treaties. Trust-in-god: 'put your trust in Allah' (v61) → trust-in-god. Direct address 'O prophet' in v64, v65 → muhammad. 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' (v63) → power + wisdom. 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' (v61) → knowledge. Patience explicitly named: 'Allah is with the steadfast' (v66) → patience. 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' throughout. 10 labels — within ceiling.

8:67.notes: Section addresses rules about prisoners of war → manumission-and-captives + war-and-treaties. 'It is not for a prophet' → prophethood-general. 'Allah is Strong and Wise' (v67) → power + wisdom. Divine decree in v68 ('a predetermined decree from Allah') → divine-decree. Taqwa explicitly named in v69 ('remain conscious of Allah') → taqwa. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' (v69) → mercy. Direct address context is to the Prophet/believers about war conduct → muhammad (substantively about prophetic conduct in war).

8:70.notes: Direct address 'O prophet' in v70 → muhammad. 'Say to those you hold prisoners' → qul-statements. Captives/prisoners of war addressed → manumission-and-captives. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' (v70) → mercy. 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' (v71) → knowledge + wisdom.

8:72.notes: Migration (hijrah) explicitly the subject throughout v72 → migration. War-and-treaties: mutual aid obligations and treaty exceptions in v72 → war-and-treaties. Covenant: 'a people with whom you have a treaty' (v72) → covenant. 'Allah is Seeing of what you do' → knowledge. Believers and disbelievers as collective groups discussed.

8:73.notes: Corruption on earth explicitly named: 'turmoil in the land, and much corruption' (v73) → corruption-on-earth. Migration and struggle in v74 → migration. War-and-treaties context. 'They will have forgiveness, and a bountiful provision' (v74) → mercy + provision. Believers and disbelievers as opposing groups.

8:75.notes: Migration explicitly referenced → migration. 'Family members are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah' (v75) — this refers to inheritance precedence over the bonds of emigration → inheritance. 'Allah is Cognizant of everything' → knowledge. War-and-treaties context of struggle alongside believers.

9:1.notes: Treaty dissolution with polytheists announced at Greater Pilgrimage. Taqwa triggered explicitly: 'Allah loves the righteous (muttaqin)' v.4.

9:5.notes: Fight/spare clauses for polytheists; asylum-seeker escorted to safety; sacred mosque treaty exception. Closing 'Forgiving, Merciful' → mercy.

9:8.notes: Exposes polytheists' bad faith with believers; vv.11 conditions brotherhood on prayer+zakat; v.9 'traded away Allah's revelations' → the-quran.

9:13.notes: Direct address to believers urging battle; v.13 references plot to exile the Messenger → muhammad. Closing 'Knowledgeable and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

9:17.notes: Who may attend mosques; comparison of pilgrimage service vs. faith+striving; reward for those who believe, emigrate, strive. 'Their Lord announces mercy' → mercy. Paradise promised to believers. Taqwa implicit in 'fear none but Allah' v.18 — explicit naming: 'fearing' (khashiya) Allah; borderline but tagging generously.

9:23.notes: O believers addressed directly. 'Say' (qul) in v.24 → qul-statements. Family loyalty vs. faith loyalty → marriage-and-family. Battle of Hunayn recalled; divine aid sent down. Closing 'Forgiving, Merciful' → mercy already implicit but main attribute here is divine aid; repentance in v.27.

9:28.notes: O believers: ban polytheists from Sacred Mosque; fight People of the Book until jizyah. 'Allah will enrich you from His grace' → provision. Closing 'Aware and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

9:30.notes: Jews' claim about Ezra, Christians' claim about the Messiah son of Mary (Jesus named via 'the Messiah') → jesus. Both claims refuted as shirk → tawhid + shirk. 'Glory be to Him' (Subḥānahu) v.31 → praise. Messenger sent with guidance → guidance + prophethood-general.

9:34.notes: O believers warned about rabbis/priests consuming wealth illicitly and hoarding gold/silver; hellfire punishment described. Corruption on earth (blocking Allah's path, consuming people's wealth) explicit.

9:36.notes: Twelve sacred months established since creation of heavens and earth → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'In the decree of Allah' (fi kitab Allah) → divine-decree. Taqwa: 'Allah is with the righteous (muttaqin)'. Postponement (nasī') is disbelief → disbelief.

9:38.notes: Section covers vv.38–42. Cave incident reference → muhammad. 'Allah has power over all things' v.39 → power. Closing 'Mighty and Wise' v.40 → wisdom. Hypocrites referenced implicitly in v.42 (those who swear falsely); tagging hypocrisy.

9:43.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Section vv.43–55: direct address to Prophet ('May Allah pardon you') → muhammad. Extensive hypocrite exposure. Multiple qul commands vv.51–53 → qul-statements. v.51 divine decree → divine-decree. v.51 trust in Allah → trust-in-god. v.44 'Allah is fully aware of the righteous' → knowledge + taqwa. v.48 plotting → plotting. Trim candidates: divine-decree (v.51 brief mention), taqwa (secondary).

9:56.notes: Hypocrites swear falsely, flee, criticize charity distribution; v.60 defines zakat recipients → zakat-and-charity. Closing 'All-Knowing, Most Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

9:61.notes: Hypocrites insult the Prophet → muhammad + slander-and-backbiting. 'Say' (qul) commands vv.61,65 → qul-statements. Prophet described as 'mercy for believers' → mercy. Hell for those who oppose → hell.

9:64.notes: 14 labels — overflow. Trim candidates: prophethood-general (not the explicit subject), punishment-of-past-nations (redundant given specific nation labels).

9:71.notes: Believing men and women described as allies, commanding good, forbidding evil, performing prayer, giving zakat → prayer + zakat-and-charity + righteous-conduct. Allah will have mercy → mercy. Paradise promised → paradise. Closing 'Noble and Wise' → wisdom.

9:73.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' → muhammad. Strive against disbelievers and hypocrites. Hell their abode. v.74 plotting referenced. Repentance offered. 'Allah and His Messenger have enriched them from His grace' → mercy (provision of grace).

9:75.notes: Hypocrites made a covenant with Allah then broke it → covenant. Stinginess → greed-and-miserliness. v.78 'Allah knows their secrets' → knowledge. v.79 mockery of charitable believers → mockery. v.80 seventy-times forgiveness withheld.

9:81.notes: Those who stayed behind the Messenger → muhammad. 'Say: Fire of Hell is much hotter' → qul-statements. Hell mentioned explicitly. Disbelief of those who stayed behind.

9:84.notes: Direct instruction to the Prophet not to pray over dead hypocrites → muhammad. v.86 references revealed surah → the-quran. v.89 paradise for believers → paradise. Death of hypocrites in disbelief → death-and-dying.

9:90.notes: Desert-Arabs excuses for exemption; genuine excused parties defined (weak, sick, poor). 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. The righteous (muhsinun) not blamed → righteous-conduct.

9:94.notes: 'Say: do not offer excuses' → qul-statements. 'Returned to the Knower of the Invisible' → knowledge + reckoning. Hell for hypocrites v.95. 'Allah does not accept the wicked' v.96.

9:97.notes: Desert-Arabs categorized: most steeped in disbelief/hypocrisy; among them sincere believers. v.97 'limits Allah revealed' → the-quran. v.97 closing 'Knowing and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. v.98 'Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge. v.99 'Allah will admit them into His mercy' → mercy.

9:100.notes: The Pioneers: Migrants (Muhajirin) and Supporters (Ansar) → migration. Allah pleased with them; Paradise prepared → paradise. 'Allah is pleased with them' conveys mercy/approval → mercy.

9:101.notes: Hypocrites around Medina identified. v.102 those who confess sins and mix good/bad deeds; repentance offered → repentance. v.103 take contributions/zakat → zakat-and-charity. v.103 'Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge. v.104 Allah accepts repentance → mercy. v.105 'Say: Work' → qul-statements. 'Returned to the Knower' → reckoning. v.106 closing 'Aware and Wise' → wisdom.

9:107.notes: Mosque of harm (Masjid al-Dirar) built to divide believers and aid enemies of Allah and His Messenger → muhammad (substantively about the Prophet's role). Taqwa: mosque founded on taqwa v.108. Closing 'Knowing and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. Plotting: built to harm and as outpost for enemies → plotting.

9:111.notes: Allah's bargain with believers: lives/property for paradise → paradise + covenant. Torah, Gospel, Quran mentioned → previous-scriptures + the-quran. v.112 'those who praise' (al-hamidun) → praise. v.112 those who kneel/bow → prayer. v.112 those who repent → repentance. v.112 advocate righteousness/forbid evil → righteous-conduct.

9:113.notes: Prophet and believers forbidden from seeking forgiveness for polytheists → muhammad. Abraham's case explained → abraham. v.115 Allah would not lead guided people astray → guidance. v.115 'Allah has knowledge of all things' → knowledge. v.116 'To Allah belongs the dominion of heavens and earth; He gives life and causes death' → sovereignty + death-and-dying.

9:117.notes: Allah redeemed the Prophet, Emigrants, Supporters → muhammad + migration. Repentance of the three left behind → repentance. 'Kind and Compassionate' / 'Redeemer, Merciful' → mercy.

9:119.notes: 'O you who believe! Be conscious of Allah (ittaqu Allah)' → believers + taqwa. 'Be with the sincere (sadiqin)' → sincerity. v.120 inhabitants of Medina not to stay behind the Messenger → muhammad. 'Allah does not waste the reward of the righteous' → righteous-conduct. v.121 expenditures recorded → zakat-and-charity (spending in God's cause). 'Allah is fully aware' → knowledge.

9:122.notes: Not all believers should march out; some remain to gain understanding of religion → the-quran (learning the revelation). v.123 'O you who believe! Fight disbelievers near you' → believers + disbelievers + war-and-treaties. 'Allah is with the righteous (muttaqin)' → taqwa.

9:124.notes: When a surah revealed, believers' faith increases; hypocrites' corruption deepens → the-quran. v.125 'they die as unbelievers' → disbelief. v.126 they do not repent → repentance (negatively invoked, but repentance is explicit subject: 'they do not repent'). Hypocrisy of those who slip away.

9:128.notes: Single verse about the Prophet's character → muhammad. 'From among yourselves' addresses humanity broadly → mankind. 'Compassionate and merciful' toward believers → mercy.

9:129.notes: 'Say: Allah is enough for me; there is no god except He' → qul-statements + tawhid. 'In Him I have put my trust' → trust-in-god. 'Lord of the Sublime Throne' → sovereignty. Direct address implies prophet's response → muhammad.

11:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Ra → disjoined-letters. The section describes the Quran's perfection, calls to worship Allah alone (tawhid), commands repentance, promises provision, and warns of a grievous Day. 'Wise and Informed' → wisdom + knowledge. 'Capable of all things' → power. The warner/bearer-of-good-news formula is prophethood-general. Verse 2 contains 'I am a warner… bearer of good news' as a qul-statement-style declaration (the imperative address 'That you shall worship none but Allah' functions as a Say-command); tagged qul-statements on this basis at medium confidence for that specific label.

11:5.notes: Verse 5: God knows what hearts conceal → knowledge. Verse 6: sustenance of every creature is on Allah → provision. 'Everything is in a Clear Book' → divine-decree.

11:7.notes: Creation of heavens and earth in six days → creation-of-heavens-earth. Disbelievers' reaction to resurrection → disbelievers + resurrection + day-of-judgment. Calling it 'plain witchcraft' → denial-of-revelation + mockery. Verse 11 explicitly names 'those who are patient' and promises forgiveness → patience (concrete trigger: the word 'patient'). Forgiveness/great reward → mercy.

11:12.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('perhaps you wish to disregard…', 'you are only a warner') → muhammad. Challenge to produce ten chapters → challenge-to-produce. 'He invented it' → denial-of-revelation. Disbelievers' demands for treasure/angel → disbelievers. 'Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy' → previous-scriptures. 'The Fire is his promise' → hell. 'Revealed with Allah's knowledge' → knowledge. Prophethood as a category throughout → prophethood-general. tawhid: 'there is no god but He'.

11:18.notes: Fabricating lies against Allah, witnesses on the Day → day-of-judgment + reckoning. Curse on wrongdoers → justice. Hindering from the path → corruption-on-earth. Doubled punishment → hell. Disbelief in the Hereafter → disbelief. Believers who humble themselves → paradise + believers. Verse 24 parable of blind/deaf vs. seeing/hearing summarises the two groups.

11:25.notes: Noah's mission to his people → noah. Worship none but Allah → tawhid. Disbelieving notables' rejection → disbelievers. 'Clear warner', 'messenger' → prophethood-general. Warning of a painful Day → day-of-judgment. 'Allah knows what lies in their souls' / 'Allah is Aware' → knowledge. 'He has given me a mercy' → mercy. 'It is Allah who will bring it upon you, if He wills' → divine-decree.

11:35.notes: Single verse: 'Say, if I made it up…' → qul-statements. The accusation of fabrication → denial-of-revelation. The Quran's authenticity is the subject → the-quran.

11:36.notes: Revelation to Noah that no more will believe → divine-decree. Building the ark under God's eyes → divine-decree + noah. Mockery by his people → mockery + disbelievers. 'Forgiving and Merciful' (closing formula in v.41) → mercy. Noah calling to his son, warning him not to be with disbelievers → marriage-and-family (family relationship, son's fate). Son drowning: 'except for him on whom He has mercy' → mercy, divine-decree.

11:44.notes: Flood's end, ark settling on Judi → noah + punishment-of-past-nations. Noah's uttered prayer about his son: 'O My Lord, my son is of my family… Your promise is true, and You are the Wisest of the wise' → dua-family-offspring (asking about his son/family) + wisdom (attribute invoked). God's reply correcting Noah → divine-decree. Noah's second uttered supplication: 'I seek refuge with You… Unless You forgive me and have mercy on me' → dua-forgiveness (forgiveness explicitly requested) + mercy. Blessings pronounced on Noah and communities → mercy. Verse 49 addresses patience and revelation of hidden stories → prophethood-general. 'The future belongs to the pious' (taqwa-adjacent but 'pious'/'muttaqin' is named) — borderline; tagging taqwa because 'muttaqin' appears explicitly.

11:50.notes: Hud sent to 'Ad → hud + ad. Call to worship Allah alone → tawhid. Their idols → shirk. Their rejection of Hud → disbelievers + denial-of-revelation. 'I have placed my trust in Allah' (v.56) → trust-in-god (explicit). 'Ask forgiveness… repent' (v.52) → repentance (explicit command). Salvation of Hud and believers, destruction of 'Ad → punishment-of-past-nations + mercy. Prophethood theme → prophethood-general. Day-of-Resurrection curse → day-of-judgment. Adding day-of-judgment for v.60 curse on Day of Resurrection.

11:61.notes: Salih sent to Thamud → salih + thamud. 'Worship Allah, no god other than Him' → tawhid. 'He initiated you from the earth' → human-creation. 'My Lord is Near and Responsive' → nearness-and-response (explicit attribute). She-camel as a sign → miracles. Hamstringing the she-camel and destruction → punishment-of-past-nations. Salvation by mercy → mercy. 'The Strong, the Mighty' (v.66) → power. Prophethood → prophethood-general. Disbelievers' rejection → disbelievers.

11:69.notes: Messengers (angels) come to Abraham → abraham + angels. Good news of Isaac and Jacob (v.71) → isaac + jacob. Abraham's wife laughs → marriage-and-family (wife/family). 'Mercy and blessings of Allah upon you… He is Praiseworthy and Glorious' → mercy + praise (praise uttered). Abraham's intercession for Lot's people → lot. 'The command of your Lord has come; irreversible punishment' → divine-decree + punishment-of-past-nations. 'You are the Wisest of the wise' (cf. v.45 in prior section; here v.73 praises God as Hamid Majid) → wisdom. Adding praise for 'He is Praiseworthy and Glorious' (v.73).

11:77.notes: Angels arrive at Lot → lot + angels. His people rush to commit sins (their habitual evil) → corruption-on-earth + disbelievers. Lot offers his daughters → marriage-and-family. Angels reveal the command and tell Lot to flee, his wife's fate → divine-decree + marriage-and-family. City overturned, stones rained down → punishment-of-past-nations.

11:84.notes: 15 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Shuaib sent to Madyan → shuayb + madyan. Tawhid call → tawhid. Do not short-measure/weight → trade-and-debt + justice-and-witness. 'Do not spread corruption in the land' (v.85, explicit) → corruption-on-earth. Repentance commanded (v.90) → repentance. 'My Lord is Merciful and Loving' (v.90 closing) → mercy. 'In Him I trust' (v.88 explicit) → trust-in-god. References to people of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot (v.89) → noah + hud + salih + lot. Prophethood → prophethood-general. Destruction of past nations → punishment-of-past-nations. Trim candidates: justice-and-witness (subsumed under trade-and-debt for the weighing context), lot (only a passing reference in v.89 alongside others).

11:91.notes: People threaten Shuaib → shuayb + disbelievers. Salvation of Shuaib and believers, destruction of wrongdoers → punishment-of-past-nations + mercy. Thamud mentioned in comparison (v.95) → thamud. 'My Lord comprehends everything you do' → knowledge. Prophethood → prophethood-general. Madyan destroyed → madyan.

11:96.notes: Moses sent with signs → moses + miracles. To Pharaoh and nobles → pharaoh. Pharaoh's command not wise → disbelievers. Pharaoh leading people into the Fire on Day of Resurrection → hell + day-of-judgment. Curse in this world and the next → punishment-of-past-nations. Prophethood → prophethood-general.

11:100.notes: Reports of destroyed towns → punishment-of-past-nations. Their gods availed them nothing → shirk + disbelievers. Day of Gathering for all humanity → day-of-judgment + mankind. The miserable in the Fire → hell. The happy in Paradise → paradise. 'We only postpone it until a predetermined time' → divine-decree. 'We did not wrong them' → justice. 'Your Lord is Doer of whatever He wills' → sovereignty.

11:109.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('So be not in doubt', 'be upright as you are commanded') → muhammad. Moses given the Scripture which was disputed → moses + previous-scriptures. 'He is Aware of everything they do' → knowledge. 'Those who repented with you' (v.112 explicit tawbah) → repentance. 'The Fire may touch you' → hell. Full recompense → justice. Disbelievers worshipping as ancestors → disbelievers. 'Be upright' addresses the Prophet and believers as commanded — taqwa is not named explicitly. However, 'do not transgress' and 'do not incline toward wrongdoers' are direct moral injunctions; taqwa is not the explicit subject, so not tagged.

11:114.notes: Establish prayer at borders of day → prayer (explicit institution). 'Good deeds take away bad deeds. This is a reminder for those who remember' → remembrance (explicit). 'Be patient' (v.115, explicit sabr) → patience. Speaking against corruption on earth (v.116, explicit 'fasad') → corruption-on-earth. 'Allah will not waste the reward of the virtuous' → mercy. 'I will fill Hell with jinn and humans' (v.119) → hell + jinn + mankind. 'The Word of your Lord is final' → divine-decree. Had your Lord willed, one community → divine-decree (reinforced).

11:120.notes: Narrating stories of messengers to strengthen the Prophet's heart → muhammad + prophethood-general + the-quran. 'A reminder for the believers' → believers. 'Say to those who do not believe' (v.121 qul) → qul-statements + disbelievers.

11:123.notes: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth → knowledge + sovereignty + creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Worship Him and rely on Him' → tawhid + trust-in-god (explicit tawakkul). 'Your Lord is never unaware' → knowledge (reinforced).

12:1.notes: Section opens with Alif-Lam-Ra (disjoined letters) and immediately identifies these as verses of the Clear Book revealed as an Arabic Quran.

12:3.notes: Joseph's dream of eleven planets and the sun/moon bowing to him; Jacob warns him not to tell his brothers lest they plot. Abraham and Isaac named as forefathers. God's choosing and teaching Joseph. Closing formula 'Knowing and Wise' triggers knowledge+wisdom. Iblis named as man's enemy triggers iblis label.

12:7.notes: Brothers' envy of Joseph and his brother, their plot to kill or abandon Joseph, and the compromise suggestion to throw him in the well. Envy is the explicit driver ('dearer to our father than we are'). Plotting (makr/kayd) is explicit. Anger-and-violence: murder discussed.

12:11.notes: Brothers deceive Jacob to take Joseph out; Jacob's fear and their false reassurance. The domestic family dynamics and the deception/plotting are central.

12:15.notes: Joseph thrown into the well; God's revelation to him. Brothers return with fake blood-stained shirt. Jacob's response 'patience is beautiful' is an explicit invocation of sabr, meeting the rule-5 trigger. Divine-decree: God inspires Joseph. Slander: false story told to Jacob.

12:19.notes: Caravan finds Joseph in the well, sells him as merchandise for a cheap price. Knowledge: 'Allah was aware of what they did.' Trade-and-debt: the sale transaction. Manumission-and-captives: Joseph treated as a slave commodity.

12:21.notes: Egyptian buyer takes Joseph in, plans to adopt him. God establishes Joseph in the land to teach him interpretation of events. 'Allah has control over His affairs' → divine-decree. 'Most people do not know' → knowledge. Wisdom implicit in the plan but not explicitly named — dropping it; knowledge sufficient.

12:22.notes: Joseph reaches maturity and receives wisdom/knowledge from God. The seduction attempt by the wife, Joseph's refusal ('Allah forbid'), the tearing of his shirt, the confrontation with her husband, and the shirt evidence. Knowledge and wisdom explicitly granted. Sincerity: Joseph's 'He is my Lord, He has given me a good home' models sincere loyalty. Plotting: her scheme. Justice-and-witness: the shirt-evidence adjudication.

12:30.notes: City women gossip; wife invites them and they marvel at Joseph. Wife threatens imprisonment. Joseph utters an explicit du'a: 'My Lord, prison is more desirable… unless You turn their scheming away from me' — uttered supplication in distress → dua-distress. God answers him → nearness-and-response. Closing 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' → knowledge. Plotting: women's scheme. Sincerity: Joseph's steadfastness. Slander: women's gossip about the wife is borderline but the primary frame is the seduction scheme, not the slander itself.

12:35.notes: Short section: decision to imprison Joseph despite seeing the signs; two fellow prisoners recount their dreams to Joseph. Divine decree implicit in what befalls Joseph. Simple narrative transition.

12:37.notes: Joseph speaks to his prison companions: attributes his knowledge to God's teaching; rejects the religion of non-believers; follows the faith of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; explicitly refutes multiple lords ('are diverse lords better or Allah the One?'); charges them with worshipping mere names without divine authority; affirms judgment belongs to God alone. Tawhid: explicit assertion of God's oneness. Shirk: 'not for us to associate anything with Allah.' Disbelief: 'people who do not believe in Allah… they are deniers.' Day-of-judgment: 'regarding the Hereafter, they are deniers' implies eschatological reference. Prophethood-general: Joseph's prophetic teaching role.

12:43.notes: The king's dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones and grain spikes; his court cannot interpret it; the released prisoner remembers Joseph and offers to go to him. Joseph's interpretive gift (from God) is the background. Narrative setup — minimal direct theological content beyond Joseph's God-given knowledge.

12:46.notes: Joseph interprets the king's dream: seven years of plenty, seven of hardship, then relief. Provision: agricultural management, storing food. Knowledge: Joseph's divinely-given interpretive ability. Divine-decree: the predetermined cycle of years.

12:50.notes: King summons Joseph; Joseph insists on clearing his name first regarding the women who cut their hands. Women and the governor's wife confess the truth about Joseph's innocence. Joseph (or the wife per some readings) acknowledges human weakness: 'the soul commands evil except those on whom my Lord has mercy.' Closing: 'my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Knowledge: 'my Lord is well aware of their schemes.' Justice-and-witness: the inquiry and testimony. Plotting: the schemes of the betrayers explicitly referenced.

12:54.notes: King establishes Joseph in authority over the land's storehouses. God establishes Joseph and rewards the righteous. 'We touch with Our mercy whomever We will' → mercy. 'The reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and observed piety' — taqwa explicitly named ('ittaqaw'), paradise implied by 'reward of the Hereafter' → taqwa, paradise. Sovereignty: Joseph given authority over the land's treasuries. Medium confidence on paradise — it is implied rather than described.

12:58.notes: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt; he recognizes them but they do not recognize him. He provides for them and demands they bring their other brother. Short narrative section. Knowledge: Joseph recognizes them while they do not recognize him. Plotting: Joseph's strategy of withholding the brother's identity.

12:63.notes: Brothers return to Jacob; he demands a pledge before Allah for Benjamin's safety. 'Allah is the Best Guardian and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful' → mercy. Jacob instructs them to enter by different gates, saying 'on Him I rely' — explicit tawakkul → trust-in-god. 'The decision rests only with Allah' → sovereignty (but sovereignty not centrally argued; trust-in-god is the explicit theme). Covenant/oaths: formal pledge before Allah. Knowledge: Jacob's divinely-taught knowledge noted at end.

12:69.notes: Joseph reveals himself to his full brother; places the cup in Benjamin's bag; the accusation of theft; the brothers' denial and their offer of a substitute. Plotting: Joseph's stratagem with the cup. Justice-and-witness: the legal proceedings around the alleged theft. Covenant: the brothers' earlier pledge invoked.

12:76.notes: The cup found in Benjamin's bag through God's plan for Joseph. 'We devised a plan for Joseph; he could not have detained his brother unless Allah so willed' → divine-decree. 'We elevate by degrees whomever We will' → sovereignty. 'Above every person of knowledge, there is one more learned' → knowledge.

12:77.notes: Brothers slander Joseph's past; Joseph keeps his composure. 'Allah is Aware of what you allege' → knowledge. Brothers invoke the pledge given to Jacob and acknowledge their earlier failure with Joseph. The eldest refuses to leave without his father's permission or God's decision. Justice-and-witness: the brothers testify about the theft.

12:83.notes: Jacob responds with beautiful patience again ('Patience is a virtue' — explicit sabr); expresses hope God will reunite them. 'He is the Knowing, the Wise' → knowledge, wisdom. Jacob says 'I only complain of my grief to Allah' (not quite a formal du'a utterance but a cry to God) — borderline; not tagging as dua-distress as it lacks the formal supplication form. Jacob urges sons not to despair of God's mercy: 'None despairs of Allah's comfort except the disbelieving people' → disbelief as explicit contrast. Trust-in-god: Jacob's reliance implied but patience is the explicit named virtue.

12:88.notes: Brothers confess their past sin to Joseph; Joseph reveals himself; reunion. 'He who practices piety and patience — Allah never fails to reward the righteous': taqwa and patience explicitly named. 'Allah has been gracious to us' → mercy. 'Allah will forgive you. He is the Most Merciful of the merciful' → mercy. Brothers acknowledge wrongdoing ('we were definitely in the wrong') → repentance theme present. Joseph forgives them. Zakat-and-charity: 'be charitable towards us — Allah rewards the charitable' — explicit sadaqah mention. The miraculous shirt restoring Jacob's sight is a minor miracle but the section's core is the reunion and forgiveness.

12:94.notes: Jacob senses Joseph's presence. The shirt restores Jacob's eyesight — miracle. 'I know from Allah what you do not know' → knowledge. Brothers ask Jacob to pray for forgiveness of their sins — 'Father, pray for the forgiveness of our sins' — this is a request for intercession/du'a. Jacob says 'I will ask my Lord to forgive you' — he utters a commitment to supplicate for forgiveness → dua-forgiveness. Closing 'He is the Forgiver, the Most Merciful' → mercy. Miracles: restoration of sight through the shirt.

12:99.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: marriage-and-family (family reunion is the context but not the legal/institutional subject of the section; the surah's family theme is pervasive). Suggest trimming marriage-and-family.

12:102.notes: God addresses the Prophet about this revealed narrative being unseen knowledge. Most people will not believe. The Quran is a reminder for all mankind. Signs in the heavens and earth ignored. Most associate partners with God. Warning about sudden punishment or the Hour. Verse 108: 'Say, this is my way… Glory be to Allah and I am not of the polytheists' → qul-statements, praise (subhan Allah uttered), shirk (negated). The-quran: the narrative is framed as divine revelation. Mankind: 'reminder for all mankind.' Disbelief: explicit. Shirk: explicit. Signs-of-the-hour: the Hour coming suddenly. Day-of-judgment: punishment or the Hour. Prophethood-general: the Prophet's mission framed.

12:109.notes: God sent men from towns before the Prophet; people should travel and see the fate of past nations. The Hereafter is better for the righteous (taqwa explicitly: 'those who are righteous/ittaqaw'). Messengers nearly despaired before God's help came; disbelievers punished. Day-of-judgment: the Home of the Hereafter. Punishment-of-past-nations: explicit reference to consequences for those before. Prophethood-general: the pattern of sending messengers. Disbelievers: 'guilty people' whom God's severity strikes.

12:111.notes: Closing verse: the stories of the prophets contain lessons; the Quran is not fabricated but confirms what came before and provides detailed guidance and mercy for believers. The-quran: the Quran itself described. Previous-scriptures: confirmation of what came before it. Guidance: explicitly named ('hudā'). Mercy: explicitly named ('rahmah'). Believers: 'for people who believe' — the addressed beneficiaries.

13:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Meem-Ra → disjoined-letters. Verse 1 asserts the Scripture's truth with most people not believing → the-quran, disbelievers. Verses 2–4 describe God raising heavens, the Throne, sun and moon running courses → creation-of-heavens-earth, cosmic-bodies, sovereignty, power. Spread earth, mountains, rivers, fruits, night/day cycle → natural-signs. Fruits and provision of the earth → provision. 'Signs for people who reflect/reason' frames mankind as the addressed audience.

13:5.notes: Verse 5: denial of resurrection ('when we are dust, a new creation?') → resurrection, disbelievers; 'yokes around their necks, inhabitants of the Fire' → hell. Verse 6: 'examples have passed away before them' → punishment-of-past-nations; 'your Lord is full of forgiveness… yet severe in retribution' → mercy, justice. Verse 7: disbelievers demand a miracle; 'you are only a warner' → prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation.

13:8.notes: Verses 8–9: 'Allah knows what every female bears… everything is by measure'; 'Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, the Grand, the Supreme' → knowledge, sovereignty, power. Verse 10: God's equal knowledge of hidden and manifest speech → knowledge. Verse 11: angelic succession guarding humans; 'Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves'; His hardship-will is irresistible → divine-decree, power, angels.

13:12.notes: Verses 12–13: lightning, heavy clouds, thunder glorifying God, angels in awe, thunderbolts → natural-signs, angels, praise (thunder 'praises His glory'), power. 'He is Tremendous in might' → sovereignty/power. Verse 14: 'To Him belongs the call to truth; those they call upon besides Him respond with nothing' → tawhid, shirk, disbelievers. Verse 15: everything in heavens and earth prostrates to Allah willingly or unwillingly → sovereignty, tawhid.

13:16.notes: Verse 16: four 'Say:' imperatives → qul-statements; 'Allah is the Creator of all things, the One, the Irresistible' → tawhid, creation, sovereignty; 'associates who cannot profit or harm themselves' → shirk; blind vs. seeing, darkness vs. light → guidance metaphor. Verse 17: rain flowing in riverbeds, froth parable for truth vs. falsehood → natural-signs. Verse 18: those who do not respond face 'worst reckoning' and Hell → reckoning, hell, disbelievers.

13:19.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Verse 19: contrast of the knowing vs. the blind; 'only those who reason will remember' → believers. Verse 20: 'fulfill the promise to Allah, do not violate the agreement' → covenant. Verse 21: 'join what Allah commanded to be joined, fear their Lord, dread the dire reckoning' → taqwa, reckoning. Verse 22: 'those who patiently seek… pray regularly… spend from Our provisions… repel evil with good' → patience (sabr explicitly named), prayer, zakat-and-charity, righteous-conduct, provision. Verses 23–24: Gardens, parents/spouses/descendants entering, angels at every gate, 'Peace be upon you because you endured' → paradise, angels. Verse 25: those who violate covenant, sever ties, spread corruption → covenant (breach), corruption-on-earth. Verse 26: Allah expands/restricts provision → provision.

13:27.notes: Verse 27: disbelievers demand a miracle → disbelievers, miracles; 'Say, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whoever repents' → qul-statements, guidance, divine-decree. Verse 28: 'hearts find comfort in the remembrance of Allah' — remembrance explicitly named → remembrance, believers. Verse 29: believers doing righteous deeds, beautiful return → believers. Verse 30: sent among a community, they deny Ar-Rahman; 'Say, He is my Lord… in Him I trust, to Him is my repentance' → qul-statements, prophethood-general, the-quran; 'would have guided all humanity' → mankind. Verse 31: hypothetical Quran moving mountains; 'every decision rests with Allah'; disasters for disbelievers → the-quran, divine-decree.

13:32.notes: qul-statements also applies (verse 33 has 'Say') — adding it would push to 9 labels which is fine.

13:35.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: reckoning (subsumed by broader judgment theme), plotting (verse 42 mentions past nations' scheming but it is a secondary point). Verse 35: paradise for muttaqun, Fire for disbelievers → paradise, hell, taqwa, disbelievers. Verse 36: People of the Book rejoice at revelation, some factions reject parts; 'Say, I am commanded to worship Allah and never associate' → people-of-the-book, qul-statements, tawhid, shirk, the-quran. Verse 37: revealed as Arabic code → the-quran. Verse 38: messengers sent before with wives and offspring, signs only by God's permission → prophethood-general, divine-decree. Verse 39: 'Allah abolishes whatever He wills… with Him is the source of the Scripture' → divine-decree, the-quran. Verse 40: 'your duty is to inform, Ours is the reckoning' → prophethood-general, reckoning. Verse 41: 'Allah judges, nothing holds back His judgment' → sovereignty (implicit), reckoning. Verse 42: 'those before them planned, but the entire plan is up to Allah; He knows what every soul earns' → plotting, knowledge.

13:43.notes: Disbelievers deny the Prophet's messengership → disbelievers, prophethood-general. 'Say, Allah is a sufficient witness between me and you' → qul-statements. 'Whoever has knowledge of the Scripture' — refers to those with knowledge of prior scripture (people of the Book / scripture scholars) → people-of-the-book, the-quran, knowledge.

14:1.notes: Disjoined letters Alif-Lam-Ra open the section. 'Bring humanity from darkness to light' is an explicit guidance trigger. 'Almighty, Praiseworthy' → sovereignty/power. 'Mighty, Wise' closing → wisdom. Guidance named explicitly as the Quran's purpose satisfies rule-5 trigger for the guidance label.

14:5.notes: 'Every patient and thankful person' names patience (sabr) and gratitude (shukr) explicitly, satisfying rule-5 triggers for both. Pharaoh's people referenced as oppressors of Bani Israel. 'Days of Allah' refers to past signs and punishments. Moses sent with signs → miracles.

14:9.notes: Noah, 'Ad, Thamud named explicitly. Messengers' reply includes 'In Allah let the faithful put their trust' and 'We will persevere' — both patience (sabr named via 'persevere/patience') and trust-in-god are explicitly named/commanded. 'Maker of the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. Denial of messengers → denial-of-revelation.

14:13.notes: 'We will destroy the wrongdoers / settle you in the land after them' references expulsion of messengers (migration motif) and divine punishment of past peoples. 'He who fears My Majesty' is an explicit taqwa trigger. Hell described in vivid detail (v16–17). Works-like-ashes simile for disbelievers.

14:19.notes: Iblis's speech on the Day of Judgment is the centrepiece. Creation of heavens and earth asserted (v19). Power: 'He can do away with you and bring a new creation / that is not difficult for Allah.' Shirk: Satan says 'I reject your associating with me in the past.' Paradise described (v23). Hell implicit in Satan's speech about torment.

14:24.notes: The good-word/bad-word parable is addressed to 'the people' (mankind). 'Allah presents the parables to the people' — explicit universal address. Good word = firm faith/truth (tayyibah kalimah per tafsir), bad word = kufr. Guidance is the implicit fruit. Wisdom label earned by the parable structure itself being attributed to Allah's teaching. The-quran: the parable is about the word of God vs. falsehood.

14:28.notes: Two 'Qul' imperatives present (v30, v31) → qul-statements. Shirk: 'they set up rivals to Allah.' Hell: 'your destination is the Fire.' Prayer and zakat-and-charity explicitly enjoined on believers (v31). Day of Judgment referenced as the Day of no trading or friendship.

14:32.notes: Rain, fruits, ships, rivers → natural-signs and provision. Sun, moon, night, day → cosmic-bodies. 'Created the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth and creation. 'If you were to count Allah's blessings you would not enumerate them' is an explicit gratitude trigger (recognising blessings as innumerable). Mankind implicit in 'for your sustenance' universal address.

14:35.notes: 14 labels — over the 12-label ceiling. Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac all named. Multiple uttered supplications: 'Rabbi-j'al hadha al-balad aminan' (dua-protection for the land and family from idol-worship); 'keep me and my sons from worshiping idols' (dua-protection + dua-family-offspring); 'provide them with fruits' (dua-family-offspring / provision); 'Rabbanā ighfir lī wa-liwālidayya' (dua-forgiveness); 'al-ḥamdu lillāh' in v39 (praise + dua-gratitude). Sacred House / valley mentioned → sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. Prayer explicitly asked for offspring to establish it. Mercy: 'You are Forgiving and Merciful.' Knowledge: 'You know what we conceal and what we reveal.' Trim candidates if needed: dua-gratitude (subsumed by praise in v39), dua-family-offspring (closely overlapping with dua-protection in context).

14:42.notes: 'Warn mankind' — explicit universal address. Allah defers wrongdoers to the Day → day-of-judgment with vivid imagery (v43). 'You inhabited the homes of those who wronged themselves' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'Their plans are known to Allah' → knowledge. 'They planned their plans' (makara) → plotting. Prophethood-general: the wrongdoers promise to follow the messengers.

14:47.notes: Allah will not break His promise to messengers → prophethood-general. 'The One, the Irresistible' → tawhid and sovereignty. Vivid Day of Judgment imagery (earth changed, sinners in chains, fire on faces). Reckoning: 'Allah is Quick in reckoning' (v51). Justice: 'repay each soul according to what it has earned.' Power: 'Allah is Strong, Able to Avenge.'

14:52.notes: 'A proclamation for mankind' — explicit universal address. 'Know that He is One God' → tawhid. 'People of understanding may remember' → remembrance (dhikr named as the purpose). The-quran: the verse describes the Quran's function as a proclamation and warning.

15:1.notes: Section opens with Alif-Lam-Ra disjoined letters → disjoined-letters. The Quran is explicitly named and its preservation declared (v9) → the-quran. Disbelievers wish they were Muslims (v2) and mock the Prophet as insane (v6) → disbelievers, mockery, denial-of-revelation. They demand angels (v7) → angels. Past nations sent messengers who were mocked (vv10-11) → prophethood-general, punishment-of-past-nations. Each nation has a set time (vv4-5) → divine-decree.

15:16.notes: Constellations placed in the sky and guarded from devils (vv16-18) → cosmic-bodies, creation-of-heavens-earth, iblis. Earth spread with mountains and balanced growth (v19) → natural-signs. Livelihoods created (v20) → provision. Stores of all things sent in precise measure (v21) → provision, divine-decree. Fertilizing winds and rain (v22) → natural-signs. God gives life and causes death (v23) → death-and-dying. He knows all who go before and behind (v24) → knowledge. Closing 'Wise, the Knowing' (v25) → wisdom, knowledge.

15:26.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Human created from clay and jinn from fire (vv26-27) → human-creation, jinn. Angels commanded to prostrate before Adam → adam, angels. Iblis refuses → iblis. Iblis's refusal is rooted in pride ('I am not about to prostrate before a human') → arrogance. Iblis requests reprieve until Day of Judgment (v36) and vows to lead humans astray → day-of-judgment. Except God's sincere servants (v40) implicitly invokes taqwa as the quality of those who are protected; v45 explicitly names 'the righteous' (al-muttaqin) → taqwa. Hell described with seven doors (vv43-44) → hell. Paradise described with gardens, springs, peace and security (vv45-48) → paradise. 'I am the Forgiver, the Merciful' (v49) → mercy. Iblis's vow and the reprieve decree → divine-decree.

15:51.notes: The guests (angels) visit Abraham (vv51-57) → abraham, angels. Abraham is given news of a knowledgeable boy → (Isaac implied but not named; not tagged per rule 3 — only named figures tagged). Abraham invokes 'Lord's mercy' (v56) → mercy. Angels sent to the sinful people (Lot's people) and will save Lot's family except his wife (vv58-60) → lot. The decree about Lot's wife being left behind → divine-decree.

15:61.notes: Angels arrive at Lot's family (v61) → lot, angels. The town's people come and Lot tries to protect his guests (vv67-71) → lot. The Blast destroys them (vv73-74) → punishment-of-past-nations. 'We informed him of Our decree' (v66) → divine-decree. 'Surely in that is a sign for the believers' (v77) → believers.

15:78.notes: People of the Woods (Ashab al-Aykah, associated with Madyan/Shuayb) → madyan. People of the Rock (al-Hijr, associated with Thamud) → thamud. Both rejected messengers and were destroyed → prophethood-general, punishment-of-past-nations, denial-of-revelation. The mountain-carving detail matches Thamud's known characteristic.

15:85.notes: 11 labels. Heavens and earth created with truth (v85) → creation-of-heavens-earth, creation. 'The Hour is coming' → day-of-judgment. 'Your Lord is the All-Knowing Creator' → knowledge, creation. 'Seven of the pairs and the Grand Quran' given to the Prophet (v87) → the-quran. Direct address to the Prophet ('do not extend your eyes', 'lower your wing', 'your heart is strained') → muhammad. 'And say, I am the clear warner' (v89) → qul-statements. 'Those who made the Quran obsolete' and questioning on the Day (vv91-93) → reckoning, denial-of-revelation subsumed by the-quran context. 'Turn away from the polytheists' (v94) → polytheists. Mockers mentioned (v95) → mockery. 'Glorify the praise of your Lord' (v98) — praise uttered as command to the Prophet; borderline but the formula 'sabbih bi-hamdi rabbika' is close to a praise utterance from the Prophet's perspective → praise. Note: denial-of-revelation trimmed in favor of the-quran (already captures the Quran-as-subject theme).

15:99.notes: A single-verse section commanding worship of God until certainty (death) comes. 'Worship your Lord' is an explicit instruction in devotion → remembrance (dhikr/worship). 'Until certainty comes' is a Qur'anic idiom for death, invoking sustained God-consciousness → taqwa. Only two labels appropriate for this brief closing verse.

16:1.notes: 12 labels at the ceiling. 'Subhanahu' in v1 and v3 triggers praise. V2 covers angels sent with revelation and tawhid proclamation. V3-8 cover creation of heavens/earth, humans from a drop, livestock/horses as provision and natural signs. Closing 'Rauf, Rahim' triggers mercy. V9 covers guidance. Trim candidates if needed: human-creation (brief mention) or prophethood-general (implicit via 'give warning').

16:10.notes: V10-11 rain, vegetation, fruits — natural-signs and provision. V12 night/day, sun, moon, stars — cosmic-bodies. V13 diverse things on earth — natural-signs. V14 sea, ships — natural-signs and provision. V15-16 mountains, rivers, stars for navigation — natural-signs. V17 rhetorical 'Is He who creates like him who does not?' — tawhid argument via creation.

16:18.notes: V18 God's uncountable favors + 'Forgiving and Merciful' (mercy). V19 God knows what you hide — knowledge. V20-21 idols create nothing and are dead themselves — tawhid and shirk refutation. V22 'Your God is one God' — tawhid explicitly. Those who deny the Hereafter are in denial — disbelief. 'They are arrogant' (mustakbirun) — arrogance explicitly named. V23 God knows what they conceal; He does not like the arrogant — knowledge and arrogance. Resurrection mentioned in v21 (when will they be resurrected) and implied Hereafter denial — day-of-judgment and resurrection.

16:24.notes: V24 'Legends of the ancients' — denial-of-revelation. V25 carrying full loads on Day of Resurrection — day-of-judgment and reckoning. V26 those before them schemed (makr) — plotting.
