V27 Day of Resurrection disgrace, disbelievers named explicitly — day-of-judgment, disbelievers. V28 angels taking souls — angels. V29 enter gates of Hell — hell. 'Miserable is the residence of the arrogant' — arrogance explicitly named. V28 'Allah is aware of what you used to do' — knowledge.

16:30.notes: V30 question to those who maintained piety (taqwa named explicitly) — taqwa. Gardens of perpetuity described — paradise. V32 angels taking the righteous in wholesome state — angels. V33-34 waiting for angels or command of the Lord; those before them did likewise — punishment-of-past-nations. V34 'what they used to ridicule engulfed them' — mockery (istahza'). Believers implicitly addressed as the pious, contrasted with disbelievers.

16:35.notes: V35 polytheists' fatalistic argument — polytheists and shirk. 'Are the messengers responsible for anything but clear communication?' — prophethood-general. V36 messengers sent to every community — prophethood-general. 'Worship Allah, avoid idolatry' — shirk refuted. 'See what the fate of the deniers was' — punishment-of-past-nations. V37 God does not guide those He has led astray — guidance and divine-decree. V38-39 denial of resurrection — resurrection and disbelief. V40 'Be, and it becomes' — divine-decree and power. V41 emigrants after persecution — migration. V42 those who endure patiently and trust their Lord — patience and trust-in-god explicitly named. 11 labels, within ceiling.

16:43.notes: V43 'We sent before you only men whom We inspired' — prophethood-general. 'Ask the people of knowledge' — previous-scriptures (ahl al-dhikr). V44 'We revealed to you the Reminder (dhikr) to clarify to the people' — the-quran and mankind (address to people generally).

16:45.notes: V45-46 those who scheme evils — plotting, disbelievers. 'Earth caving in' and unexpected punishment — power. V47 'Your Lord is Gentle and Merciful' — mercy. V48-50 shadows prostrating, everything in heavens and earth bowing including angels — natural-signs and angels. The universal prostration theme underscores God's sovereignty/power.

16:51.notes: V51 'Do not take two gods; He is only One God' — tawhid explicitly. V52 to Him belongs everything in heavens and earth — sovereignty. V53 every blessing is from Allah — provision. V53-54 when harm touches you, you call on Him; when lifted, some associate partners — shirk. V55 'Enjoy yourselves. You will soon know' — warning to disbelievers — disbelief. Mankind addressed broadly throughout.

16:56.notes: V56 allocating share of provision to false gods — shirk. 'You will be questioned' — reckoning. V57 attributing daughters to Allah — 'Subhanahu' uttered — praise. Also relates to pre-Islamic practice of female infanticide/marriage-and-family concerns. V58-59 burying daughters — marriage-and-family (female infanticide as family/social issue). V60 'Allah sets the Highest Example; He is the Mighty, the Wise' — wisdom. Those who do not believe in Hereafter — disbelief. day-of-judgment (Hereafter reference). V61 if Allah held mankind for injustices... postpones to appointed time — mankind, mercy (forbearance). V62 attribute what they dislike to Allah; for them is the Fire — disbelief.

16:63.notes: V63 messengers sent to communities before; Satan made deeds alluring — iblis, prophethood-general. 'He is their master today and they will have painful punishment' — disbelievers, punishment-of-past-nations. V64 'We revealed to you the Scripture to clarify... guidance and mercy for people who believe' — the-quran, guidance, mercy, believers.

16:65.notes: V65 rain reviving the earth — natural-signs, provision. V66 milk from cattle bellies — natural-signs, provision. V67 date-palms, grapevines producing drink and food (note: mention of intoxicant aspect sakan implied but not legislated here) — natural-signs, provision. V68-69 bees inspired by God, honey with healing — natural-signs, provision, creation (God's inspiration of the bee). 'For the people' — mankind. The section is a unified block of natural signs as proofs of God's creative provision.

16:70.notes: V70 God created you then takes you away; some reduced to feeble age — human-creation, death-and-dying. 'Allah is Omniscient and Omnipotent' — knowledge and power. V71 God favored some over others in livelihood — provision. Parable of master and slave not sharing equally — implicit shirk argument. V72 God gave you mates, children, grandchildren, good provisions — marriage-and-family, provision. V73 they serve what possesses no provisions — shirk refuted. V74 'Do not cite examples for Allah; Allah knows' — knowledge, tawhid.

16:75.notes: V75 parable of slave vs. free generous man — 'Al-hamdu lillah' uttered — praise. V76 parable of dumb burden vs. one who commands justice — tawhid argument. V77 'To Allah belongs the unseen of heavens and earth; the Hour is like a twinkling of the eye; Allah has power over everything' — knowledge, power, day-of-judgment. V78 brought you out of mothers' wombs knowing nothing; gave you hearing, sight, brains — human-creation. 'That you may give thanks' — gratitude not explicitly the subject but commanded (borderline; holding off). V79 birds flying sustained by Allah — natural-signs. V80-81 homes, livestock hides, garments — provision, natural-signs.

16:84.notes: V84 Day when a witness raised from every community — day-of-judgment, prophethood-general (witnesses are messengers). V85 wrongdoers see punishment — hell (punishment not lightened). V86 idolaters see their associates — polytheists, shirk. V87 they offer submission that Day; inventions abandon them — day-of-judgment, reckoning. V88 disbelievers and those who obstruct from Allah's path — added punishment 'on account of the mischief they used to make' — corruption-on-earth explicitly triggered by 'mischief/fasad'.

16:89.notes: Single verse section. 'We raise in every community a witness from among them' — day-of-judgment, prophethood-general. 'We bring you as a witness against these' — direct address to the Prophet (second person 'you/ka') — muhammad. 'We revealed to you the Book as explanation, guidance, mercy and good news for those who submit' — the-quran, guidance, mercy, believers.

16:90.notes: V90 'Allah commands justice, goodness, generosity toward relatives; forbids immorality, injustice, oppression' — justice, righteous-conduct (explicit instruction in righteous conduct). V91 'Fulfill Allah's covenant... do not break your oaths after ratifying them; Allah knows what you do' — oaths-and-vows, covenant, knowledge. V92 parable of woman unraveling yarn; oaths as deception; Allah testing; Day of Resurrection will clarify — day-of-judgment.

16:93.notes: V93 God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills — guidance, divine-decree. 'You will be questioned about what you used to do' — reckoning. V94-95 do not use oaths for deception — oaths-and-vows. V96 'We will reward the patient according to the best of their deeds' — patience explicitly named. V97 'Whoever works righteousness... while being a believer' — righteous-conduct explicitly named. 'We will grant him a good life' — provision of a good life; believers addressed. trust-in-god: implied by 'What is with Allah remains' but not named explicitly — dropping this; patience and righteous-conduct are explicitly named triggers.

16:98.notes: 16 verses, richly thematic. V98 seeking refuge from Satan while reading Quran — the-quran, iblis. V99-100 Satan's authority only over followers — iblis, believers. V101-103 substitution of verses; accusation of imposture — denial-of-revelation, the-quran. V102 'Say: The Holy Spirit brought it down' — qul-statements. V103-105 accusations; those who do not believe in Allah's revelations — disbelief, denial-of-revelation. V106 renouncing faith after belief — disbelief. V107-109 preferring worldly life; Allah sealed their hearts — disbelief. V110 those who emigrated after persecution and then struggled and persevered; 'your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful' — migration, mercy. V111 Day when every soul pleads for itself; paid in full — day-of-judgment, reckoning. V112-113 parable of ungrateful town; a messenger came and they denounced him — punishment-of-past-nations, prophethood-general. 12 labels at ceiling.

16:114.notes: V114 eat lawful and good things; be thankful for Allah's blessings — food-and-dietary, provision. 'Be thankful' (shukru) explicitly commanded — gratitude (shukr trigger). V115 forbidden foods listed — food-and-dietary. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' — mercy. V116 do not fabricate halal/haram — justice-and-witness (borderline) — keeping food-and-dietary. V118 for those who are Jews, We prohibited what We mentioned before — people-of-the-book (Jews explicitly named). V119 those who do wrong in ignorance then repent — repentance explicitly named.

16:120.notes: V120-122 Abraham described as devoted monotheist, not among polytheists, thankful for blessings — abraham, tawhid, shirk (negated), polytheists, gratitude (shakiran li-an'umihi — shukr explicitly). God guided him — guidance. V123 'We inspired you: follow the religion of Abraham the Monotheist' — direct address to Prophet — muhammad. V124 Sabbath decreed for those who differed about it (Jews context) — people-of-the-book. 'Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection' — day-of-judgment.

16:125.notes: V125 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good advice' — direct address to Prophet — muhammad, prophethood-general. 'Wisdom' (hikmah) explicitly named — wisdom. 'Your Lord knows those who stray and those who are guided' — knowledge, guidance. V126 if you retaliate, do so proportionately; if you resort to patience it is better — patience explicitly named. V127 'Be patient... do not grieve... do not be stressed by their schemes' — patience again, plotting (makr explicitly named in last word 'yamkurun').

16:128.notes: Single verse. 'Allah is with those who are righteous (taqwa) and those who are virtuous (muhsinun)' — taqwa explicitly named, righteous-conduct (ihsan/virtuous conduct explicitly named), believers (those described are the faithful).

17:1.notes: Verse 1: 'Subhana' opens with praise formula; Muhammad's night journey from Sacred Mosque; Moses given Scripture as guide for Children of Israel; Noah named as appreciative servant. Knowledge tagged for 'the Listener, the Beholder' closing attribute. Sacred-mosque-and-qiblah tagged for al-Masjid al-Haram. Miracles tagged for the Isra itself as a miraculous sign shown to the Prophet.

17:4.notes: The section narrates God's decree to Children of Israel about two episodes of corruption on earth, the punishment sent against them, their restoration, and closes with Hell for disbelievers and hope of mercy. 'Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you' triggers mercy. Divine-decree tagged for 'We conveyed… in the Scripture.' Corruption-on-earth explicitly named ('you will commit evil on earth').

17:9.notes: The Quran described as guide (guidance explicitly named); good news for believers with great reward (paradise implied); painful punishment for disbelievers (hell). Verse 12: night and day as two signs (cosmic-bodies). Verse 13: fate attached to neck, record on Day of Resurrection (reckoning, divine-decree). Verse 14: self-reckoning on the Day (reckoning confirmed).

17:15.notes: Verse 15: no punishment without sending a messenger (prophethood-general, justice/divine-decree). Verse 16: destruction of towns (punishment-of-past-nations). Verse 17: many generations destroyed after Noah (punishment-of-past-nations). Verse 18: Hell for those who desire the fleeting life. Verse 20: God's gifts extended to all (provision). Verse 17 closing: 'Your Lord is sufficient as Knower and Beholder' (knowledge). Guidance named explicitly in v15.

17:22.notes: 15 labels — over the 12-label ceiling. Full ethical code section: tawhid/shirk (v22 do not set up another god); righteous-conduct (general ethical conduct toward parents, orphans, wayfarers, honesty in measure); marriage-and-family (honor parents); zakat-and-charity (give relative/poor/wayfarer their rights, v26); orphan-care (v34 do not go near orphan's property); covenant (v34 honor your pledge); trade-and-debt (v35 give full measure, accurate scales); iblis (v27 extravagant are brethren of devils); provision (v30 Lord expands/restricts rizq); mercy (v28 seeking mercy from your Lord; v25 He is Forgiving); knowledge (v30 closing 'fully Informed'); humility (v24 'lower to them the wing of humility' — word explicitly used); dua-forgiveness (v24 'My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was a child' — uttered supplication). Trim candidates if needed: trade-and-debt (subsumed in righteous-conduct context), humility (borderline — word used but not primary subject).

17:31.notes: Ethical injunctions: do not kill children (anger-and-violence, provision — 'We provide for them'); do not come near adultery (marriage-and-family); do not kill the soul except in justice (anger-and-violence, justice-and-witness); orphan's property (orphan-care); honor pledge (covenant); full measure and accurate scales (trade-and-debt); do not pursue what you have no knowledge of (justice-and-witness); do not walk proudly (arrogance — 'walking proudly' is the explicit vice named). Righteous-conduct tagged as the section is structured as a series of explicit ethical instructions.

17:39.notes: Verse 39: 'some of the wisdom your Lord has revealed' — wisdom explicitly named; do not set up another god (tawhid/shirk); thrown in Hell (hell). Verse 40: challenge to the polytheist claim that God took daughters from angels (shirk, angels). Knowledge implicit in 'Your Lord knows' context but not explicitly named here; dropping it. Confidence high on tawhid, shirk, hell, wisdom, angels.

17:41.notes: Verse 41: the Quran explained in various ways (the-quran). Verse 42: 'Say' (qul-statements) — if there were other gods they would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne (tawhid, shirk, sovereignty). Verse 43: 'Subhanahu' — praise formula uttered (praise). Verse 44: seven heavens and earth praise Him (creation-of-heavens-earth); closing 'Forbearing and Forgiving' (mercy). Disbelievers implicitly addressed throughout.

17:45.notes: Verses 45–48: Quran recitation, veil placed between Prophet and non-believers, their mockery/denial (the-quran, disbelievers, denial-of-revelation, knowledge — 'We know well'). Verses 49–52: disbelievers deny resurrection ('shall we really be resurrected?'); multiple 'Say' commands (qul-statements); 'The One who originated you the first time' — power and creation; Day when He calls you — resurrection. Tawhid tagged for 'The One who originated you.'

17:53.notes: Verse 53: Tell My servants to say what is best; Satan sows discord (iblis). Verse 54: Your Lord knows you best, mercy or punishment (knowledge, mercy). Verse 55: 'Your Lord knows well' (knowledge); prophets favored over others (prophethood-general); David given the Psalms (david, previous-scriptures). Verse 56: 'Say' — call on those besides Him, they have no power (qul-statements, shirk). Verse 57: those they call upon seek access to their Lord, fear punishment. Verse 58: every city will be destroyed before Day of Resurrection, inscribed in the Book (punishment-of-past-nations, divine-decree).

17:59.notes: Verse 59: ancients denied miraculous signs; Thamud given the she-camel (a visible sign) but mistreated her (thamud, miracles, denial-of-revelation). Verse 60: 'We said to you that your Lord encompasses humanity' — direct address to Prophet (muhammad); the vision shown to him as a test for the people (mankind); knowledge invoked implicitly. Muhammad tagged for direct 'We said to you.'

17:61.notes: Classic Iblis-prostration narrative: angels commanded to bow to Adam (adam, angels, iblis); Satan's refusal and claim of superiority (arrogance — explicitly 'honored more than me', the refusal narrative); his vow to mislead Adam's descendants (divine-decree for God's response); Hell as reward for followers (hell); Adam created from mud (human-creation).

17:66.notes: Verse 66: ships propelled at sea for your bounty (natural-signs, provision); 'He is towards you Most Merciful' (mercy). Verse 67: harm at sea, those prayed to vanish except Him (tawhid implied but not the explicit subject); saved to land then turn away — 'The human being is ever thankless' (disbelief, gratitude — ingratitude explicitly named). Verses 68–69: power to destroy on land or sea (power). Verse 70: honored Children of Adam, carried on land and sea, provided good things (mankind — 'Children of Adam' = universal; provision). Gratitude tagged because ingratitude (kufur as thanklessness) is the explicit subject of v67.

17:71.notes: Verses 71–72: Day when every people called with their leader; record given in right hand; blind in this world = blind in Hereafter (day-of-judgment, reckoning). Verses 73–77: direct address to Prophet — 'they almost lured you away from what We revealed to you'; 'Had We not given you stability'; threat of double punishment; they almost expelled him — all substantively about the Prophet's personal situation and mission (muhammad, prophethood-general). Disbelievers as the opposing party. Knowledge implied in God's awareness but not named explicitly; dropping it. Divine-decree tagged for 'The tradition of the messengers We sent before you — you will find no change in Our rules.'

17:78.notes: Verse 78: prayer at decline of sun through darkness of night; Quran at dawn (prayer, the-quran). Verse 79: night vigil tahajjud as extra prayer for the Prophet (prayer, muhammad). Verse 80: 'Say, My Lord, lead me in through an entry of truth…' — uttered supplication (dua-protection — seeking God's supporting power and truthful path). Verse 81: 'Say, the truth has come and falsehood has withered' (qul-statements). Guidance tagged because v80 asks to be led on the path of truth.

17:82.notes: Verse 82: Quran as healing and mercy for believers (the-quran, believers, mercy). Verse 83: human being turns away in blessing and despairs in adversity — no concept label triggered explicitly. Verse 84: 'Say, each does according to his disposition; your Lord knows best who is better guided' (qul-statements, knowledge, guidance — 'better guided in the way' explicitly names guidance).

17:85.notes: Verse 85: question about the Spirit; 'Say, the Spirit belongs to the domain of my Lord; you were given only little knowledge' (qul-statements, knowledge). Verse 86–87: God could take away the revelation; except through mercy (the-quran, mercy). Verse 88: 'Say, if mankind and jinn came together to produce the like of this Quran' — challenge to produce (challenge-to-produce, qul-statements, mankind, jinn). Verse 89: displayed for mankind every similitude, most insist on denying (denial-of-revelation, mankind, disbelievers). Verses 90–93: demands for miracles; 'Say, Glory be to my Lord. Am I anything but a human messenger?' (prophethood-general, qul-statements, praise implied in Subhana). Verse 94–96: nothing prevented people from believing except 'Did Allah send a human messenger?' (prophethood-general); multiple Say commands (qul-statements). 11 labels — within ceiling.

17:97.notes: Verse 97: whomever God guides is the guided one; gathered on Day of Resurrection blind/dumb/deaf; abode is Hell (guidance, day-of-judgment, hell, resurrection). Verse 98: punishment for denying revelations and denying resurrection (disbelief). Verse 99: 'Do they not consider that Allah who created the heavens and the earth is Able to create the likes of them?' (power, creation-of-heavens-earth). Verse 100: 'Say' — if you possessed the treasuries of my Lord's mercy you would withhold for fear of spending; human being is stingy (qul-statements, greed-and-miserliness, mercy).

17:101.notes: Moses given nine clear signs (moses, miracles); ask the Children of Israel (children-of-israel); Pharaoh calls Moses bewitched (pharaoh, denial-of-revelation); Moses responds that only the Lord of the heavens and earth sent these as eye-openers (knowledge); Pharaoh drowned with all his people (punishment-of-past-nations); God said to Children of Israel to inhabit the land and at the promise of the Hereafter brought together (divine-decree).

17:105.notes: Verse 105: Quran sent with truth; Prophet sent as bearer of good news and warner (the-quran, prophethood-general). Verse 106: Quran unfolded gradually (the-quran). Verse 107: 'Say, believe in it or do not'; those given knowledge before it (people-of-the-book — those given knowledge before the Quran per tafsir) fall prostrating (qul-statements, people-of-the-book). Verse 108: 'Glory to our Lord' — praise uttered (praise). Verse 109: fall weeping, adds to their humility — humility explicitly named (humility). Believers implicit in those who respond with prostration and awe.

17:110.notes: Verse 110: 'Say, call Him Allah or call Him the Most Merciful; whichever name you use, to Him belong the Best Names' — tawhid (all names belong to One God), qul-statements, mercy (Al-Rahman explicitly invoked). Instruction on prayer volume (prayer). Knowledge implied in 'the Best Names' but not explicitly named; confidence in tawhid, prayer, qul-statements, mercy is high.

17:111.notes: Verse 111: 'Say, Praise be to Allah who has not begotten a son, nor has He a partner in sovereignty' — uttered praise formula (praise, qul-statements); assertion of God's absolute oneness, no son, no partner (tawhid, shirk refuted); sovereignty ('no partner in sovereignty'). Clean 5-label single-verse section.

18:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'al-hamdu lillah' → praise. The Quran as revealed Book is the subject → the-quran. Believers promised reward/paradise. Those who say 'Allah has begotten a son' → shirk + tawhid refutation. Verse 6 addresses the Prophet directly about his grief over non-believers → muhammad (direct second-person address to him about his personal distress).

18:7.notes: Verses 7–8 describe the earth as ornament for testing → natural-signs. Verse 9 introduces People of the Cave as a wondrous sign → companions-of-the-cave + miracles. Verse 10 contains the uttered supplication 'Rabbana atina min ladunka rahmatan wa hayyi' lana min amrina rashada' → mercy + dua-guidance. Verse 12: God's knowledge of their duration → knowledge. The sealing of their ears by God → divine-decree.

18:13.notes: The youth's declaration 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will not call on any god besides Him' → tawhid, rejection of shirk. Their people who 'taken gods other than Him' → shirk + disbelievers. God increasing them in guidance → guidance. Verse 16 mentions 'your Lord will unfold His mercy' → mercy.

18:17.notes: The sun veering from their cave → cosmic-bodies + natural-signs (the phenomenon framed as a sign of God). 'That was one of Allah's wonders' → miracles. 'He whom Allah guides is truly guided; he whom He misguides…' → guidance. The sleeping youths turned by God → companions-of-the-cave.

18:19.notes: The awakening and dialogue of the cave youth → companions-of-the-cave + miracles (miraculous sleep). 'Your Lord knows best how long you stayed' → knowledge. Sending one to city for provision/food → provision. Fear of persecution/forced return to their religion provides context but no specific label is triggered beyond the narrative.

18:21.notes: Their discovery 'that the promise of Allah is true, and that of the Hour there is no doubt' → day-of-judgment + resurrection. Verse 22 contains 'Qul rabbi a'lamu' → qul-statements. 'His is the mystery of the heavens and the earth' → knowledge. 'He shares His Sovereignty with no one' → sovereignty. The dispute about the number and building a mosque over them → companions-of-the-cave.

18:27.notes: Verse 27: 'Recite what was revealed to you from the Book of your Lord' → the-quran. Verse 28: 'those who pray to their Lord…desiring His Presence' + command not to follow the heedless → believers + remembrance (dhikr of Our remembrance explicitly mentioned). Verse 29: 'Qul al-haqqu min rabbikum' → qul-statements; disbelievers warned with Fire → disbelievers + hell. Verses 30–31: believers who do righteous deeds → believers + paradise (Gardens of Eden). guidance implied in verse 27's 'no refuge except in Him' and verse 28's heedlessness contrast.

18:32.notes: 13 labels — over ceiling. Trim candidates: day-of-judgment (the man merely denies the Hour; not a full scene). Keeping all as each is independently triggered.

18:45.notes: Verse 45: parable of worldly life as water from sky → natural-signs; 'Allah has absolute power over everything' → power. Verses 47–49: the Day when mountains are set in motion, earth emerges, all gathered → day-of-judgment + resurrection. The book placed, sinners fearful → reckoning. 'Your Lord does not wrong anyone' → justice. Sinners/disbelievers featured → disbelievers.

18:50.notes: Verse 50: Angels commanded to bow to Adam → adam + angels. Iblis refused (was of jinn) → iblis + jinn. Warning against taking Iblis as lord → shirk. 'We did not call them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. Verse 52: Day when false gods called → day-of-judgment. Verse 53: sinners see Fire → hell + disbelievers.

18:54.notes: Verse 54: 'We have elaborated in this Quran for the people' → the-quran + mankind. People's refusal to believe despite guidance → disbelievers + guidance. Verse 56: messengers sent as deliverers of good news and warners → prophethood-general. Disbelievers argue with false argument against truth and take revelations as a joke → denial-of-revelation. Verse 58: 'Your Lord is the Forgiver, Possessor of Mercy' → mercy. Verse 59: destroyed towns for injustice → punishment-of-past-nations.

18:60.notes: Moses and his servant journey to the junction of two rivers → moses. The mysterious servant given 'mercy from Us, and knowledge from Our Own' → mercy + knowledge. Moses asks to be taught 'guidance' and the servant warns he will not be able to endure (patience theme explicitly named: 'you will not be able to endure/sabar') → patience (the word sabr/patience is explicitly used multiple times). The miraculous fish finding its way to the river → miracles. Moses's request for knowledge/guidance → dua-knowledge-wisdom? Moses says 'may I follow you so that you may teach me some of the guidance' — this is a request for knowledge but not a formal du'a (no 'Rabbi…' formula); not tagging dua-knowledge-wisdom.

18:71.notes: Moses and the servant: the boat holed, the boy killed, the wall repaired → moses (named throughout). The servant's explanations reveal divine wisdom behind each act → wisdom + knowledge (God's knowledge of what is hidden, the servant taught from God). The wall belonging to two orphaned boys → orphan-care. 'As a mercy from your Lord' (verse 82) → mercy. 'I did not do it of my own accord' — the divine decree behind actions → divine-decree.

18:83.notes: Verse 83: 'Qul sa-atlu' → qul-statements. Dhul-Qarnayn narrative begins → dhul-qarnayn. 'We established him on earth and gave him all kinds of means' → sovereignty + power. He reaches the setting sun and finds a people; God gives him authority to punish or be kind → justice. The wrongdoer 'will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him' → day-of-judgment. 'We had full knowledge of what he had' → knowledge.

18:92.notes: Dhul-Qarnayn reaches the two barriers; Gog and Magog spreading corruption → dhul-qarnayn + corruption-on-earth (explicitly: 'spreading chaos in the land'). He builds the dam with God's empowerment → power. His statement 'What my Lord has empowered me with is better' → trust-in-god (explicit tawakkul in God's provision). Gog and Magog (Yajuj and Majuj) are a sign of the Hour in Islamic tradition, but the section here is narrative not eschatological warning — not tagging signs-of-the-hour at this point as the eschatological framing comes in the next section.

18:98.notes: Verse 98: 'This is a mercy from my Lord' → mercy; 'the promise of my Lord is always true' → day-of-judgment (promise of the Hour). Verse 99: Trumpet blown, all gathered → resurrection + signs-of-the-hour (the barrier breaking, surging of peoples as sign). Verse 100: Jahannam presented to disbelievers → hell + disbelievers. Dhul-Qarnayn's final words close his narrative → dhul-qarnayn.

18:103.notes: Verse 103: 'Qul hal nunabbiukum' → qul-statements. The greatest losers whose works are misguided → disbelievers. They 'rejected the communications of their Lord' and 'took My revelations and My messengers in mockery' → mockery. 'We will consider them of no weight on the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment + reckoning. Hell as their requital → hell. Believers who do righteous deeds get Gardens of Paradise → believers + paradise.

18:109.notes: Verse 109: 'Qul law kana al-bahru midadan' → qul-statements. The inexhaustibility of the words of the Lord → the-quran (the Quran/God's words as subject). God's infinite knowledge and speech → knowledge.

18:110.notes: Verse 110: 'Qul innama ana basharun mithlukum' → qul-statements. The Prophet describes himself as a human receiving revelation → muhammad (substantive about his role/nature as prophet) + prophethood-general. 'Your god is One God' → tawhid. 'Never associate anyone with the service of his Lord' → shirk (warning against). 'Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him work righteousness' → day-of-judgment (meeting the Lord) + righteous-conduct (explicit instruction to work righteous deeds).

20:1.notes: Section opens with the disjoined letters Tā-Hā. Verse 2 addresses the Quran's purpose; verse 4 names the Creator of earth and heavens; verse 5 'Most Merciful on the Throne'; verse 7 God's knowledge of the secret; verse 8 the explicit tawhid formula and Beautiful Names.

20:9.notes: Moses is called at the burning bush; God declares 'I am Allah, there is no god but I' (tawhid); commands prayer 'for My remembrance'; mentions the coming Hour and warns against those who deny it.

20:17.notes: The staff miracle and white hand miracle are shown to Moses. Moses utters the full supplication asking for ease, loosening of tongue, and appointing Aaron — this is the du'a for eloquence/knowledge (dua-knowledge-wisdom per 20:25–28) as well as for assistance. Verses 33–34 explicitly name glorification and remembrance of God.

20:36.notes: God recounts His prior favour to Moses: the basket in the river, his mother, his sister, his killing of a man, his years in Madyan — all framed as divine providence and decree. Pharaoh named as destination. Verse 42 commands not to neglect God's remembrance.

20:45.notes: Moses and Aaron utter 'Rabbanā' — a supplication expressing fear of Pharaoh (dua-distress). God responds 'I am with you, I hear and I see' (nearness-and-response, knowledge). They are told to deliver the message about the Children of Israel and warn of punishment for disbelief.

20:49.notes: Moses answers Pharaoh's question about God by describing Him as the Creator who guides all things (creation, guidance). Verses 53–54 detail rain, plants, paths — natural signs and provision. Verse 55 'from it We created you, return you, and bring you out again' = human-creation + resurrection.

20:56.notes: Pharaoh denies all of Moses's signs, accuses him of sorcery, and sets the stage for the contest. The denial of miracles as magic = denial-of-revelation + sorcery.

20:60.notes: Pharaoh gathers his plan and his magicians; the contest takes place. Moses's staff swallows their ropes and sticks. God reassures Moses. Pharaoh's scheming = plotting; the magic contest = sorcery + miracles.

20:70.notes: The magicians fall prostrate and believe — repentance. Their uttered statement 'We have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive us our sins' = dua-forgiveness. Pharaoh threatens them with torture (anger-and-violence). Verses 74–76 (in this section boundary per breaks at 70 and 74) — actually break is at 74, so verses 74–76 are in the next section. This section ends at verse 73. The magicians' faith and Pharaoh's threats are the main content.

20:74.notes: Short section contrasting the fate of those who come to God guilty (hell) versus the believer who has done righteous deeds (paradise, highest ranks). Direct eschatological contrast.

20:77.notes: God commands Moses to lead the Israelites by night; the sea is parted (miracles). Pharaoh pursues and is drowned. His misleading of his people noted. This is the Exodus climax.

20:80.notes: Direct address to Children of Israel recalling their deliverance from Pharaoh, the manna and quails (provision), the promise by the Mount (covenant). God warns against excess and promises forgiveness to the repentant (mercy, repentance).

20:83.notes: Moses rushes ahead to God; his people are led astray by the Samarian who made the golden calf — explicit idol worship (shirk). Aaron warned them but they refused. Moses returns angry. The Samarian (unnamed collective figure) is the agent of shirk. Iblis not directly named but this is the paradigmatic shirk episode; confidence high without iblis tag since iblis is not mentioned.

20:92.notes: Moses confronts Aaron; Aaron explains his reluctance to cause division among Bani Israel. Moses interrogates the Samarian and pronounces his punishment. The calf is destroyed. Verse 98 asserts the tawhid declaration 'your god is Allah… He comprehends everything in knowledge' — tawhid + knowledge.

20:99.notes: God tells the Prophet these are narrations from the past and a Reminder has been given (the-quran). Those who turn away will bear a burden on Day of Resurrection. The Trumpet is blown and sinners gathered — day-of-judgment, resurrection, reckoning.

20:105.notes: Verse 105 begins with 'they ask you… Say' = qul-statements. The mountains crumbled on that Day = signs-of-the-hour. Verse 109 on intercession only for those the Merciful permits = intercession + mercy. Verse 110 God's all-encompassing knowledge. Verse 111 humility of faces before the Living, the Eternal; injustice will despair = justice. Verse 113 'We revealed it an Arabic Quran' = the-quran.

20:114.notes: Verse 114 'Exalted is Allah, the True King' (sovereignty) and the uttered du'a 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge' (dua-knowledge-wisdom). Verses 115–122 recount Adam's covenant and forgetfulness, the angels' prostration, Iblis's refusal, Satan's whispering, Adam's eating and disobedience — Adam narrative. Verse 122 God pardoned and guided Adam (repentance, guidance, divine-decree implicit in the covenant). Paradise mentioned as the Garden from which Adam was expelled.

20:123.notes: God tells Adam and Satan to descend — the expulsion from the Garden. God's promise: whoever follows guidance will not go astray. Whoever turns from the Reminder will have a confined life and be raised blind on the Day of Resurrection (day-of-judgment). Verse 127 warns of the Hereafter's punishment. Verse 128 references destroyed past generations (punishment-of-past-nations).

20:129.notes: Addressed directly to the Prophet ('your Lord', 'your people') = muhammad. Verse 130 commands patience (sabr explicitly in 'bear patiently') and glorification/praise before sunrise and sunset (praise + prayer times). Verse 131 warns against coveting worldly provision; God's provision is better. Verse 132 commands family to pray and persist (prayer); 'the good ending is for taqwa' explicitly names taqwa.

20:133.notes: Disbelievers demand a miracle; the Quran points to miracles in former scriptures (previous-scriptures). Verse 134 — God's justice in sending a messenger before punishment so they cannot complain (justice, prophethood-general).

20:135.notes: Single verse. Opens with 'Say' (qul-statements). Commands waiting — those on the straight path and those rightly-guided will become clear (guidance). Brief closing section.

21:1.notes: Verse 4 has 'My Lord knows what is said in the heaven and the earth; He is the Hearer, the Knower' — tagging knowledge. Verse 7 references prophethood as a category. Verse 6 references destroyed towns as warning. Denial accusations in v3 and v5 (sorcery, jumble of dreams, poet) trigger denial-of-revelation. The-quran is borderline here since the Book isn't named explicitly, but the fresh reminder and the accusations about the Prophet's revelation are the subject.

21:10.notes: Verse 10 explicitly refers to the revealed Book. Verses 11–15 depict the destruction of guilty towns as warning — punishment-of-past-nations.

21:16.notes: Verses 16–17 assert the creation was purposeful (not for amusement) — creation-of-heavens-earth and sovereignty. Verse 19 states all in heavens and earth belong to Him — sovereignty and tawhid. Verses 19–20 describe angels praising night and day — angels and praise (subḥān/tasbīḥ uttered by angels).

21:21.notes: Verse 22 contains 'Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne' — praise uttered. Verse 24 contains qul ('Say, bring your proof'). Verse 25 asserts tawhid as the universal prophetic message. Verses 26–28 refute the claim of God taking a son and describe angels' obedience and intercession limits. Verse 28 mentions intercession. Verse 29 warns of Hell for anyone claiming to be a god.

21:30.notes: Verse 30 references the heavens and earth being torn apart and water as source of life — creation-of-heavens-earth and natural-signs. Verse 33 mentions creation of night, day, sun and moon — cosmic-bodies. Verses 34–35 address death and mortality of all souls — death-and-dying. Human-creation tagged because of the water-as-origin-of-all-life motif and the reference to human mortality. Verse 36 describes disbelievers mocking the Prophet — mockery.

21:37.notes: Verse 37 references the human being created of haste — human-creation. Verses 38–40 describe disbelievers asking when the promise comes and the fire overtaking them — day-of-judgment and hell.

21:41.notes: Verse 41 references mockery of prior messengers — mockery and prophethood-general and punishment-of-past-nations. Verses 42 and 45 contain qul commands. Verse 47 describes the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection — reckoning, justice, and day-of-judgment.

21:48.notes: Verses 48–49 give Moses and Aaron the Criterion (Furqan — the Torah as prior scripture) as illumination and reminder for the righteous who fear their Lord — previous-scriptures and taqwa (the muttaqun/those who fear are explicitly named as the subject). Verse 50 refers to this Qur'an as a blessed message — the-quran. Believers tagged for the implied addressees described as the God-fearing at the close.

21:51.notes: Long narrative section covering Abraham's confrontation with idol-worshippers, breaking the idols, and the miraculous fire. Shirk addressed via idol worship throughout. Tawhid asserted by Abraham in v56. Creation-of-heavens-earth referenced in v56 ('Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them'). Miracles — the fire made cool by divine command in v69. Plotting — v57 and v70 reference plans against Abraham.

21:71.notes: Abraham and Lot saved and delivered — abraham and lot. Isaac and Jacob granted as gift — isaac and jacob. Verse 73 explicitly mentions prayer (salah) and charity (zakat) being revealed to them — prayer and zakat-and-charity. Verse 75 references admission into mercy — mercy. Lot's people described as wicked — punishment-of-past-nations. Prophethood-general for the leaders guiding by divine command.

21:76.notes: Noah called out and was answered — nearness-and-response. His people drowned for rejecting signs — punishment-of-past-nations and denial-of-revelation. God's mercy invoked in saving Noah.

21:78.notes: David and Solomon's judgment narrative — david and solomon. Verse 79 mentions divine wisdom and knowledge given to both. Mountains and birds praising with David — praise (tasbīḥ) and natural-signs. Solomon's control over wind — miracles. Verse 81 references wind blowing at his command. Devils (jinn/shayateen) diving for Solomon — jinn. Verse 80 references teaching David shield-making as a divine gift.

21:83.notes: 17 labels — over the 12 ceiling. This is a dense multi-prophet section. Trim candidates: angels (only implied via the spirit breathed into Mary, not explicitly named as angels), miracles (Mary and Jesus as a sign is the explicit wording but miracles label applies; borderline). All prophets named explicitly: job, ishmael (v85), idris (v85 as Enoch), dhul-kifl (v85 as Ezekiel), jonah (v87), zechariah (v89), john (v90), mary (v91), jesus (v91 as 'her son'). Job's du'a in v83 is uttered in distress — dua-distress. Jonah's tasbīḥ in v87 is an uttered supplication in distress — also dua-distress. Zechariah's du'a in v89 asks for offspring/heir — dua-family-offspring. Mercy named multiple times (v83, v84, v86). Patience explicitly named in v85 ('each was one of the steadfast'). Nearness-and-response: God answers Job, Jonah, Zechariah repeatedly. Mary and Jesus as sign — miracles.

21:92.notes: Verse 92 addresses humanity as one community — mankind and tawhid. Verse 93 references factions/return to God — day-of-judgment. Verse 94 mentions righteous deeds and believers explicitly — righteous-conduct and believers. Verse 96 mentions Gog and Magog let loose — signs-of-the-hour. Verses 97–100 describe the Day's horror for disbelievers and Hell as fuel — day-of-judgment, hell, disbelievers, shirk. Reckoning implied in the accounting/return theme.

21:101.notes: Verses 101–102 describe the righteous kept away from Hell and in paradise. Verse 103 mentions angels receiving the believers on the Day. Verse 104 references the folding of the heaven like a scroll and the repetition of creation — creation-of-heavens-earth and day-of-judgment.

21:105.notes: Verse 105 references the Psalms (Zabur) and the Reminder (prior scripture) — previous-scriptures. Verse 107 addresses the Prophet directly as mercy to mankind — muhammad and mercy and mankind. Verse 108 contains qul — qul-statements. Tawhid asserted in v108 ('your God is One God'). Knowledge — v110 ('He knows what is said openly and what you conceal'). Prophethood-general for the sending-of-messenger motif.

21:112.notes: Single verse. An uttered du'a: 'My Lord, judge with justice' — dua-distress (calling on God under pressure from opponents). Justice explicitly invoked ('judge with justice'). Mercy named ('Our Lord is the Gracious/Most Merciful'). The closing 'Whose help is sought' reinforces nearness-and-response but the du'a framing is primary.

22:1.notes: Opens with 'O people' (yā ayyuhā an-nās) → mankind. Taqwa explicitly commanded ('be conscious of your Lord'). The quaking of the Hour and its terrors → signs-of-the-hour and day-of-judgment. The defiant devil (Iblis figure) who misleads → iblis. Those who follow him are led to the Blaze → hell. 'It was decreed for him' → divine-decree.

22:5.notes: Opens with 'O people' addressing doubt about the Resurrection → mankind, resurrection. Stages of human creation from dust/drop/clot/lump → human-creation. Divine will in settling in the womb → divine-decree. Rain reviving the earth as analogy for resurrection → natural-signs. 'He is Capable of everything' → power.

22:7.notes: 'The Hour is coming—no doubt' and 'Allah will resurrect those in the graves' → resurrection. Disbelievers who argue without knowledge → disbelievers. Punishment of burning on Day of Resurrection → hell. 'Allah is not unjust to the servants' → justice. 'Among the people' (min an-nās) → mankind (generic address though not the full formula; borderline but tagged generously).

22:11.notes: Those who worship on the edge and turn back → disbelievers. Invoking what neither harms nor benefits, associating false objects of worship → shirk. Gardens with rivers for believers → paradise. 'Allah guides whomever He wills' → guidance. 'Thus We revealed it as clarifying signs' → the-quran.

22:17.notes: Lists believers, Jews, Sabeans, Christians, Zoroastrians, polytheists being judged → people-of-the-book, sabeans, polytheists, believers, day-of-judgment. 'Allah is witness to all things' → knowledge. Sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, animals prostrating → cosmic-bodies, natural-signs. 'Allah does whatever He wills' → sovereignty. Garments of fire and scalding water for disbelievers → hell. Gardens with rivers and silk for believers → paradise. Notes: 11 labels, within ceiling.

22:25.notes: Disbelievers blocking the Sacred Mosque → disbelievers, sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. Mosque designated for 'all mankind' → mankind. Abraham shown the location of the House → abraham. Announcing pilgrimage, circling, rites of cleansing, fulfilling vows → hajj-and-pilgrimage, oaths-and-vows, ritual-purity. Purifying the House for those who pray → prayer. Feeding the poor from sacrificial animals → food-and-dietary, zakat-and-charity.

22:30.notes: Veneration of God's sanctities, avoiding idols, the Ancient House → hajj-and-pilgrimage. 'Stay away from the abomination of idols' → shirk. 'Without associating anything with Him' → tawhid. Livestock permitted with exceptions → food-and-dietary. 'Whoever venerates sacraments—it is from the piety of the hearts' → taqwa (explicitly named: 'min taqwā al-qulūb'). For every nation a rite, 'Your God is One God, submit to Him' → tawhid. Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, who endure, pray, and spend → remembrance, patience, prayer, zakat-and-charity.

22:36.notes: The animal offerings (budun) as emblems of Allah, pronouncing Allah's name upon them → hajj-and-pilgrimage, remembrance. Eating from them and feeding the poor/beggar → food-and-dietary, zakat-and-charity. 'That you may be thankful' — gratitude mentioned as purpose but not the section's explicit subject; not tagged per rule 5.

22:37.notes: Flesh and blood don't reach Allah; taqwa does → taqwa (explicitly named). Allah glorified for guidance → hajj-and-pilgrimage. Allah defends believers → believers. Permission to fight given to those wronged → war-and-treaties. Those evicted from homes → migration. 'Allah is Strong and Mighty' → power. Those empowered establish prayer and give zakat → prayer, zakat-and-charity.

22:42.notes: People of Noah, Aad, Thamud, Abraham, Lot, Midian, and Moses all named → noah, ad, thamud, abraham, lot, madyan, moses. All denied their prophets → prophethood-general, disbelievers. Destroyed towns lying in ruins → punishment-of-past-nations, previous-creations-destroyed. 11 labels, within ceiling.

22:47.notes: Disbelievers asking to hasten punishment → disbelievers. 'Allah never breaks His promise' → divine-decree. 'A day with your Lord is like a thousand years' → day-of-judgment. Towns reprieved then seized → punishment-of-past-nations.

22:49.notes: 14 labels — over the 12-label ceiling. 'Say, O people, I am only a plain warner' → qul-statements, mankind, prophethood-general. Believers with forgiveness and provision → believers, paradise. Those who strive against revelations → hell, disbelievers. Satan interfering with prophets' wishes, Allah nullifying → iblis, the-quran. 'Allah is Omniscient and Wise' → knowledge, wisdom. Trial for those with diseased hearts → disbelievers. Allah guides believers to straight path → guidance. Sovereignty on that Day belongs to Allah → sovereignty, day-of-judgment. Trim candidates: sovereignty (subsumed by day-of-judgment context), wisdom (closing formula only).

22:58.notes: Those who emigrate in Allah's cause and are killed or die → migration. Allah provides them fine provisions and admits them → paradise, provision (but provision is a divine-attribute label; keeping believers). 'Allah is the Best of Providers' → provision... wait, 'provision' is a divine-attributes label — tagging it. 'Allah is Knowing and Clement' → knowledge, mercy. Retaliating proportionally; Allah assists the wronged → justice. 'Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving' → mercy. Allah merges night into day → cosmic-bodies. 'Allah is Hearing and Seeing' → knowledge. 'Allah is the Reality; what they invoke is vanity' → tawhid. 'Allah is the Sublime, the Grand' → power (sovereignty cluster). Revised label set below.

22:63.notes: Rain from the sky greening the earth → natural-signs. 'Allah is Kind and Aware' → knowledge. 'To Him belongs everything in the heavens and earth; Allah is the Rich, the Praised' → sovereignty. Ships sailing by His command, holding up the sky → creation-of-heavens-earth (sovereignty of cosmos), provision. 'Allah is Gracious towards the people, Most Merciful' → mercy. 'He gives you life, then makes you die, then revives you' → death-and-dying.

22:67.notes: For every nation appointed acts of devotion → prophethood-general. 'Do not let them dispute with you' — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad. 'You are upon a straight guidance' → guidance. 'Say, Allah is fully aware of what you do' → knowledge. 'Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment. 'Allah knows everything in heavens and earth; it is in a Book' → knowledge, divine-decree. Note: verse 68 contains 'qul' (Say) → qul-statements.

22:71.notes: Worshipping besides Allah without knowledge → shirk, disbelievers. Verses recited and disbelievers reacting with disgust → the-quran. 'The Fire! Allah has promised it to those who disbelieve' → hell. 'O people! A parable…' → mankind. 'Say, shall I inform you…' → qul-statements. Idols cannot create a fly → tawhid. 'Allah is Strong and Powerful' → power.

22:75.notes: Allah chooses messengers from angels and people → angels, prophethood-general. 'Allah is Hearing and Seeing; knows what is before them and behind them' → knowledge. 'O you who believe! Kneel, and prostrate, and worship your Lord, and do good deeds' → believers, prayer. Direct address 'yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū' → believers.

22:78.notes: Address to believers to strive for Allah → believers, war-and-treaties. 'The faith of your father Abraham, it is he who named you Muslims' → abraham. The Messenger as witness → prophethood-general, muhammad (the Messenger's witnessing role is substantive reference). 'Pray regularly and give regular charity' → prayer, zakat-and-charity. 'Cleave to Allah. He is your Protector' → trust-in-god.

23:1.notes: The section opens with 'the believers' as its explicit subject and enumerates their qualities: humility in prayer, avoiding nonsense, paying zakat, guarding chastity (marriage-and-family context), faithfulness to trusts and pledges (covenant), and maintaining prayers. Paradise is explicitly promised. Taqwa is implicit in 'khashi'un' but humility in prayer and the overall framing of the muttaqun is close enough; however 'righteous-conduct' is triggered by the explicit enumeration of ethical duties. 'covenant' is triggered by 'trusts and pledges' named explicitly.

23:12.notes: 'Tabaaraka Allahu ahsan al-khaliqeen' utters praise — tag praise. The stages of embryological creation are the section's subject — human-creation. Death is named explicitly in v15. Resurrection on the Day of Resurrection in v16. 'Mankind' fits as the section addresses humanity universally about their own origin.

23:17.notes: Seven pathways above (heavens) — creation-of-heavens-earth. Rain sent down, gardens, palms, vines, livestock, ships — natural-signs and provision. 'We are Able to take it away' — power. Creation as divine act throughout.

23:23.notes: Noah's narrative: sent to his people, their rejection, the ark, the flood. Tawhid: 'worship Allah, you have no deity other than Him.' Prophethood-general: the sending of a messenger. Disbelievers: the rejecting notables. Punishment-of-past-nations: the drowning of Noah's people. Dua-distress: 'My Lord, help me, for they have rejected me' (v26) — uttered supplication in distress. Praise uttered in v28: 'al-hamdu lillahi alladhi najjana' — explicit hamd. Dua-protection: v29 'My Lord, land me with a blessed landing' is a supplication for safe landing/protection. Divine-decree: 'when Our decree comes to pass' (v27). Miracles: the ark built by divine inspiration and the flood as miraculous sign. Note: dua-distress and dua-protection both apply as two distinct uttered supplications appear.

23:31.notes: Generic pattern: a new generation, a messenger sent, rejection, destruction by the Blast. Prophethood-general: 'We sent among them a messenger.' Disbelievers: the rejecting notables. Denial-of-revelation: they call him a liar making up lies about Allah. Punishment-of-past-nations: 'the Blast struck them, We turned them into scum.' Resurrection: denied explicitly by the people ('we are not resurrected' v37) — the section makes resurrection its explicit dispute, so the label applies. Divine-decree: 'No nation can advance its time, nor can they postpone it' (v43). Disbelief: 'away with a people who do not believe' (v44). The dua in v39 ('My Lord, help me') mirrors Noah's — tag dua-distress.

23:45.notes: Moses and Aaron sent with signs to Pharaoh — moses, aaron, pharaoh, miracles. Pharaoh and his nobles turned arrogant — arrogance explicitly named ('istakbaru'). They were destroyed — punishment-of-past-nations. Moses given the Scripture — previous-scriptures. Mary's son and his mother made a sign — mary, jesus. Prophethood-general: the sending of messengers with signs. Guidance: 'that they may be guided' (v49).

23:51.notes: Address to messengers to eat of good things (food-and-dietary). 'This nation is one nation' and 'fear Me' — tawhid and taqwa explicitly invoked ('ittaqoon'). Sectarian division condemned. Disbelievers misled by wealth and children. Believers described: those in awe of their Lord, who believe in His verses, who associate no partners (tawhid), who give charity with fearful hearts. Reckoning: 'with Us is a record that tells the truth, they will not be wronged.' Arrogance: v67 'arrogant towards it.' Denial-of-revelation: 'My Verses were recited to you but you turned back' (v66), 'arrogant towards it, talked nonsense about it, disregarded it' (v67). Punishment context: seized with torment (v64). Note: 12 labels exactly at ceiling.

23:68.notes: Questions about why they don't ponder 'the Word' — the-quran. Denial: they call the messenger possessed, deny the truth — denial-of-revelation. Prophethood-general: 'their messenger.' 'He brought them the truth' — guidance. Provider: 'the revenue from your Lord is better, and He is the Best of providers' — provision (named divine attribute). Mercy: 'if We had mercy on them' (v75) — mercy named. Disbelievers and disbelief as the section's subjects throughout. 'You are inviting them to a straight path' — guidance.

23:78.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: cosmic-bodies (passing mention of night/day), human-creation (could be subsumed under creation in this context).

23:99.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: paradise (only indirectly implied), dua-distress (the dying man's plea could be classified simply as regret rather than canonical distress supplication).

23:116.notes: Exalted is Allah the Ruler, the Real, no god except He, Lord of the Noble Throne — tawhid and sovereignty. Whoever invokes another god — shirk. His reckoning rests with his Lord — reckoning. Disbelievers will not succeed — disbelievers.

23:118.notes: Uttered supplication: 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy' — dua-forgiveness. 'You are the Best of the merciful' — mercy (divine attribute named). 'Say:' (qul) command — qul-statements.

24:1.notes: Section covers the hudud for zina and for false accusation of chaste women (qadhf), plus the closing 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' earning mercy. Repentance is explicitly named in v5 ('except those who repent afterwards'). Slander-and-backbiting applies to the qadhf ruling (false accusation).

24:6.notes: The li'an procedure — mutual oath-swearing between spouses when there are no witnesses to an adultery accusation. Closing divine-wrath formula in v9 invokes God's justice implicitly; 'knowledge' not explicitly named here so not tagged as divine attribute. Section is purely procedural law on spousal accusation.

24:10.notes: The Ifk (slander) incident passage. Covers believers addressed directly (v21 yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū), the slander spread among believers, God's mercy and grace repeatedly invoked (vv10,14,20,21), closing 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' (v18) and 'Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing' (v21) — knowledge+wisdom. Iblis is explicitly named ('do not follow Satan's footsteps', v21). Repentance is implicit in the call to not return to it, but 'tawbah' is not the explicit subject — however the instruction 'repent to Allah' is absent in this block; held back. Corruption/immorality spreading is the subject of v19 but 'corruption-on-earth' requires fasad as explicit subject — this is closer to slander. Section is large (12 verses); labels justified individually.

24:22.notes: Single verse urging the affluent not to withhold from relatives, the needy, and emigrants (muhajirin → migration). Exhortation to pardon and overlook. Closing 'Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful' → mercy. The call to pardon invokes the hope that Allah will pardon the giver → repentance theme is surface-level but the verse explicitly names 'pardon' and connects it to God's forgiveness, which is the repentance-mercy link.

24:23.notes: Vv23-25: curse on those who slander believing women + Day of Judgment reckoning when limbs testify. V26: forgiveness and generous provision for the pure. 'Reckoning' triggered by v25 (Allah will pay their account in full). 'Mercy' from 'forgiveness for them' in v26. 'Provision' from 'generous provision' in v26.

24:27.notes: Section opens with yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū → believers. Rules on seeking permission before entering homes (vv27-29), lowering the gaze and guarding modesty for men and women (vv30-31). 'Tell' (qul-like imperative) in v30 'Say to the believing men' and v31 'Say to the believing women' — these are qul-statements (directive commands to declare/instruct). Closing 'repent to Allah, all of you believers' in v31 is an explicit repentance command → repentance. 'Allah knows what you do' repeatedly → knowledge. Righteous-conduct is explicitly structured as instruction in conduct (lowering gaze, guarding modesty). Marriage-and-family from the detailed family-member exceptions in v31.

24:32.notes: V32: command to wed the unmarried and righteous servants — marriage-and-family. God will enrich the poor from His bounty → provision. 'Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing' → knowledge. V33: those who seek mukatabah (manumission contract) — manumission-and-captives. Prohibition of compelling servant-girls into prostitution; closing 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy.

24:34.notes: Single verse: 'We have sent down clarifying revelations' → the-quran. 'Examples of those who passed on before you' → punishment-of-past-nations (past nations as warning examples). 'Advice for the righteous (muttaqin)' — taqwa is explicitly named as the addressee class.

24:35.notes: V35: the Ayat al-Nur (Light Verse) — 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth… Allah guides to His light whomever He wills… Allah is cognizant of everything' → guidance, knowledge. 'Subḥān' formula not present but 'He is glorified therein morning and evening' (v36) → praise (uttered glorification in those houses). V37: men not distracted from dhikr → remembrance; nor from salah → prayer; nor from zakat → zakat-and-charity. They fear the Day → day-of-judgment. V38: 'Allah provides without reckoning' → provision. 'Allah thus cites the parables for the people' (v35) → mankind. Notes: 9 labels, within ceiling.

24:39.notes: Vv39-40: two parables for disbelievers' deeds — mirage in a desert and darkness in a deep ocean. 'Allah settles his account' → reckoning. 'He to whom Allah has not granted a light has no light' → guidance (its absence). Natural imagery (desert, ocean, waves, fog) → natural-signs. Disbelievers as subject → disbelievers + disbelief.

24:41.notes: V41: everything in heavens and earth glorifies Allah, birds in formation → praise (glorification uttered by creation), natural-signs (birds). V42: 'to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. V43: rain, hail, lightning — natural phenomena as signs → natural-signs. Night and day alternation (v44) → cosmic-bodies. V45: 'Allah created every living creature from water… Allah is Capable of everything' → creation, power. 'Allah is Knowing' (v41) → knowledge.

24:46.notes: V46: 'We sent down enlightening revelations… Allah guides whomever He wills' → the-quran, guidance. Vv47-50: description of those who claim belief then turn away — characteristic of hypocrites → hypocrites. Vv51-52: true believers say 'we hear and obey'; those who fear Allah and are conscious of Him (taqwa explicit in v52) → believers, taqwa. V53: 'Say, Do not swear' → qul-statements. V54: 'Say, Obey Allah and obey the Messenger… it is only incumbent on the Messenger to deliver the Clarifying Message' → qul-statements, prophethood-general. 'Allah is experienced with what you do' (v53) → knowledge.

24:55.notes: V55: Allah's promise to make believers successors on earth, establish their religion, replace fear with security; 'they worship Me, never associating anything with Me' → tawhid; divine promise → divine-decree. V56: 'Pray regularly and give regular charity' → prayer, zakat-and-charity. V57: disbelievers cannot escape; 'their place is the Fire' → hell, disbelievers. The promise of earthly succession speaks to God's sovereignty over kingdoms → sovereignty.

24:58.notes: Vv58-60: rules on when servants and children must seek permission before entering private spaces — three times tied to prayer times (dawn prayer, noon, evening prayer) → prayer (times referenced); marriage-and-family (household rules); manumission-and-captives (servants/those whose right hands possess). V60: older women and the relaxation of modesty rules → marriage-and-family. Closing 'Allah is Knowledgeable and Wise' (vv58,59) and 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' (v60) → knowledge, wisdom.

24:61.notes: Single verse permitting the blind, lame, and sick, and everyone else to eat from family members' homes — food-and-dietary (what is permitted in terms of eating from various homes). Family relations enumerated → marriage-and-family. Greeting upon entering homes as a command. Believers addressed implicitly. No divine attributes named in closing formula here (it ends with 'so that you may understand').

24:62.notes: V62: true believers do not leave the Prophet's assembly without permission — direct second-person address to the Prophet ('ask Allah's forgiveness for them', 'give permission to any of them you wish') → muhammad. Believers as subject → believers. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' closing → mercy. V63: warns those who oppose the Messenger's orders; 'Allah knows those who slip away' → knowledge. Muhammad is substantively the subject (his authority, his assembly, addressing him directly).

24:64.notes: Single closing verse: 'to Allah belongs everything in the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. 'He knows what you are about… Allah has full knowledge of all things' → knowledge. 'On the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did' → day-of-judgment, reckoning.

25:1.notes: Tabāraka opens the surah → praise. 'Mulk of heavens and earth, no son, no partner' → tawhid + sovereignty. 'Created everything and determined its measure' → power + creation. 'Sent down the Criterion' → the-quran + prophethood-general. Verse 3 refutes false gods → shirk + disbelievers. 'Warning to humanity' → mankind.

25:4.notes: Verses 4–9: disbelievers deny the Quran as fabrication → denial-of-revelation + disbelievers. Verse 6 'Say, it was revealed by He who knows the Secret' → qul-statements + knowledge. Closing 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verses 10–14: hell described in detail → hell. Verse 15 'Say, is this better or the Garden' → qul-statements + paradise. Verses 17–19: gathering of false gods on Day of Judgment → day-of-judgment + shirk. Direct address to the Prophet ('provide you with better', 'invent examples for you') → muhammad. 11 labels — within ceiling.

25:20.notes: Verse 20: prior messengers ate food → prophethood-general; 'will you be patient?' — patience is the explicit subject of the question → patience. Verse 21: 'they have grown arrogant' — word 'arrogant' explicit → arrogance. Angels mentioned twice (vv. 21, 25) → angels. Verse 22: Day when they see angels, no good news for sinners → day-of-judgment. Verse 23: works turned to dust → reckoning. Verse 24: companions of Paradise → paradise. Verses 25–26: sky cleft, angels sent down, sovereignty of the Merciful → sovereignty. Verse 27–29: wrongdoer bites hands, blames friend, Satan as betrayer → iblis. Disbelievers as subject throughout → disbelievers. Hell implied by 'no good news for sinners' but not explicitly named; reckoning covers the deeds-scattered dust scene.

25:30.notes: Verse 30: the Messenger complains about abandonment of the Quran — direct second-person address context and the Messenger speaking → muhammad + the-quran. Verse 31: enemies assigned to every prophet → prophethood-general; 'your Lord suffices as a Guide' → guidance. Verse 32: disbelievers object to piecemeal revelation → disbelievers + denial-of-revelation + the-quran. Verse 34: those herded into Hell on their faces → hell.

25:35.notes: Verse 35: Moses and Aaron named explicitly → moses + aaron. Verse 36: people who rejected signs destroyed → punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 37: people of Noah drowned → noah + punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 38: 'Aad and Thamood' named → ad + thamud + punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 40: city 'drenched by terrible rain' — tafsir identifies this as Lot's city → lot. Hell mentioned obliquely ('painful retribution' prepared for wrongdoers, v.37) — not named directly as Jahannam; 'painful retribution' overlaps with hell. Mockery of the Prophet in v.41 → disbelievers. Prophethood as recurring theme → prophethood-general.

25:45.notes: Verses 45–46: shadow extended, sun as pointer → cosmic-bodies + natural-signs. Verse 47: night as covering, sleep, day as revival → natural-signs. Verse 48–49: winds, rain, reviving dead land, drink for animals and humans → natural-signs + provision. Verse 50: most people persist in thanklessness (kufūran) → disbelievers. Verse 51: could have sent a warner to every town → prophethood-general implicit but not the explicit subject; omitted per rule 5. Verse 52: direct address to the Prophet ('do not obey the disbelievers, strive against them with it') — 'it' refers to the Quran → muhammad + the-quran. 'Your Lord' addressing the Prophet throughout → muhammad. Creation of natural phenomena → creation + power.

25:53.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Verse 53: two seas, barrier → natural-signs. Verse 54: human created from fluid → human-creation; marriage/kinship relationships → this is about human-creation not marriage law per se. 'Your Lord is Omnipotent' → power. Verse 55: worshipping useless idols → shirk + disbelievers. Verse 56: Prophet sent as herald → prophethood-general context but addressed to Muhammad → muhammad (borderline; omitted in favour of trim). Verse 57: Say → qul-statements. Verse 58: 'put your trust in the Living' → trust-in-god; 'celebrate His praise' → praise; 'All-Informed Knower' → knowledge. Verse 59: created heavens and earth in six days, Throne → creation-of-heavens-earth + creation; 'the Most Merciful' → mercy. Verse 60: denial of the Merciful → disbelievers. Verse 61: Tabāraka, constellations, lamp (sun), moon → praise + cosmic-bodies. Verse 62: night and day alternate → natural-signs. Trim candidates (lowest priority): creation (subsumed by creation-of-heavens-earth and human-creation), prophethood-general (not the explicit focus).

25:63.notes: Verse 63: 'servants of the Merciful… walk in humility' — humility explicitly named → humility; believers described → believers. Verse 64: night prostrations and standing → prayer. Verse 65: uttered supplication 'Our Lord, avert from us the suffering of Hell' → dua-protection + hell. Verse 67: spending neither wastefully nor stingily → zakat-and-charity (charitable spending). Verse 68: no other god, no unjust killing, no adultery → shirk + anger-and-violence + righteous-conduct (explicit list of righteous conduct). Verse 69: punishment doubled on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment. Verse 70: 'except those who repent' — repentance explicitly named → repentance; 'Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. 12 labels — at ceiling.

25:72.notes: Verse 72: do not bear false witness → justice-and-witness. Verse 73: reminded of revelations of their Lord — responding to the Quran → the-quran. Verse 74: uttered supplication 'Our Lord, grant us delight in our spouses and children, and make us a good example for the righteous' → dua-family-offspring; 'for the righteous/muttaqeen' → taqwa (muttaqeen explicitly named). Verse 75: 'awarded the Chamber for their patience' — patience explicitly named as the cause of reward → patience; Paradise described → paradise. 'Greetings and peace' and humility in conduct (v.72 passing indecencies with dignity) → humility. Believers are the subject throughout → believers.

25:77.notes: Verse 77: 'Say' → qul-statements. 'What are you to my Lord without your prayers' — prayer (du'a/worship) as the subject → prayer; addressed universally → mankind. 'You have denied the truth' → disbelievers. 'The inevitable will happen' → day-of-judgment.

26:1.notes: Opens with Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm → disjoined-letters. Direct address to the Prophet about his grief → muhammad. Natural signs invoked (earth's plant-pairs). Closing formula 'Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy.

26:10.notes: Moses called by God, his fear and distress expressed as a plea ('My Lord, I fear…'), requesting Aaron; God reassures them. Aaron requested explicitly by name. Children of Israel mentioned as the goal. 'We will be with you, listening' → nearness-and-response.

26:18.notes: Dialogue between Pharaoh and Moses about Moses's upbringing and his killing of an Egyptian; Moses recounts being guided to prophethood. Children of Israel referenced as enslaved.

26:23.notes: Pharaoh challenges 'What is the Lord of the Worlds?' Moses answers with sovereignty and creation attributes. Staff and white hand miracles performed. Pharaoh accuses Moses of sorcery. Magicians summoned.

26:41.notes: Magicians' contest: Moses's staff swallows their trickery; magicians prostrate and profess faith. Pharaoh threatens crucifixion. Magicians express hope for God's forgiveness ('We are eager for our Lord to forgive us our sins') — uttered supplication → dua-forgiveness. Their conversion is repentance. Aaron named by the magicians (v.48).

26:52.notes: Night escape of Israelites; Pharaoh pursues. Splitting of the sea — Moses's staff strikes it (miracle). Moses: 'My Lord is with me, He will guide me' → guidance + nearness implied. Pharaoh and his army drowned. Children of Israel inherit their gardens. Closing 'Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy.

26:69.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: dua-family-offspring (weakest mapping; no offspring requested explicitly), guidance (implicit rather than named attribute in this section).

26:90.notes: Paradise brought near for the righteous; Hell displayed for deviators. Idolaters confess equating their idols with God (shirk). 'We have no intercessors' → intercession (negated). Soldiers of Iblis cast into Hell. Closing 'Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy. punishment-of-past-nations label not strongly triggered here — this is eschatological rather than historical punishment. Removed in favor of keeping within ceiling.

26:105.notes: Noah's people disbelieve; Noah preaches taqwa and obedience. They threaten stoning. Noah utters a du'a: 'My Lord, my people have denied me. So judge between me and them decisively, and deliver me and the believers who are with me' → dua-distress. Ark narrative; rest drowned. Closing 'Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy.

26:123.notes: Hud sent to 'Ād; preaches taqwa and obedience. Accuses them of vain monument-building and merciless violence (corruption-on-earth). They deny and are destroyed. Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:141.notes: Salih sent to Thamūd; the she-camel sign as miracle. They slay her and are punished. Corruption-on-earth triggered by v.152: 'who spread turmoil on earth, and do not reform.' Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:160.notes: Lot's people disbelieve; he condemns their approach to males and abandonment of wives (marriage-and-family). Lot utters a du'a: 'My Lord, save me and my family from what they do' → dua-distress. Lot and family saved except the old woman; others destroyed. Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:176.notes: Shuayb sent to People of the Woods (associated with Madyan). Instructions on full measure and accurate scales → trade-and-debt + justice-and-witness. Warning against corruption on earth (explicit in v.183). They deny him; destroyed by punishment of the day of gloom. Closing formula → power + mercy. knowledge: v.188 'My Lord is Well Aware of what you do' → knowledge.

26:192.notes: The Qur'an's divine origin affirmed; the Trustworthy Spirit (Gabriel/angels) brought it down on the Prophet's heart → muhammad (direct address implied in 'upon your heart'). It is foretold in prior scriptures and recognized by scholars of the Children of Israel → previous-scriptures. Disbelievers will not believe until they see punishment → denial-of-revelation. 'We are never unjust' → justice.

26:210.notes: Devils barred from bringing the Qur'an → the-quran. Direct address to the Prophet: warn relatives, lower wing to believers, trust in God → muhammad. 'Do not pray to another god' → tawhid/shirk. 'Put your trust in the Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy. 'He is the Hearer, the Aware' → knowledge. Poets and devils contrasted to affirm Qur'an's divine origin. denial-of-revelation present through the context of refuting the charge that devils revealed it.

26:225.notes: Short section critiquing poets: they roam every style and say what they don't do — a counterpoint to the Prophet's truthful message, contextualizing the accusation that he is a poet.

26:227.notes: Exception carved out for poets who believe, do good deeds, and remember God frequently — explicit naming of righteous-conduct and remembrance. Warning to wrongdoers about their overturning → day-of-judgment.

27:1.notes: Opens with Ṭā-Sīn disjoined letters → disjoined-letters. The Quran is the explicit subject of v1 and v6 → the-quran. Believers addressed as those who pray and give zakat → prayer, zakat-and-charity. Disbelievers destined for grievous punishment → disbelievers, hell, day-of-judgment. 'All-Wise, All-Knowing' closing formula → wisdom, knowledge. Guidance explicitly named in v2 → guidance (concrete trigger: the word appears).

27:7.notes: Moses's call at the burning bush; staff miracle and white hand → miracles. 'Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds' in v8 → praise (uttered formula). 'The Almighty, the Wise' → wisdom, power. 'I am Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Nine miracles to Pharaoh named → pharaoh. Prophethood theme throughout → prophethood-general.

27:13.notes: Signs come to Pharaoh's people who call them sorcery → denial-of-revelation. They rejected them out of 'wickedness and pride' — arrogance explicitly triggered ('pride' = uluww). Corruption-on-earth: 'mischief-makers' (mufsideen) named. Punishment-of-past-nations: 'see how the outcome was' is the classic warning-by-example formula.

27:15.notes: David and Solomon given knowledge → knowledge. 'Praise Allah' uttered by them → praise. Solomon addresses 'O people' (mankind). Teaching of birds' language → miracles. Solomon's du'a in v19 asking to be thankful → dua-gratitude; 'thankful' (ashkur) also explicitly names gratitude → gratitude. 10 labels, within ceiling.

'Lord of the Sublime Throne' → sovereignty. God 'brings to light the mysteries' and 'knows what you conceal' → knowledge. Jinn ('sprites') in Solomon's troops → jinn. Animals (hoopoe) as narrative vehicle → natural-signs.

27:36.notes: Solomon rejects the gift: 'What Allah has given me is better' → provision. He threatens military conquest → power. A jinn-imp offers to bring the throne miraculously → jinn, miracles. Continuation of Solomon-Sheba narrative.

27:40.notes: Throne transported in a blink 'by knowledge from the Book' → knowledge, miracles. Solomon's reflection on gratitude vs. ingratitude is the explicit subject of v40 → gratitude (concrete trigger: 'grateful/ungrateful' is the section's explicit subject). 'My Lord is Independent and Generous' → no new attribute label needed beyond knowledge already tagged. 'We destroyed them' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'We saved those who believed and were pious' → believers, taqwa. Salih's call for forgiveness invokes mercy → mercy. 'We planned a plan' — divine counter-plan → divine-decree. 10 labels, within ceiling.

27:54.notes: Lot rebukes his people for lewdness → lot, prophethood-general, corruption-on-earth. They expel Lot's family; God saves him except his wife 'whom We destined' → divine-decree. Rain of punishment → punishment-of-past-nations.

27:59.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Multiple 'qul' imperatives in v59 and v64 → qul-statements. 'Praise Allah' uttered → praise. Repeated 'Is there another god with Allah?' refrain → tawhid, shirk, polytheists. Creation of heavens/earth, rain, gardens → creation-of-heavens-earth, natural-signs. Rain as provision → provision. 'Who answers the one in need' → nearness-and-response. 'Who guides you' → guidance. 'Who originates creation and repeats it' → creation, power. Trim candidates: power (subsumed by creation), polytheists (shirk covers it well enough). Keeping all 13 and flagging.

27:65.notes: Multiple 'qul' imperatives (v65, v69, v72) → qul-statements. 'No one knows the future except Allah' → knowledge. Resurrection denied by disbelievers → resurrection, disbelievers. 'Observe the fate of the guilty' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'Do not be troubled by what they plot' → plotting (concrete trigger: makr named). 'Your Lord knows what their hearts conceal' → knowledge (already tagged). 'In a Clear Book' → divine-decree. Direct address 'do not grieve over them' to the Prophet → muhammad. 'Your Lord is gracious towards humanity' → not a standalone people-tag trigger here, but mercy could apply; held back since the section's main thrust is eschatology and knowledge.

27:76.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Quran resolves Children of Israel's disputes → the-quran, children-of-israel. 'Guidance and mercy for the believers' → guidance, mercy, believers. Day of gathering those who rejected revelations → day-of-judgment, denial-of-revelation. The earth-creature and trumpet → signs-of-the-hour. Trim candidates: signs-of-the-hour (v82's creature is a sign of the Hour but could be considered day-of-judgment); wisdom (could be subsumed by justice). Keeping all 13 and flagging.

27:86.notes: Night and day as signs → cosmic-bodies, natural-signs. Trumpet blown; mountains pass like clouds → resurrection, day-of-judgment. Mountains perfected by Allah → wisdom. 'He is fully Informed' → knowledge. Good deeds rewarded; evil faces tumbled into Fire → paradise, hell. 'Lord of this town who has sanctified it' → sacred-mosque-and-qiblah (Mecca). 'Worship the Lord of this town … to Whom everything belongs' → tawhid. 12 labels — at the ceiling.
