28:1.notes: Section opens with Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm disjoined letters. Introduces the Moses/Pharaoh narrative as revelation from the Quran. Pharaoh's corruption and oppression of Bani Israel explicitly named. God's plan to favor the oppressed is divine decree.

28:7.notes: The basket/river episode — inspiration to Moses's mother, Pharaoh's household picking up the infant, Pharaoh's wife intervening. God's promise to return Moses and make him a messenger is both divine decree and a miracle-framing. Marriage-and-family covers the mother–child and adoption-proposal dynamics.

28:14.notes: Moses reaches maturity, given wisdom and knowledge by God. He kills a man, identifies the act as Satan's doing (iblis), then utters 'Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li' — an explicit uttered supplication for forgiveness. Closing 'He is the Forgiver, the Merciful' tags mercy. Anger-and-violence covers the killing.

28:18.notes: Moses flees the city in fear after his identity as the killer is exposed. He utters 'Rabbi najjini min al-qawm al-zalimin' — an explicit du'a for protection and deliverance from oppressors. Both dua-distress and dua-protection apply as the supplication is uttered in fear of being killed.

28:22.notes: Moses travels to Midian, helps two women at the well, and arranges a marriage-and-labor contract with Shuayb's father (identified by tafsir as Shuayb or a righteous elder of Midian). The marriage contract and the term-of-service agreement are central. 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way' invokes guidance. Oaths-and-vows covers 'Allah is witness over what we say.' Moses also expresses dua-like trust but no formal uttered supplication beyond 'perhaps my Lord will guide me' — this is borderline; tagged guidance rather than dua-guidance as it is not a fully uttered supplication formula.

28:29.notes: Moses at the burning bush: God's self-revelation 'I am Allah, Lord of the Worlds' — tawhid. The staff-snake and white hand miracles granted as signs for Pharaoh. Moses asks God for help citing his fear and requests Aaron be sent — this is an uttered supplication in distress. God promises authority and triumph. Aaron explicitly named.

28:36.notes: Pharaoh and his court reject Moses's signs as fabricated magic — denial-of-revelation and sorcery accusation. Pharaoh claims to be the only god — shirk (associating himself with divinity). Moses asserts God knows best who brings guidance — knowledge attribute. Pharaoh orders Haman to build a tower to reach 'the god of Moses.'

28:39.notes: Pharaoh and his troops act with explicit arrogance (istakbara). God seizes and drowns them — punishment of past nations. They are made 'leaders calling to the Fire' — hell. Cursed in this world and despised on Resurrection Day — day-of-judgment. Moses given the Scripture after their annihilation as guidance and mercy — previous-scriptures.

28:44.notes: Direct second-person address to Muhammad ('You were not on the Western Side…') — muhammad tagged. God explains Muhammad was not a witness to Moses's commission yet recites it — establishes the Quran's miraculous knowledge. Disbelievers compare Muhammad unfavorably to Moses and reject both as 'two works of magic' — denial-of-revelation. 'Say: bring a scripture more conducive to guidance' — qul-statements. People-of-the-book implied in the comparison challenge (they previously disbelieved in Moses). Mercy for sending a warner. 10 labels — within ceiling.

28:51.notes: Those given scripture before (people-of-the-book) who believe in the Quran. Their qualities: patience ('because they persevered' — sabr explicitly named), countering evil with good (righteous-conduct — explicitly described as their practice), spending from God's provision (zakat-and-charity). They are described as believers. The Quran is the subject of their belief — the-quran.

28:56.notes: Direct address to Muhammad — 'You cannot guide whom you love' — muhammad. God guides whom He wills — guidance and knowledge attributes. Quraysh's excuse about being snatched from their land if they follow guidance; God's response mentions the Safe Sanctuary (Haram) with fruits provided — sacred-mosque-and-qiblah and provision. Past cities destroyed for ingratitude — punishment-of-past-nations. Prophethood-general: 'Your Lord never destroys without first sending a messenger.'

28:61.notes: Contrast between those given God's fine promise (paradise) and those arraigned on the Day — day-of-judgment, paradise, hell, reckoning. God calls to the polytheists about their associates — shirk. Those who misled others disown them. Repentance explicitly mentioned ('he who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds'). 'Subhan Allah wa ta'ala' — praise uttered. 'He is Allah, there is no god but He' — tawhid. 'To Him belongs all praise… His is the decision' — praise and sovereignty. 10 labels — within ceiling.

28:71.notes: Multiple 'Say:' commands — qul-statements. Night/day alternation as God's sign — cosmic-bodies. 'Out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day' — mercy. Provision: seeking bounty, fruits of the sanctuary. Day of Judgment: perpetual night/day until the Day; God calls about associates — day-of-judgment. Shirk: 'Where are My associates?' Evidence against polytheism — tawhid and shirk. Power: God alone can bring light or night.

28:76.notes: Qarun (Korah) of Moses's people — his immense treasures, his arrogance, his people warning him against exultation and corruption. 'Allah does not love the seekers of corruption' — corruption-on-earth explicitly named. His destruction by earth-caving — punishment-of-past-nations (he is among destroyed wrongdoers). Provision: God spreads and restricts bounty as He wills. Greed-and-miserliness: his hoarding and pride in wealth. Justice: outcome for the ungrateful.

28:83.notes: Paradise assigned to those who seek no superiority or corruption — paradise, taqwa ('the cautious'). Reward for good vs. evil deeds — reckoning. 'He who ordained the Quran for you' — the-quran. Direct address to Muhammad about the Scripture — muhammad. 'Say: My Lord knows best' — qul-statements. 'You did not expect the Scripture except as mercy' — mercy. 'Do not be a supporter of disbelievers' — disbelievers. 'Never be of the polytheists' — shirk. Guidance: 'who comes with guidance.' 10 labels — within ceiling.

28:88.notes: Closing verse: 'Do not invoke with Allah any other god. There is no god but He' — tawhid and shirk. 'All things perish except His presence. His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned' — sovereignty and day-of-judgment. Short single-verse section; 4 labels appropriate.

29:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Mim → disjoined-letters. The section addresses all people about the test of faith (mankind). Verse 8 commands good to parents and warns against shirk when parents press for it. 'Righteous deeds' and admission among the righteous in v7/9 triggers righteous-conduct. marriage-and-family is borderline — v8 is about parent-child conduct rather than marriage per se; keeping it because the instruction to parents is a family-conduct passage. Removed if reviewer finds it too loose. paradise implied by 'admit them among the righteous.'

29:14.notes: Noah sent to his people, the Flood, the Ark as a sign for all peoples. The Ark as 'a sign' triggers miracles.

Resurrection implicit in 'brings about the next existence' and 'to Him you will be restored'. punishment-of-past-nations not directly referenced here — removed. Day of return is eschatological → resurrection.

Prophethood and Scripture placed in his descendants. Idol worship condemned → shirk. Day of Resurrection: mutual disowning and cursing → day-of-judgment. Hell ('Your destiny is Hell') → hell. 'He is the Noble [Aziz], the Wise' → power + wisdom. miracles: Abraham saved from fire supernaturally. Trim candidates if needed: iblis (not named), day-of-judgment (could subsume into hell).

29:28.notes: Lot's narrative: his people's sexual corruption (corruption-on-earth explicitly named 'people of corruption' in v30). Lot utters 'My Lord, help me against the people of corruption' → dua-distress (uttered supplication in distress). Angels arrive to Abraham and then Lot. Abraham's intercession for Lot. Lot's wife left behind → marriage-and-family. 'We are well aware' → knowledge. Destruction of the town → punishment-of-past-nations.

29:36.notes: 15 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Shuayb to Madyan. 'Ad and Thamud named. Quaroon, Pharaoh, Hamaan — Moses came to them. Iblis embellished their deeds. Arrogance: 'they acted arrogantly in the land' (v39, explicit). Corruption-on-earth: Shuayb warns against spreading corruption (v36). Punishment of all these nations. Shirk: worship idols. 'He is the Almighty, the Wise' → wisdom + power (but power not directly stated as attribute name; 'Almighty/Aziz' → sovereignty label or power; using knowledge+wisdom for v42 closing formula 'He is the Almighty, the Wise'). Spider parable → natural-signs. Creation of heavens and earth in v44 → tawhid/creation-of-heavens-earth. Trim candidates: natural-signs (spider is a simile not a natural-sign per se), tawhid (v44 is creation-focused rather than oneness-assertion), iblis (named but brief).

29:45.notes: Verse 45: command to recite Scripture and establish prayer; 'remembrance of Allah is greater' → remembrance explicitly named. Verse 46: address to People of the Book → people-of-the-book + previous-scriptures + tawhid ('our God and your God is One'). Verse 47: the revealed Scripture → the-quran. 'Allah knows what you do' → knowledge. Addressed to the Prophet directly ('you did not read... your right hand' in v48 is next section, but here 'Recite what is revealed to you' is direct address → muhammad).

29:48.notes: Sections 48–52: Prophet's illiteracy as proof (muhammad). The Quran as clear signs in the hearts of the learned → the-quran. Two 'Say' (qul) commands in v50 and v52 → qul-statements. 'Miracles are only with Allah' → prophethood-general. Denial that Quran is genuine → denial-of-revelation. 'He knows everything in heavens and earth' → knowledge. 'In that is mercy' (v51) → mercy. Disbelievers named → disbelievers.

29:53.notes: They demand the punishment be hastened. 'A specified time' → divine-decree. Hell will engulf disbelievers → hell. Day when punishment envelops them → day-of-judgment. The threatened punishment also echoes past-nations pattern → punishment-of-past-nations (borderline; the section is about future punishment, not explicitly past nations — removing punishment-of-past-nations for cleaner tagging).

29:56.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. 'O My servants who have believed, My earth is vast' → believers + migration (the call to migrate for worship). 'Every soul will taste death' → death-and-dying. Paradise with rivers → paradise. 'Those who endure patiently' → patience (explicitly named). 'In their Lord they trust' → trust-in-god (explicitly named). Provision from Allah for all creatures → provision. 'He is the Hearer, the Knowledgeable' → knowledge. Sun and moon regulated (v61) → cosmic-bodies. Rain reviving dead earth (v63) → natural-signs. Creation of heavens and earth (v61) → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Say, Praise be to Allah' (v63) → qul-statements + praise (uttered hamd). Trim candidates: creation-of-heavens-earth (only mentioned in passing rhetorical question), cosmic-bodies (similarly in rhetorical question — but both are explicit so keeping).

29:64.notes: This life as diversion vs. the Hereafter as true life → day-of-judgment. They pray to Allah sincerely at sea then commit shirk on land → shirk + tawhid. Secure Sanctuary (Haram) → sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. Hell for the disbelievers (v68) → hell. Fabricating lies about Allah and rejecting truth → denial-of-revelation. Disbelievers named → disbelievers.

29:69.notes: Those who strive for Allah will be guided → guidance (God as source of guidance, explicitly promised here). 'Doers of good' → righteous-conduct (the term is explicitly used). 'Allah is with the doers of good' → believers implicitly addressed.

30:1.notes: Disjoined letters (Alif-Lam-Mim) open the section. The Roman-Byzantine prediction functions as a statement of divine sovereignty and decree. 'The matter is up to Allah' → sovereignty + divine-decree. 'Almighty, the Merciful' closing → power + mercy. Verse 8 references creation of heavens and earth and meeting the Lord (day of judgment). Believers explicitly named as those who will rejoice.

30:9.notes: The section surveys past nations — 'messengers came to them with clear signs' → prophethood-general; 'they rejected Allah's revelations and used to ridicule them' → denial-of-revelation; 'Allah would never wrong them' → justice; 'Allah originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned' → resurrection; ruins-and-travel theme → previous-creations-destroyed; punishment-of-past-nations is explicit.

30:12.notes: Day of Hour described; guilty despair. 'No intercessors from among their idols' → intercession (negated) + shirk. Believers in meadows → paradise. Disbelievers hauled into torment → hell.

30:17.notes: 11 labels, within ceiling. 'Glorify Allah / His is the praise' → praise (uttered glorification formula subhan + hamd). Verses 19-27 enumerate signs: living from dead / revival of land → natural-signs + resurrection; creation from dust → human-creation; mates created → marriage-and-family; creation of heavens and earth + diversity of languages → creation-of-heavens-earth; sleep by night and day, lightning + rain → natural-signs (also cosmic-bodies implied by heaven/earth standing); 'He is the Almighty, the Wise' → power + wisdom; 'all are submissive to Him' → sovereignty. Creation as a divine act → creation.

30:28.notes: Parable for mankind to refute shirk → tawhid + shirk. 'Fitrah Allah instilled in mankind' → mankind + human-creation (fitrah as created nature). 'Do not be of the idolaters' → polytheists. 'Perform the prayer' → prayer. 'Who can guide whom Allah leaves astray' → guidance. Those who follow desires without knowledge → disbelievers (wrongdoers). Verses 31-35 address repentance-then-shirk pattern after mercy → shirk reinforced.

30:36.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. 'When We give people a taste of mercy' → mercy + mankind. 'Allah expands provision' → provision. 'Give the relative his rights, the destitute, the wayfarer' → zakat-and-charity. 'The usury you practice… will not multiply with Allah; what you give in charity' → interest + zakat-and-charity (interest already counted). 'Corruption has appeared on land and sea' → corruption-on-earth. 'Qul: roam the earth… most were idolaters' → qul-statements + polytheists + punishment-of-past-nations. 'Before there comes a Day that cannot be averted' → day-of-judgment. 'Subhanahu wa ta'ala' (v.40) → praise.

30:46.notes: Winds bearing good news and rain → natural-signs + mercy + provision. Messengers sent with clear proofs → prophethood-general. 'It is incumbent on Us to help the believers' → believers. Disbelief persisting even after blessing → disbelievers. Verse 54: created from weakness, then strength, then weakness again → human-creation. Closing 'He is the Omniscient, the Omnipotent' → knowledge + power.

30:55.notes: Sinners swearing they stayed but an hour → day-of-judgment + disbelievers. Those with knowledge and faith correct them → believers + knowledge. 'This is the Day of Resurrection' → resurrection. Excuses not accepted → reckoning.

30:58.notes: 'We have cited in this Quran every sort of parable' → the-quran. 'Even if you bring them a miracle, those who disbelieve will say you are fakers' → denial-of-revelation + miracles + disbelievers. 'Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know' → knowledge (inverted — absence of knowledge as the trigger for sealing).

30:60.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet — 'do not let those who lack certainty belittle you' → muhammad (direct address). 'Be patient' — explicit command naming patience → patience. 'The promise of Allah is true' → divine-decree. Those who lack certainty → disbelievers.

31:1.notes: 15 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: 'guidance' (named explicitly as subject so rule-5 trigger is met — keep); 'natural-signs' (rain, creatures, plants in v10 — keep); 'shirk' (v11 challenges polytheists but the word 'shirk' is not used, only 'those besides Him' — marginal, trim candidate); 'arrogance' (v7 uses 'turns away in pride' / 'istakbara' — keep as trigger is met); 'mockery' (v6 explicitly 'make a mockery of it' — keep). 'Shirk' is explicitly named in v13 ('do not associate anything with Allah, for idolatry is a terrible wrong'). 'Marriage-and-family' applied because Luqman's advice is delivered to his son in a father-son parenting context. 'Wisdom' because Luqman is explicitly given hikma.

31:14.notes: 'Gratitude' triggered explicitly — 'give thanks to Me and to your parents'. 'Shirk' triggered by 'if they strive to have you associate with Me'. 'Human-creation' triggered by description of mother carrying child through hardship and two-year weaning — stages of human nurture. 'Righteous-conduct' triggered by explicit instruction on keeping company with parents in kindness. 'Marriage-and-family' for the parent-child obligations being legislated.

31:16.notes: 'Knowledge' triggered by 'Allah is Kind and Expert' / 'Latif Khabir' closing v16. 'Prayer' triggered explicitly in v17 ('observe the prayer'). 31:20.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: 'the-quran' (v20 references 'enlightening Scripture' and v27 the inexhaustible Words of Allah — arguably applies, keep); 'creation-of-heavens-earth' (v25 rhetorical question about who created heavens and earth — keep); 'resurrection' (v28 explicitly mentions creation and resurrection — keep). 'iblis' triggered by v21 explicit mention of Satan calling them to the Blaze. 'trust-in-god' triggered by v22 'whoever submits himself wholly to Allah and is a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handle'.

'tawhid' triggered by v30 'Allah is the Reality and what they worship besides Him is falsehood'. 'shirk' triggered by v30 'what they worship besides Him is falsehood'. 'sincerity' triggered by v32 'they call upon Allah devoting their religion to Him' — ikhlas is explicitly named (mukhlisina lahu al-din). 'mankind' triggered by v33 explicit 'O people!' (ya ayyuha al-nas). 'day-of-judgment' triggered by v33 'dread a Day when no parent can avail his child'. 'taqwa' triggered by v33 explicit 'be conscious of your Lord' (ittaqu rabbakum). 'divine-decree' triggered by v29 'each running for a stated term' and v33 'the promise of Allah is true'. 'provision' for ships sailing by grace of Allah as provision/blessing. 'knowledge' triggered by v29 'Allah is Cognizant of everything you do' and v30 sovereignty assertion.

31:34.notes: 'knowledge' triggered by explicit 'Allah is All-Knowing, Well-Informed' closing and the five items of exclusive divine knowledge. 'divine-decree' triggered by God's exclusive knowledge of the Hour and what souls will earn. 'natural-signs' triggered by 'He sends down the rain'. 'human-creation' triggered by 'He knows what the wombs contain'. 'day-of-judgment' triggered by 'knowledge of the Hour'. 'death-and-dying' triggered by 'no soul knows in what land it will die'.

32:1.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Disjoined letters open the section (Alif-Lam-Meem). The section covers: the Quran's divine origin and denial thereof; creation of heavens/earth in six days and the Throne; God's knowledge of visible/invisible; power and mercy named explicitly in v.6; human creation from clay through stages; the angel of death and return to God (death-and-dying); and the 'Say:' command in v.11 (qul-statements). Intercession is mentioned negatively ('no intercessor') but the section does not develop intercession as a theme — not tagged. Day of Resurrection for judgment of disputes — day-of-judgment.

33:1.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' triggers muhammad. Verse 4 addresses zihar (equating wives with mothers) and adopted-son fiction — both marriage-and-family. 'Allah speaks the truth and guides to the path' triggers guidance. Closing 'Knowledgeable and Wise' triggers knowledge and wisdom. 'Put your trust in Allah' is an explicit exhortation to tawakkul — triggers trust-in-god. Taqwa is explicitly commanded ('Fear Allah'). 10 labels, within ceiling.

33:5.notes: Adopted-son naming rules continue the marriage-and-family theme. Verse 6 establishes the Prophet's closeness to believers and his wives as mothers — marriage-and-family. 'More equitable with Allah' invokes justice. Closing 'Forgiving and Merciful' triggers mercy. Verse 6 mentions emigrants (muhajirun) alongside believers — migration tagged. Direct concern with the Prophet's household relationship to believers tags muhammad.

33:7.notes: Five prophets named explicitly (Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus) — all tagged. The solemn covenant/pledge taken from the prophets triggers covenant. 'Painful punishment prepared for disbelievers' triggers disbelievers and hell. 'Messenger and a prophet' pattern throughout — prophethood-general.

33:9.notes: 11 labels. The wind sent against the confederates is a divine natural intervention (natural-signs). Covenant broken by hypocrites (verse 15). Two 'Say' commands in verses 16–17 confirm qul-statements.

33:18.notes: Exposes the hypocrites' cowardice and hindrance during battle — hypocrites and hypocrisy central. 'These have never believed' — disbelief. Verse 21 'remembers Allah frequently' — remembrance explicitly named. Verse 21 'excellent example in the Messenger of Allah' substantively about Muhammad as model — muhammad. Believers addressed implicitly throughout. War context continues — war-and-treaties.

33:22.notes: Believers' faith strengthened at sight of confederates — believers. Hypocrites to be rewarded or pardoned — hypocrites. 'Forgiving and Merciful' closing — mercy. 'Allah repelled the disbelievers' — disbelievers. 'Strong and Mighty' — power. Verse 26 explicitly names 'People of the Book who backed them' — people-of-the-book. Verse 26 mentions killing and taking captives — manumission-and-captives. Verse 23 references covenant pledges of true believers — covenant. War context — war-and-treaties.

33:28.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' repeatedly — muhammad. Entire section addresses the Prophet's wives and household — marriage-and-family. Verse 33 explicitly commands 'perform the prayer' — prayer. Verse 33 commands 'give regular charity' — zakat-and-charity. Verse 33 'Allah desires to purify you' and taqwa invoked for the wives ('if you observe piety') — taqwa. Closing verse 34 'remember what is recited of Allah's revelations and wisdom' — the-quran. 'And wisdom' could suggest wisdom but it refers to the revelations recited, so the-quran covers it. 'Forgiving and Informed' closing — knowledge. Verse 29 and 31 mention reward in the Hereafter/paradise — paradise. 8 labels, within ceiling.

33:35.notes: This verse enumerates believing men and women across ten virtues. 'Patient men and patient women' — patience explicitly named. 'Humble men and humble women' (khashi'in) — humility explicitly named. 'Charitable men and women' — zakat-and-charity. 'Fasting men and fasting women' — fasting explicitly named. 'Men who remember Allah frequently' — remembrance explicitly named. 'Allah has prepared for them a pardon and immense reward' — paradise and mercy. Addressed to believers broadly. Universal enough in scope to warrant mankind. 10 labels, within ceiling.

33:36.notes: Verse 36 commands obedience to Allah and Messenger for believers — believers. Verse 37 names Zaid and describes the Prophet's marriage after Zaid's divorce — marriage-and-family and muhammad (substantively about his domestic life). 'The command of Allah was fulfilled' / 'absolute decree' — divine-decree. Verse 40 names Muhammad explicitly as Messenger and Seal of Prophets — muhammad confirmed, prophethood-general. 'Allah is Cognizant of everything' — knowledge. Verses 41–42 command remembrance and glorification — remembrance. 7 labels.

33:45.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' — muhammad. Description of the Prophet's roles as witness, bearer of good news, warner, caller to Allah — prophethood-general. Verse 47 gives believers the good news of great reward — believers, paradise. Verse 48 commands not obeying disbelievers and hypocrites — disbelievers, hypocrites. 'Trust in Allah' explicitly commanded — trust-in-god. 'Allah is Ever-Merciful towards the believers' (v.43 context spills; verse 47 'great reward from Allah') — mercy.

33:49.notes: Verse 49 addresses believers about divorce before consummation — divorce and marriage-and-family. 'O you who believe' — believers. Verse 50 is direct address to the Prophet about his permitted wives — muhammad. 'Forgiving and Merciful' — mercy. 'Allah is Omniscient' — knowledge. Section is entirely about the Prophet's marital permissions — marriage-and-family dominant.

33:53.notes: Rules about entering the Prophet's home and the hijab screen — marriage-and-family and muhammad. 'O you who believe' — believers. Verse 56: 'Allah and His angels give blessings to the Prophet' — angels. 'Whether you declare or hide it, Allah is Aware' — knowledge. Verse 57 warns those who insult/harm Allah and Messenger — slander-and-backbiting. Verse 58 warns those who harm believing men and women unjustly — slander-and-backbiting confirmed. Verse 55 closes with 'be conscious of Allah' — taqwa. 7 labels.

33:59.notes: Verse 59 direct address 'O Prophet' to instruct his wives and daughters and believing women on garments — muhammad, believers, marriage-and-family. 'Forgiving and Merciful' — mercy. Verses 60–61 threaten hypocrites and those with sickness in their hearts — hypocrites. Verse 62 invokes Allah's precedent with past nations — divine-decree (pattern of Allah = His established decree/sunna). Disbelievers not explicitly named but the threat covers those who spread corruption — borderline; held back to keep label count clean.

33:63.notes: Verse 63 'The people ask you' — mankind. 'Say, the knowledge rests with Allah' — qul-statements and knowledge. Verses 64–65 describe the fate of disbelievers in the Blaze forever — disbelievers, hell. Verse 66 describes the Day when faces are flipped into the Fire — day-of-judgment. Verses 67–68 contain an uttered supplication by the disbelievers in hell ('Lord, give them double punishment') — this is a du'a uttered but by the condemned in despair/curse, not a proper supplication for mercy; tagged as reckoning rather than dua-distress. Muhammad addressed implicitly via 'you' (qul). 8 labels.

33:69.notes: Verse 69 'O you who believe' — believers. Moses named explicitly — moses. Verse 70 'O you who believe, be conscious of Allah' — taqwa explicitly commanded. Verse 72 describes the Trust offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains, then accepted by humans — creation-of-heavens-earth and human-creation (the human being as a created entity bearing the Trust). The human described as 'unfair and ignorant' is the moral characterization, not a separate label. Hypocrites and polytheists appear in verse 73 which is a separate section, so not tagged here.

33:73.notes: Single verse. Hypocrites (men and women) — hypocrites. Idolaters/mushrikun (men and women) — polytheists. Believers redeemed — believers. 'Allah will punish' — implies hell for hypocrites and idolaters. 'Allah will redeem the believers' — mercy and repentance (tawbah explicitly mentioned: 'yatuba'). Closing 'Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful' — mercy confirmed. 6 labels.

34:1.notes: 12 labels at ceiling. 'Al-hamdu lillah' opens the surah → praise. Sovereignty (all in heavens/earth belongs to Him). Knowledge (knows what enters/exits earth and sky). Wisdom (al-Hakim). Mercy (al-Rahim, al-Ghafur). Provision (generous provision for believers). Day of Judgment (praise in the Hereafter; the Hour). Believers rewarded with forgiveness and provision. Disbelievers deny the Hour. Denial-of-revelation (those who strive against Our revelations). Hell implied for the latter but not described — kept to 12. Trim candidate if needed: provision (secondary to the eschatological frame).

34:6.notes: 'Those who received knowledge' (ahl al-'ilm) most plausibly refers to learned people of the Book who recognise the truth of what was revealed — tagged people-of-the-book with medium confidence per Ibn Kathir. 'It guides to the path of the Majestic' → guidance. Disbelievers mock resurrection (new creation). Verse 9 — heaven and earth caving in — natural-signs and power and creation-of-heavens-earth.

34:10.notes: David: mountains and birds echo with him, iron softened → miracles, natural-signs. Solomon: wind subjugated, spring of tar, jinn working → miracles, jinn. 'Work with appreciation' (O House of David) → gratitude (explicit command to give thanks / shukr). 'Spring of tar' / cauldrons → provision (secondary). God's knowledge (unseen) contrasted with jinn's ignorance at Solomon's death → knowledge. God's omnipotence over wind and matter → power. Death of Solomon → death-and-dying.

34:15.notes: Sheba narrative: two gardens, provision, 'eat of your Lord's provision and give thanks' → provision and gratitude (explicit shukr command). Flood punishment for ingratitude → punishment-of-past-nations. 'A forgiving Lord' → mercy. Iblis fulfils his assessment over them → iblis. 'Except a group of believers' → believers. Disbelievers follow Iblis → disbelievers. God as Guardian over all things ('your Lord is Guardian') → knowledge/divine-decree. Natural-signs: the two gardens and the flood as environmental signs.

34:22.notes: Heavy qul-sequence (verses 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30) → qul-statements. Tawhid asserted against false deities → tawhid + shirk. Intercession only with God's permission → intercession. 'He is the High, the Great' → sovereignty. 'Who provides from heavens and earth? Allah' → provision. 'He is the All-Knowing Judge' → knowledge + wisdom. 'We sent you universally to all people' → mankind + prophethood-general. Day promised that cannot be postponed → day-of-judgment. Disbelievers mock and question → disbelievers. 12 labels at ceiling.

34:31.notes: 13 labels — over ceiling. 'We will never believe in this Quran nor in what came before it' → the-quran + previous-scriptures + disbelief + denial-of-revelation. Wrongdoers captive before Lord, mutual blame between arrogant and oppressed → arrogance + reckoning. 'It was your scheming by night and day' → plotting. Yokes around necks, taste punishment of Fire → hell. Every town's warner rejected by affluent → prophethood-general + disbelievers. 'My Lord spreads/restricts provision' → provision. Qul appears at verses 36 and 39 → qul-statements. Trim candidates: previous-scriptures (only implied by 'what came before it'), prophethood-general (secondary to the eschatological scene).

34:40.notes: Day of gathering: angels asked if they were worshipped → day-of-judgment + angels + shirk. Angels say 'subhanaka' → praise (uttered glorification). Jinn worshipped instead → jinn. 'Taste the agony of the Fire' → hell. Disbelievers call revelation fabrication and magic → denial-of-revelation + the-quran + disbelievers. Past nations also denied messengers and were punished → punishment-of-past-nations.

34:46.notes: Six consecutive qul-commands → qul-statements. 'He is just a warner to you' → prophethood-general. 'Before the advent of a severe punishment' → day-of-judgment. 'He is the Knower of the Unseen' → knowledge. 'He is Hearing and Near' → nearness-and-response. 'If I am guided it is by what my Lord inspires me' → guidance. Disbelievers implied as addressees of the warner → disbelievers. Denial of the truth (falsehood vs. truth theme) → denial-of-revelation.

34:51.notes: Short two-verse section. Terror at seizure with no escape → day-of-judgment. Deathbed/too-late declaration of belief → disbelievers + disbelief. Their belief from 'a distant place' — too late to attain what they rejected → denial-of-revelation.

34:53.notes: Single verse. 'They have rejected it in the past and made allegations from a far-off place' → disbelief + denial-of-revelation + disbelievers. Minimal section; 3 labels appropriate.

34:54.notes: Single verse. Barrier placed between them and what they desire, as done with their counterparts before → punishment-of-past-nations. 'They were in disturbing doubt' → disbelief. Final sealing of fate → day-of-judgment. Disbelievers as subject → disbelievers.

35:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'al-hamdu lillah' → praise. Angels described as messengers with wings → angels. Verse 3 addresses 'O people' (ya ayyuha an-nas) → mankind. 'Is there a creator other than Allah' → tawhid. 'Provides for you from heaven and earth' → provision. 'Over all things competent' → power. 'None can withhold mercy' → mercy. 'Originator of heavens and earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'His is the dominion' is implicit in sovereignty claim.

35:4.notes: Verse 4 addresses the Prophet directly ('if they reject you') → muhammad. 'Messengers before you were rejected' → prophethood-general. Verse 5 addresses 'O people' → mankind. 'The Tempter' (Satan) inviting his gang to the Inferno → iblis + hell. 'Those who disbelieve will suffer harsh punishment' → disbelievers. 'Those who believe… will have forgiveness and great reward' → believers. 'Allah leads astray… and guides' → guidance. 'Allah knows exactly what they do' → knowledge. 'To Allah all matters are returned' + Day of Resurrection implied context → day-of-judgment (medium trigger but present via 'returned to Allah').

35:9.notes: Verse 9: wind, clouds, rain reviving dead land → natural-signs. 'Likewise is the Resurrection' → resurrection. Verse 11: created from dust then drop → human-creation. 'Nothing in a female's womb except with His knowledge' and 'in a Record' → knowledge. 'Easy for Allah' → power. Verse 10: 'those who plot evil, a terrible punishment awaits them' → plotting. 'All honor belongs to Allah' → sovereignty.

35:12.notes: Verse 12: two seas, fresh meat, jewelry, ships → natural-signs + provision. 'So that you may give thanks' is a passing mention of gratitude, not the section's subject. Verse 13: merging night/day, sun and moon → cosmic-bodies. 'His is the sovereignty' → sovereignty. 'Those you call upon besides Him possess not a speck' → tawhid + shirk. Verse 14: 'On the Day of Resurrection they will reject your partnership' → day-of-judgment. 'None informs you like an Expert' → knowledge.

35:15.notes: Verse 15 addresses 'O people' → mankind. Verses 16–17: 'If He wills He can do away with you' → power. Verse 18: 'No burdened soul can carry another's burden' → justice. 'Those who fear their Lord… and perform the prayer' → prayer + believers (implied). 'To Allah is the ultimate return' reaffirms judgment. Verse 24: 'We sent you… bearer of good news and warner; every community had a warner' → prophethood-general. Verse 25: 'their messengers came with clear proofs, with the Psalms, and with the Enlightening Scripture' → previous-scriptures. Verse 26: 'Then I seized those who disbelieved' → disbelievers + punishment-of-past-nations. 'Allah is Informed of His servants' (closing of verse 24 context) → knowledge. Section is long (12 verses) warranting rich tagging.

35:27.notes: Verse 27: rain, fruits, mountains of varied colors → natural-signs. Verse 28: human beings, animals, livestock of various colors; 'the learned fear Allah' — taqwa trigger is present but the verse names the attribute of fear of God as a quality of scholars, not as the section's explicit subject of instruction; borderline. 'Allah is Almighty, Oft-Forgiving' → mercy. Verse 29: 'recite the Book of Allah' → the-quran. 'Perform the prayer' → prayer. 'Spend of what We have provided' → zakat-and-charity + provision. Verse 30: 'He is Forgiving and Appreciative' → mercy (already tagged). 'Mankind' not explicitly addressed here but verse 28 mentions 'human beings' in the context of creation diversity; kept generic.

35:31.notes: Verse 31: 'What We inspired in you of the Book is the truth confirming what preceded it' → the-quran + previous-scriptures. 'Allah is Well-Informed… All-Seeing' → knowledge. Verse 32: 'We passed the Book to those We chose' → the-quran again. Verses 33–35: Gardens of Eden with gold, pearls, silk; no sorrow, no fatigue → paradise. Verse 34: 'Praise Allah who has lifted sorrow' — this is uttered praise by the inhabitants of paradise → praise. 'Our Lord is Most Forgiving, Most Appreciative' → mercy. Verse 36: Fire of Hell, punishment never lightened for disbelievers → hell + disbelievers. Verse 37: Inhabitants screaming 'Our Lord, let us out' — this is an uttered supplication in distress → dua-distress.

35:38.notes: Verse 38: 'Allah is the Knower of the future of heavens and earth… knows what hearts contain' → knowledge. Verse 39: 'He made you successors on earth'; disbelief described and its consequences → disbelievers + disbelief. Verse 40: 'Say, have you considered those partners of yours…' → qul-statements. 'Show me what they have created' refutes partners → shirk + tawhid. 'Creation' is implicitly invoked in the challenge about what partners created → creation.

35:41.notes: Verse 41: 'Allah holds heavens and earth lest they fall apart' → creation-of-heavens-earth + power. 'Most Clement, Most Forgiving' → mercy. Verse 42: They swore if a warner came they would be guided, but when the warner came they increased in aversion → prophethood-general + disbelievers. Verse 43: 'Priding themselves on earth' — Arabic istikbar explicitly named → arrogance. 'Scheming evil' → plotting. 'Do they expect anything but the precedent of the ancients?' → punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 44: 'Observe the fate of those who preceded them' → punishment-of-past-nations (reinforced). 'He is indeed Omniscient and Omnipotent' → knowledge (already tagged) + power (already tagged).

35:45.notes: Single verse section. 'If Allah were to punish the people for what they have earned, He would not leave a single creature' → mankind + justice. 'But He defers them until a stated time' → mercy (forbearance/clemency) + divine-decree (stated appointed time). 'Allah is Observant of His creatures' → knowledge.

36:1.notes: Disjoined letters Yā-Sīn open the section. 'By the Wise Quran' → the-quran + wisdom. 'You are one of the messengers' is direct address to Muhammad → muhammad + prophethood-general. 'The Almighty, the Merciful' → mercy. 'We have tallied all things in a Clear Record' → knowledge + divine-decree. 'We revive the dead' → resurrection. Disbelievers' sealed state described.

36:13.notes: Parable of the town and the messengers. The townspeople deny the messengers and threaten stoning → denial-of-revelation + mockery. The believing man's speech explicitly rejects false gods and affirms tawhid → tawhid + shirk. 'If the Merciful desires harm…their intercession will not avail' → mercy. The parable functions as punishment-of-past-nations by framing.

36:26.notes: The believing man is told to enter Paradise → paradise. 'How my Lord has forgiven me' → mercy. Immediate destruction of the town by a single Cry → punishment-of-past-nations. The destroyed people are the disbelieving townspeople → disbelievers.

36:30.notes: 13 labels — over the 12-ceiling. Trim candidates: knowledge (subsumed by wisdom here), creation (subsumed by natural-signs/cosmic-bodies context). Section opens with lament over rejection of messengers → prophethood-general + mockery. Past destroyed generations → punishment-of-past-nations. 'All will be arraigned before Us' → reckoning. Dead land revived → natural-signs + provision. 'Glory be to Him who created all the pairs' → praise + creation. Night/day cycle → cosmic-bodies + natural-signs. 'Design of the Almighty, the All-Knowing' → wisdom + knowledge. Sun and moon in orbits → cosmic-bodies.

36:41.notes: The laden Ark → natural-signs; tafsir associates this with Noah's ark → noah (medium confidence as the text says 'their offspring' allusively rather than naming Noah explicitly). God's power to drown them 'except by mercy from Us' → mercy + provision. 'Beware of what lies before you' invokes taqwa explicitly by the command to fear → taqwa. 'Spend of what Allah has provided' → zakat-and-charity. Disbelievers mock believers' charity → disbelievers + believers.

36:48.notes: Disbelievers mock the promised Day → disbelievers + denial-of-revelation. The sudden blast seizing them while they feud → day-of-judgment + signs-of-the-hour.

36:51.notes: 11 labels — within ceiling. Trumpet blown, rising from tombs → resurrection. Standing before the Lord → day-of-judgment. Paradise described with fruits and peace from a Merciful Lord → paradise + mercy. Justice: 'no soul will be wronged' → justice + reckoning. Criminals told to step aside → hell + disbelief. 'O Children of Adam, did I not covenant with you not to serve the devil' → mankind + iblis + covenant.

36:65.notes: Hands and feet testify → day-of-judgment + reckoning. God's power to blind or cripple them → power. 'Whoever We grant old age, We reverse his development' → human-creation + death-and-dying. 'It is only a reminder and a Clear Quran' → the-quran + prophethood-general. Warning those who disbelieve → disbelievers.

36:71.notes: Livestock created for humanity to ride and eat → natural-signs + provision + creation. 'Will they not give thanks?' → gratitude (explicit shukr trigger). They take gods other than Allah → shirk + disbelievers. 'We know what they conceal and reveal' → knowledge.

36:77.notes: 'Created him from a seed' → human-creation. 'Who will revive the bones when they have decayed?' and the response → resurrection. 'Say, He who initiated them will revive them. He has knowledge of every creation' → qul-statements + knowledge. 'He who created the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth + creation + power. Fire from green trees → natural-signs. 'Be, and it comes to be' → power.

36:83.notes: 'Glory be to Him' (subḥāna) → praise uttered. 'In whose hand is the dominion of everything' → sovereignty. 'To Him you will be returned' → resurrection.

37:1.notes: Opening oath by the 'aligners/drivers/reciters' is understood as angels per Ibn Kathir. Tawhid asserted in v4. Sovereignty in v5 (Lord of heavens, earth, and the Easts). Cosmic-bodies: planets adorning lower heaven (v6). Iblis/jinn: defiant devils repelled from eavesdropping (vv7-10).

37:11.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Mockery explicit (vv12,14). Denial of resurrection and sorcery accusation (vv15-16) = denial-of-revelation. Human-creation: created from sticky clay (v11). Resurrection debated (v16). Day of Judgment named (v20). Hell: led to the way to Hell (v23). Reckoning: they will be questioned (v24). Shirk: worshipping other than Allah (v22). Arrogance: grew arrogant at 'la ilaha illa Allah' (v35). Qul-statement: 'Say: Yes indeed' (v18). Prophethood-general: 'he confirmed the messengers' (v37).

37:40.notes: Sincere servants of Allah (sincerity trigger explicit). Paradise described with fruits, gardens of bliss, furnishings, pure drink, companions. Provision: 'known provision' (v41).

37:50.notes: Dialogue between a believer in paradise and his disbelieving companion now in hell (vv50-68). Paradise and hell both described in detail. Day of Judgment setting. Disbelievers: those who denied resurrection (v52-53). Punishment-of-past-nations: 'most of the ancients before them went astray' and 'observe the end of those who were warned' (vv71-73). Prophethood-general: messengers sent to warn (v72). Mercy: 'grace of my Lord' (v57). Sincerity: 'sincere servants of Allah' (v74).

37:75.notes: Noah called out to God; God responds as Best of Responders (nearness-and-response). Family saved from calamity. Descendants made survivors. Drowning of others = punishment-of-past-nations. 'We reward the righteous' (v80) — righteous-conduct label triggered by explicit reward formula. Believers: 'one of Our believing servants' (v81).

37:83.notes: Abraham named as being of Noah's kind (v83). Abraham confronts his father and people about idol worship — shirk and tawhid explicitly invoked (vv85-87). Breaking/striking idols (vv91-93) = miracle / sign of prophethood. 'Allah created you and what you manufacture' (v96) = creation. Plotting: 'they wished him ill' (v98). Polytheists: those who worshipped idols.

37:99.notes: Ishmael not named explicitly; confidence medium on that label specifically.

37:112.notes: Isaac announced as prophet (v112). Moses and Aaron blessed and aided (vv114-116). 'Clarifying Scripture' given to Moses and Aaron = previous-scriptures. Guided upon straight path = guidance. Children of Israel: 'their people' delivered from disaster (v115). Believers: 'believing servants' (v122). Mercy/provision framing: 'We blessed… We reward the righteous.'

37:123.notes: Elijah as messenger (v123). Calls people away from Baal worship = shirk/tawhid. 'Do you not fear?' — taqwa invoked but as rhetorical address, not explicit subject; held back per rule 5. Disbelievers called him a liar = denial-of-revelation. Prophethood-general. Believers: 'one of Our believing servants' (v132).

37:133.notes: Lot named as messenger (v133); his family saved, others annihilated (vv134-136) = punishment-of-past-nations. Jonah narrative: flight, fish, wilderness, gourd tree growing over him (vv139-146) = natural-signs (gourd tree, wilderness). Praise: Jonah 'was one of those who praised' (v143) — glorification uttered implicitly referenced. Believers: 'one of Our believing servants' (implied pattern). Mercy: people believed and were given enjoyment (v148). Prophethood-general throughout.

37:149.notes: No explicit 'qul' imperative found on re-reading; removing qul-statements. Praise confirmed by 'Subhana Allah' in v159.

37:167.notes: Disbelievers claimed they would have been faithful if they had received scripture (vv167-169), then rejected it = denial-of-revelation. Prophethood-general: 'servant messengers will be supported' (vv171-173). Muhammad directly addressed: 'So disregard them… And watch them' (vv174-175, 178-179) — second-person direct address to the Prophet. Sovereignty: 'Lord of Glory' (v180). Praise: 'Subhana Rabbika' uttered (v180) = praise.

37:182.notes: Single verse: 'Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbi al-'alamin' — explicit uttered praise (hamd). Sovereignty: 'Lord of the Worlds'.

38:1.notes: Disjoined letter Sad opens the section. Disbelievers mock tawhid ('Did he turn all the gods into one God?'), accuse the Prophet of sorcery and fabrication, and past generations are cited as warning.

38:8.notes: Verse 12 names Noah, 'Aad, Pharaoh; verse 13 names Thamud, the people of Lot, and the dwellers of the Woods (Madyan/Shuayb's people). 'Treasuries of the mercy of your Lord—the Majestic, the Giver' invokes mercy and sovereignty. 'Day of Account' in v16. 13 labels — over ceiling. Trim candidates: sovereignty (secondary to mercy/denial framing), reckoning (subsumed by day-of-judgment).

38:17.notes: Opens with command to be patient ('Be patient in the face of what they say') — patience is the explicit subject of the address. David is the central figure; mountains and birds glorify with him (natural signs). Wisdom and decisive speech explicitly granted. Dispute-judgment scene invokes justice. Patience trigger met at v17 opening.

38:24.notes: David seeks forgiveness and prostrates repentantly; God forgives him — repentance and mercy both explicitly present. 'Nearness to Us' invokes nearness-and-response. 'Day of Account' closes the section explicitly.

38:27.notes: 'We did not create the heaven and the earth in vain' — creation-of-heavens-earth as explicit subject. Woe to disbelievers from the Fire. 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds' vs 'those who make trouble on earth' — righteous-conduct is explicit subject of the contrast. 'The pious' (muttaqin) named explicitly — taqwa trigger met. 'A blessed Book' in v29 names the Quran. Believers implicitly addressed via the contrast.

38:30.notes: Solomon granted to David. Solomon's horses episode, his testing, his repentance. Uttered du'a in v35: 'My Lord, forgive me, and grant me a kingdom' — dua-forgiveness triggered. Wind and demons (jinn) placed at his service — miracles. 'Nearness to Us' closes the section. Natural signs: wind controlled at his command.

38:41.notes: Job calls out to his Lord about Satan's affliction — uttered du'a in distress (v41). Family restored as mercy (v43). 'We found him patient' is explicit patience label trigger. Oath-keeping instruction in v44. Marriage-and-family: family restored.

38:45.notes: Six named prophets: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Ishmael, Elisha, Dhul-Kifl. 'Remembrance of the Home' is explicitly named as their distinguishing quality — remembrance trigger met.

38:49.notes: 'The devout will have a good place of return' — taqwa (muttaqin) explicitly named. Gardens of Eden described. 'Day of Account' in v53. 'Our bounty, inexhaustible' — provision. Believers/devout implicitly addressed throughout.

38:55.notes: Vivid hell description with boiling and bitter cold. Dispute among denizens of Hell. 'Did we take them for mockery' (v63) — mockery explicitly named as a concept. 'Day of Account' referenced. Disbelievers/transgressors as subject throughout.

38:65.notes: Two 'Say:' (qul) commands in vv65 and 67 — qul-statements. Tawhid declared: 'no god except Allah—the One'. Sovereignty: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth'. Mercy: 'the Mighty, the Forgiver'. 'The Highest Assembly' (angels) referenced in v69. 'A message of great importance' refers to the Quran/revelation.

38:71.notes: Creation of Adam from clay, prostration commanded, Iblis refuses — arrogance explicitly named ('Are you too proud?', 'He was too proud'). Disbelief: 'one of the faithless'. Hell: God will fill it with Iblis and his followers. Day of Judgment referenced in vv78 and 81. Sincerity: 'loyal servants' (mukhlaseen) explicitly named as those excluded from Iblis's seduction — sincerity trigger met. Divine-decree: Iblis deferred until the appointed day.

38:86.notes: 'Say:' opens the section — qul-statements. 'A reminder to mankind' — mankind explicitly named. Quran's nature as a reminder and the Prophet's sincerity as its messenger.

38:88.notes: Single verse. 'You will know its message after a while' — could refer to the Day of Judgment or to future events vindicating the Quran's truth. Day-of-judgment tagged on the basis that 'after a while' in context (following the hell/judgment passages) most plausibly refers to eschatological verification. Confidence medium due to brevity and ambiguity.

39:1.notes: v1: 'The revelation of the Book…Mighty and Wise' → the-quran, wisdom. v2: 'serve Allah, devoting your religion to Him' → sincerity (explicit ikhlas trigger). v3: shirk-adjacent (those taking guardians besides Him) → tawhid. v4: 'Glory be to Him…the One, the Prevailing' → tawhid, sovereignty, praise (subhanahu). v5: creation of heavens/earth, sun/moon, night/day → creation-of-heavens-earth, cosmic-bodies; 'Almighty, the Forgiver' → power, mercy. 10 labels.

39:6.notes: v6: created from one person, stages in womb → human-creation; 'His is the kingdom, no god but He' → tawhid, sovereignty; universal address about humanity → mankind. v7: 'if you disbelieve' → disbelief; 'if you are thankful, He will approve' → gratitude (shukr explicitly mentioned); 'to your Lord is your return, He will inform you' → reckoning; 'aware of what hearts contain' → knowledge. 8 labels.

39:8.notes: v8: man in adversity prays, then forgets and sets up rivals to Allah → shirk; 'Say, enjoy your disbelief…you will be among inmates of the Fire' → qul-statements, hell, disbelievers. v9: one who worships at night prostrating and standing, fearing Hereafter, hoping for mercy → prayer (explicit salah-like devotion), mercy, taqwa (mindfulness of Hereafter); 'Only those possessed of reason will remember' → remembrance. Two qul commands present → qul-statements.

39:10.notes: v10: 'Say, O My devotees who have believed, keep your duty (ittaqu) to your Lord' → believers, taqwa, qul-statements; 'the steadfast will be paid their wages without reckoning' → patience (explicit mention of sabr/steadfast). v11-14: multiple 'Say' commands about sincere worship and fear of 'a horrendous Day' → qul-statements, sincerity, day-of-judgment. v15: 'losers on the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment, disbelievers. v16: layers of Fire → hell; 'O My servants, beware of Me' → taqwa. 8 labels.

39:17.notes: v17: 'those who avoid worship of idols' → shirk (avoidance thereof); 'devoted to Allah…good news' → believers, guidance. v18: 'those whom Allah has guided' → guidance. v19: those who have deserved punishment, cannot be saved from Fire → hell. v20: 'those who fear their Lord (ittaqaw)…mansions…streams' → taqwa, paradise. 6 labels.

39:21.notes: v21: rain from sky, underground wells, varied plants, yellowing, debris — 'a reminder for those with understanding' → natural-signs, remembrance. v22: heart opened to Islam, on a light from Lord; 'woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the mention of Allah' → guidance, disbelief, remembrance. v23: 'Allah has sent down the best of narrations…that is Allah's guidance' → the-quran, guidance. 5 labels.

39:24.notes: v24: 'covers his face against the misery of the Day of Resurrection'; 'taste what you used to earn' → day-of-judgment, hell. v25: 'Those before them also denied the truth, so the penalty came upon them' → punishment-of-past-nations, denial-of-revelation. v26: 'Allah made them taste disgrace in the present life; the punishment of the Hereafter is worse' → disbelievers, hell. 5 labels.

39:27.notes: v27: 'We have cited in this Quran for mankind every ideal' → the-quran, mankind. v28: 'An Arabic Quran…so they may become righteous (yattaqun)' → the-quran, taqwa. v29: parable of a man with many squabbling partners vs. one devoted to one master — illustrates tawhid vs. shirk → tawhid; 'al-hamdu lillah' uttered → praise. 5 labels.

39:30.notes: v30: 'You (direct address to Prophet) will die, and they will die' → muhammad (direct second-person address). v31: 'on the Day of Resurrection you will be quarrelling before your Lord' → day-of-judgment. v32: 'lies about Allah…Is there not in Hell room for the ungrateful?' → hell, disbelievers. v33-34: 'those who promote truth…the righteous…will have whatever they please with their Lord' → paradise. v35: 'Allah will acquit them of the worst of their deeds' → mercy. 6 labels.

39:36.notes: v36: direct address 'they frighten you' → muhammad; 'Is Allah not enough for His servant?' → trust-in-god; guidance theme → guidance. v37: 'Allah guides…Allah is Powerful' → guidance, power. v38: polytheists admit Allah created heavens and earth → creation-of-heavens-earth; idols cannot lift harm or hold back mercy → tawhid, shirk; 'Say, Allah suffices for me; on Him the reliant rely' → qul-statements, trust-in-god. v39-40: 'Say: O my people, work…' → qul-statements. 8 labels.

39:41.notes: v41: 'We sent down upon you the Book for mankind' → the-quran, mankind. v42: 'Allah takes the souls at the time of their death…and those that have not died during their sleep' — the soul-taking at sleep and death → death-and-dying, divine-decree; 'signs for people who reflect' → natural-signs (ayat). v43: 'Or have they chosen intercessors other than Allah? Say…' → qul-statements, intercession (false intercessors). v44: 'Say, All intercession is up to Allah. To Him belongs the kingdom' → qul-statements, intercession, sovereignty. 8 labels.

39:45.notes: v45: hearts of disbelievers shrink when Allah alone mentioned, rejoice when others mentioned → tawhid, shirk, disbelievers. v46: 'Say, Allahumma (uttered supplication form), Initiator of heavens and earth, Knower of secrets…You will judge between Your servants' — this is an uttered du'a directed by God to the Prophet to say → qul-statements; the supplication asks God to judge/resolve disputes, which is distress/appeal context → dua-distress; 'Knower' → knowledge; 'You will judge' → justice. v47-48: wrongdoers on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment. Note: v46 contains 'Qul Allahumma…' — both a qul-statement and an uttered supplication. 8 labels.

39:49.notes: v49: 'When adversity touches the human being, he calls on Us; when We favor him…he says I attained this by my knowledge' → mankind (universal human pattern), disbelievers (ingratitude). v50: 'Those before them said it' → punishment-of-past-nations. v51: evils of their deeds caught up with them → punishment-of-past-nations. v52: 'Allah extends provision to whomever He wills, and constricts it; in that are signs' → provision, natural-signs (ayat for believers); 'knowledge' dimension of God's action → knowledge. 6 labels.

39:53.notes: v53: 'Say, O My servants who have transgressed…do not despair of Allah's mercy, for Allah forgives all sins. He is the Forgiver, the Clement' → qul-statements, mercy, repentance (turning back implied by 'do not despair'). v54: 'Turn to your Lord and submit…before retribution comes' → repentance. v55: 'follow the best of what was revealed…before punishment comes suddenly' → the-quran (what was revealed), repentance. v56-58: soul's regret at Day, wishing for guidance, wishing for another chance → day-of-judgment (implicit), but not explicitly named; keeping to hell and arrogance for v59. v59: 'My Verses did come to you, but you called them lies, turned arrogant, and were of the faithless' → arrogance (istakbarta explicitly), disbelief (kufr named), hell (implicit from context of the sequence), denial-of-revelation (calling Verses lies). believers tagged for the address 'O My servants who have believed' scope in v53. 8 labels.

39:60.notes: v60: 'Day of Resurrection…those who told lies about Allah with faces blackened…Is there not a place in Hell for the arrogant?' → day-of-judgment, hell, arrogance, disbelievers. v61: 'Allah will save those who maintained righteousness (ittaqaw)' → taqwa, paradise. v62: 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is in Charge of all things' → creation, sovereignty. v63: 'To Him belong the reins of the heavens and the earth; those who blaspheme…are the losers' → sovereignty, disbelievers. 8 labels.

39:64.notes: 11 labels — at ceiling. All independently justified.

39:71.notes: v71: disbelievers driven to Hell in throngs; keepers ask 'did not messengers come to you reciting revelations and warning you?' — affirms prophethood; they say 'yes but the verdict of punishment is justified against disbelievers' → disbelievers, hell, prophethood-general, day-of-judgment. v72: 'Enter the gates of Hell…How wretched is the destination of the arrogant' → hell, arrogance (mutakabbirin explicitly named). 5 labels.

39:73.notes: v73: 'those who feared their Lord (ittaqaw) led to Paradise in throngs…its keepers say Peace be upon you, you have been good, enter it' → taqwa, paradise, believers. v74: 'they will say: al-hamdu lillah who fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, enjoying Paradise as we please' → praise (hamd uttered explicitly by the inhabitants), paradise, day-of-judgment (the promise fulfilled on this day). 5 labels.

39:75.notes: v75: 'angels hovering around the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise (yusabbihuna bihamdi rabbihim)' → angels, praise (uttered glorification). 'Judgment will be passed equitably' → justice, day-of-judgment. 'Throne' implies sovereignty. 'al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alameen' uttered → praise. 5 labels.

40:1.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Ha-Meem opens the surah triggering disjoined-letters. Verse 2 names the Scripture. Verse 3 clusters multiple divine attributes: Forgiver (mercy), Accepter of repentance (mercy/justice), Severe in punishment (justice/power), tawhid explicit. Verse 5 names Noah and the confederates (punishment-of-past-nations). Verse 6 names Hell. denial-of-revelation covers verse 4-5 disputation against signs.

40:7.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Verses 7-9 contain uttered supplications by the angels: 'Rabbanā wasiʿta kulla shayʾin raḥmatan wa-ʿilman faghfir…' — dua-forgiveness and dua-protection both triggered. Paradise (Gardens of Eternity) and Hell (agony of the Blaze) both mentioned. Verse 10-12 address disbelievers at judgment; shirk explicit in verse 12. wisdom justified by 'Almighty, Most Wise' closing formula in verse 8.

40:13.notes: Verse 13 — rain/sustenance from sky as sign of provision and natural-signs. Verse 14 — 'call upon Allah with sincere devotion' triggers sincerity explicitly. Verse 15 — 'Exalted in rank, Owner of the Throne' triggers sovereignty; Spirit conveyed to warn of Day of Encounter triggers prophethood-general and day-of-judgment. Verse 16 — 'To whom does sovereignty belong? To Allah the One' triggers tawhid. Verse 17 — reckoning on the Day.

40:18.notes: Verse 18 — Day of Imminence described; 'no intercessor to be obeyed' triggers intercession label. Verse 19 — 'He knows the deceptions of the eyes and what hearts conceal' triggers knowledge. Verse 20 — 'Allah judges with justice' triggers justice; 'those they invoke besides Him' triggers shirk; tawhid asserted by contrast.

40:21.notes: Verses 21-22 — rhetorical question about travelling the earth and seeing fate of earlier peoples. Verse 22 — messengers came with clear proofs, they disbelieved, Allah seized them. 'He is Strong, Severe in retribution' closes with power and justice attributes.

40:23.notes: Verse 23 — Moses sent with signs and clear authority. Verse 24 — Pharaoh (and Hamaan and Qarun) named; accusation of 'lying sorcerer' triggers sorcery (accusation against Moses) and denial. Verse 25 — killing sons of believers, plotting. Verse 26 — Pharaoh plots to kill Moses, mentions 'spread disorder in the land.' Verse 27 — Moses utters 'I have sought the protection of my Lord and your Lord from every tyrant who does not believe in the Day of Account' — dua-protection triggered; day-of-judgment mentioned. Arrogance: 'every tyrant who does not believe.'

40:28.notes: Revised: pharaoh, believers, guidance, sovereignty, disbelievers. The man from Pharaoh's family defends Moses and warns his people. guidance named explicitly ('Allah does not guide…'). sovereignty ('yours is the dominion today'). pharaoh speaks in verse 29. believers — the man is described as 'a believing man.'

40:30.notes: The believing man continues his warning. Verse 31 names Noah, Aad, and Thamood explicitly — noah, ad, thamud, punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 31 — 'Allah wants no injustice for the servants' triggers justice. Verses 32-33 — Day of Calling Out described; 'whomever Allah misguides has no guide' triggers guidance.

40:34.notes: Verse 34 — Joseph named explicitly; his rejection by his people. 'Allah leads astray the outrageous skeptic.' Verse 35 — 'those who argue against Allah's revelations without authority' triggers denial-of-revelation; 'Allah seals the heart of every proud bully' triggers arrogance explicitly ('mutakabbir jabbār'). Verse 36-37 — Pharaoh named; instructs Hamaan to build tower to reach God of Moses — mockery of tawhid. disbelief and disbelievers present throughout.

40:38.notes: The believing man's continued da'wah. Verse 38 — 'guide you to the path of rectitude.' Verse 39 — this world vs. Hereafter. Verse 40 — paradise for believers, hell for transgressors. Verse 42 — 'you call me to reject Allah and associate with Him' — shirk and tawhid explicit. Verse 42 — 'the Mighty Forgiver' — mercy. Verse 44 — 'I commit my case to Allah' — trust-in-god explicitly.

40:45.notes: Verse 45 — Allah protected the believing man; terrible torment on Pharaoh's clan. Verse 46 — Fire exposed morning and evening, and on Day of Hour 'admit Pharaoh's clan to most intense agony' — hell and day-of-judgment. Verse 47-48 — arrogance in hell: 'those who were arrogant' named twice. Verses 49-50 — those in Fire ask keepers of Hell; messengers came with clear signs — prophethood-general. pharaoh named via 'Pharaoh's clan.'

40:51.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Verse 51 — Allah supports messengers and believers. Verse 52 — day-of-judgment. Verse 53 — Moses named; Children of Israel inherit Scripture — previous-scriptures, children-of-israel. Verse 54 — 'a guide and a reminder' — guidance. Verse 55 — 'be patient' explicitly — patience; 'ask forgiveness for your sin' (command, not uttered du'a); 'proclaim the praise of your Lord' — praise uttered/commanded (borderline: 'sabbih bi-hamdi rabbika' is a command to praise, not an uttered praise formula — however 'sabbih bi-hamd' is close enough to the praise-utterance category; keeping praise). knowledge — closing verse 56 'All-Hearing, All-Seeing.' arrogance — verse 56 'feeling of greatness.' disbelievers — verse 56 disputants.

40:57.notes: Verse 57 — creation of heavens and earth vs. creation of humanity — creation-of-heavens-earth and human-creation. Verse 58 — believers vs. sinners; 'how little you reflect.' Verse 59 — the Hour is coming — day-of-judgment. Verse 60 — 'Pray to Me and I will respond' — prayer (command to pray, not uttered du'a); 'those too proud to worship' — arrogance explicit; 'enter Hell' — hell. tawhid implicit in 'pray to Me alone' but not explicit enough by rule 5 — however verse 60 says 'Your Lord has said pray to Me' which is a monotheistic command; keeping tawhid. mankind — verse 57 addresses 'most people' universally.

40:61.notes: cosmic-bodies, natural-signs, creation, provision, tawhid, mankind, praise, disbelievers — 8 labels. praise triggered twice by 'tabāraka Allāh' (v64) and 'al-ḥamdu lillāh' (v65).

40:66.notes: Verse 66 opens with 'Say (qul)' — qul-statements. Prohibited from worshipping those invoked besides Allah — shirk and tawhid. Verse 67 — creation from dust, seed, embryo, infant, maturity, old age, death — human-creation and death-and-dying. 'A predetermined age' (ajalin musamman) — divine-decree. Verse 68 — 'He gives life and death; when He decides on a thing, Be and it is' — power and divine-decree.

40:69.notes: Verse 69 — those who dispute Allah's revelations — denial-of-revelation. Verse 70 — those who call the Book a lie — the-quran, denial-of-revelation. Verses 71-72 — dragged in chains into boiling water and Fire — hell. Verse 73-74 — 'where are those you used to deify?' — shirk. Verse 75 — 'you used to rejoice on earth in other than the truth.' Verse 76 — 'Enter gates of Hell… terrible dwelling for the arrogant' — arrogance explicit. punishment-of-past-nations implied by the general pattern of destroyed communities but not explicitly named here — removing; the section is about future punishment not past nations. Keeping: disbelievers, denial-of-revelation, the-quran, hell, shirk, arrogance.

40:77.notes: Verse 77 — direct second-person address to the Prophet ('be patient… whether We show you some of what We have promised them or take you to Us') — muhammad (direct address). 'Be patient' explicitly — patience. 'The promise of Allah is true' — divine-decree. Verse 78 — messengers sent before; miracles only by Allah's leave — prophethood-general, miracles. 'Then when the command of Allah is issued, fair judgment will be passed' — day-of-judgment. disbelievers — 'the seekers of vanity will lose.'

40:79.notes: Verses 79-81 — domestic animals for riding and eating, ships for transport — natural-signs (animals as signs of Creator), provision (sustenance and benefits from animals), creation (Allah created them). Verse 81 — 'He shows you His signs' — natural-signs confirmed. mankind — address is universal ('for you'). Short section, 4 labels appropriate.

40:82.notes: Verse 82 — 'have they not journeyed through the land' — previous-creations-destroyed and punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 83 — messengers came with clear proofs; they mocked — prophethood-general. Verse 84 — when they saw Allah's might: 'We believe in Allah alone and reject what we used to associate with Him' — tawhid and shirk explicit ('we reject what we used to associate'). disbelievers and disbelief throughout.

40:85.notes: Single verse. Faith at the moment of punishment is too late — 'This has been Allah's way of dealing with His servants' (sunnat Allāh) — divine-decree. punishment-of-past-nations (the pattern applied). disbelievers and disbelief. Short section warrants fewer labels.

41:1.notes: Disjoined letters Hā-Mīm open the section. The Quran is described as a revelation from the Most Merciful. Verse 6 contains qul. Verse 7 mentions those who do not pay zakat as disbelievers. Verse 8 promises uninterrupted reward (paradise implied). Polytheists warned with 'woe to the idolaters.'

41:9.notes: Verse 9 opens with qul. Creation of earth in two days, provisions in four days, seven heavens in two days — all creation cosmology. Stars as lamps decorate the lower heaven (cosmic-bodies). Closing formula 'the Almighty, the All-Knowing' → power and knowledge. Shirk addressed directly ('you attribute equals to Him').

41:13.notes: 'Aad and Thamood' named explicitly. Verse 13 opens with qul. 'Messengers came to them' — prophethood-general. 'Ad turned arrogant' — arrogance explicitly named (istakbara). Thamud 'preferred blindness over guidance' — guidance named as the rejected alternative. Verse 16 mentions punishment of the hereafter being more shameful — hell implied. Verse 18 'saved those who believed and were righteous' — believers and taqwa both explicitly named ('believed and were righteous/taqwa').

41:19.notes: Enemies of Allah herded into the Fire — hell. Their senses testify against them — reckoning. 'Allah who made all things speak... created you the first time' — knowledge and human-creation. Day of judgment scene throughout.

41:25.notes: Companions (devils/shaytans associated with Iblis) assigned to lead astray — iblis. Jinn and humans mentioned explicitly. Disbelievers told not to listen to the Quran — denial-of-revelation, the-quran. Verse 28 describes Fire as their home — hell. Verses 30-32 describe angels descending on the righteous with news of paradise and the mercy of 'All-Forgiving, Merciful One' — paradise, angels, mercy.

41:33.notes: 'Who is better in speech than someone who calls to Allah and acts with integrity and says I am of those who submit' — righteous-conduct and sincerity explicitly invoked. 'Repel evil with good' — righteous-conduct. 'None will attain it except those who persevere' — patience explicitly named. 'Seek refuge in Allah from the Devil' — iblis. Closing 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' — knowledge. No uttered du'a (the refuge-seeking is a command, not a quoted supplication), so no dua-protection tag.

41:37.notes: Night, day, sun and moon as signs — cosmic-bodies. Command not to worship sun/moon — tawhid and shirk. 'He Who revived it will revive the dead' — resurrection. Rain reviving the earth — natural-signs. 'He is Able to do all things' — power. Angels in the presence of the Lord praise Him night and day — angels and praise (subḥān-equivalent glorification uttered by angels).

41:40.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: 'guidance' (mentioned but not the section's primary subject), 'previous-scriptures' (passing mention of Moses's book, could be subsumed by 'moses').

41:46.notes: 'Your Lord is not unjust to the servants' — justice explicitly stated. 'To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour' — knowledge and signs-of-the-hour. 'No fruit emerges... except with His knowledge' — knowledge, divine-decree. On the Day He calls out 'Where are My associates?' — day-of-judgment, shirk (the associates are exposed as worthless).

41:49.notes: 'The human being never tires' — mankind (universal human nature). 'We let him taste a mercy from Us' — mercy. Disbelievers warned of punishment — disbelievers. 'I do not think the Hour is coming' — day-of-judgment (denial of it). 'We will show them Our proofs on the horizons and in their very souls' — natural-signs (signs on the horizons). 'Your Lord is witness over everything' — knowledge. Verse 52 contains qul — qul-statements. 'He is Able to do all things' — power (from verse 39 straddling, but the power claim in this section comes from v53 'witness over everything' which maps better to knowledge).

41:54.notes: Single verse. 'In doubt about the encounter with their Lord' — disbelievers, day-of-judgment. 'He comprehends everything' — knowledge (al-muhit, all-encompassing knowledge).

42:1.notes: Verses 1-2 open with the disjoined letters Ha-Meem and Ayn-Seen-Qaf. Verse 3 names revelation to the Prophet and those before him — prophethood-general. Verse 4 asserts sovereignty ('To him belongs everything'). Verse 5: angels glorify and seek forgiveness for those on earth — praise is uttered by the angels ('yusabbihuna bi-hamdi rabbihim'); mercy named ('al-Ghafour al-Raheem'). Verse 6: those who take masters besides Him — shirk. Power/wisdom via 'al-Azeez al-Hakeem' (v3) and 'al-Aliyy al-Azeem' (v4) — sovereignty and knowledge cluster.

42:7.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: divine-decree (implicit rather than explicit subject), provision (present but secondary to sovereignty). Core labels: the-quran (Arabic Quran revealed), prophethood-general (warning mission), day-of-judgment (Day of Assembly), paradise/hell (two groups), mercy ('admits into His mercy'), sovereignty ('keys of the heavens and earth'), knowledge ('He is aware of all things'), power ('power over all things'), creation-of-heavens-earth ('Originator of the heavens and the earth'). Verse 11 also touches human-creation via mates/pairs but the focus is the Creator's uniqueness.

42:13.notes: Four prophets named explicitly (Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus). 'Uphold the religion and be not divided' — tawhid/unity of religion. 'Idolaters' (mushrikeen) — polytheists. 'Those who were made to inherit the Book' — people-of-the-book. Divine-decree via 'a predetermined decision from your Lord' (v14). Guidance via 'He guides to Himself whoever repents.' Previous-scriptures implied by the inherited Book (v14).

42:19.notes: Verse 19: 'Allah is kind… He provides… the Powerful, the Honorable' — provision, power, mercy (latif/kind clusters with mercy). Verse 20: harvest of Hereafter vs. this world — paradise/hell contrast implicit (no share of Hereafter). Verse 21: partners legislating religion not authorized — shirk. Verse 22: unjust terrified of what they earned (hell); believers in the Meadows of Gardens (paradise). 'Those who believe and do good deeds' — believers.

42:23.notes: Verse 23: 'Say, I ask of you no wage…' — qul-statements. Believers addressed. 'Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative' — mercy. Verse 24: 'they say He forged a lie' — denial-of-revelation. 'He knows what is in the hearts' — knowledge. Verse 25: 'He who accepts repentance… remits the sins' — repentance (explicitly named). Verse 27: provision ('spreads the bounties in precise measure'). Verse 28: rain — natural-signs and mercy ('unfolds His mercy'). Disbelievers named in v26 with severe punishment.

42:29.notes: Verse 29: 'signs are the creation of the heavens and the earth and the creatures' — creation-of-heavens-earth, natural-signs. 'Able to gather them at will' — power; gathering also evokes day-of-judgment. Verse 30: misfortune from what hands earned, 'yet He pardons much' — mercy and justice (divine recompense). Verse 32-33: ships sailing like flags, winds — natural-signs. Verse 33: 'signs for every disciplined, grateful person' — the word grateful (shakour) appears explicitly but as descriptor of the audience, not the section's subject; borderline on gratitude; holding back per rule 5. Verse 35: disputers of signs have no asylum — denial-of-revelation could apply but the framing here is more about the power of God; not adding to stay within ceiling.

42:36.notes: Verse 36: 'those who believe and rely on their Lord' — believers, trust-in-god (tawakkul explicitly named: 'rely on their Lord'). Verse 37: avoid major sins, forgive when angry — righteous-conduct (the section is explicitly structured as an instruction in ethical conduct). Verse 38: 'pray regularly' — prayer (salah named explicitly). 'Conduct their affairs by mutual consultation' — justice-and-witness (consultation/shura is a justice/governance concept). Verse 40: 'whoever pardons and makes reconciliation' — mercy (God's attribute confirmed: 'He does not love the unjust'). Verse 43: 'whoever endures patiently and forgives — that is a sign of real resolve' — patience explicitly named (sabr). Disbelief not tagged as disbelievers are not the subject here; the section is addressed to believers.

42:44.notes: Verse 44: transgressors seeing torment, asking to go back — day-of-judgment, hell. 'Whoever Allah leaves astray' — guidance (its absence). Verse 45: exposed to hell, cowering; believers say 'the losers lost themselves on the Day of Resurrection' — day-of-judgment, hell, believers. 'Lasting torment' — hell. Verse 46: no allies, no way out — divine-decree (what God has decreed cannot be averted).

42:47.notes: Verse 47: 'Respond to your Lord' — universal address implying mankind. Day that cannot be turned back — day-of-judgment. Verse 48: 'We did not send you as a guardian' — prophethood-general (the messenger's role defined). 'When We let man taste mercy' — mercy. Verse 49-50: 'To Allah belongs the dominion… He creates whatever He wills… grants daughters… sons… renders sterile' — sovereignty, power, knowledge ('He is Knowledgeable and Capable'). Granting children and rendering sterile touches human-creation and divine-decree over human reproduction.

42:51.notes: Verse 51: modes of divine communication — inspiration, veil, messenger — prophethood-general; 'al-Aliyy al-Hakeem' — knowledge and wisdom. Verse 52: 'We inspired you… You did not know what the Scripture is… We made it a light with which We guide' — the-quran (the scripture described), guidance (explicitly named: 'We guide whomever We will'), prophethood-general. 'You surely guide to a straight path' — direct second-person address to the Prophet about his role — muhammad. The miraculous nature of revelation itself could support miracles.

42:53.notes: Single verse. 'The path of Allah, to whom belongs everything in the heavens and earth' — sovereignty. 'To Allah all matters revert' — tawhid (absolute divine oneness and finality). 'The path of Allah' — guidance (the straight path). Short closing verse; three labels appropriate.

43:1.notes: Ha-Meem opens the surah → disjoined-letters. Verses 2-4 assert the Quran's clarity, its Arabic character, and its sublime wise origin in the Source Book → the-quran, wisdom (hakeem), knowledge.

43:5.notes: The Reminder (Quran) threatened to be withheld → the-quran. Many prophets sent to the ancients → prophethood-general. They ridiculed every messenger → mockery. God destroyed those more powerful → punishment-of-past-nations. Collective of transgressors addressed → disbelievers.

43:9.notes: Polytheists admit God created heavens and earth → creation-of-heavens-earth, creation; 'Mighty, Knower' → knowledge, power. Earth as habitat, paths, rain reviving dead land → natural-signs, provision. Verse 13 contains uttered glorification 'Glory be to Him' (Subhana alladhi) → praise.

43:15.notes: Attributing a portion/offspring to God → shirk, tawhid challenged. Daughters attributed to God → shirk. Angels described as female servants of the Most Gracious → angels. Man described as ungrateful → disbelievers, polytheists as the agents making these claims.

43:20.notes: Excuse of divine will for idol worship → shirk. Following ancestors' religion as justification → denial-of-revelation. Pattern of wealthy rejecting warners → prophethood-general. God's vengeance on the deniers → punishment-of-past-nations.
