43:26.notes: Abraham disavows his father's and people's idols → abraham, shirk. Proclaims monotheism: 'He who created me will guide me' → tawhid, guidance. Makes it an enduring word in his progeny → abraham's legacy.

43:29.notes: God gave enjoyment until the truth and messenger came → prophethood-general, provision. They called it sorcery → denial-of-revelation, sorcery. They objected to the Quran's recipient → the-quran. 'Your Lord's mercy is better than what they amass' → mercy. God allocates livelihoods and ranks → divine-decree.

43:33.notes: God would have given disbelievers silver-roofed houses were it not for mankind becoming one community → mankind, disbelievers. The Hereafter is for the righteous (muttaqeen) → taqwa. The section contrasts worldly ornament with the afterlife reward for the God-conscious.

43:36.notes: Shunning remembrance of the Most Gracious → remembrance (as explicit subject of warning). A devil assigned as companion → iblis. On the Day they will regret their evil companion → day-of-judgment. 'You are partners in the suffering' → hell, disbelievers.

43:40.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet throughout ('Can you make the deaf hear', 'adhere to what is revealed to you', 'It is a message for you') → muhammad. The revealed message as a reminder → the-quran. Messengers before him all opposed polytheism → prophethood-general, tawhid. The blind/deaf unable to be guided → guidance. Disbelievers as subject → disbelievers.

43:46.notes: Moses sent with signs to Pharaoh → moses, pharaoh, prophethood-general. Signs shown → miracles. They laughed at the signs → mockery. Afflicted with plagues → punishment-of-past-nations (precursor to destruction).

43:51.notes: Pharaoh's proclamation of superiority and kingdom → pharaoh, arrogance. He mocks Moses ('miserable wretch') and asks why no angels came → moses, angels. He deceives his people → arrogance. God drowns them all → punishment-of-past-nations.

43:57.notes: Son of Mary cited as example → jesus. He was made an example for Children of Israel → children-of-israel. Angels mentioned as possible successors → angels. 'He is a portent of the Hour' → signs-of-the-hour. Satan as open enemy → iblis. Quraysh's argument about their gods vs. Jesus → shirk, disbelievers.

43:63.notes: Jesus came with clarifications and wisdom → jesus, wisdom. 'Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him' → tawhid. 'Fear Allah' → taqwa (explicitly named). Factions differed → day-of-judgment (painful Day). 'Are they only waiting for the Hour' → signs-of-the-hour.

43:67.notes: Friends become enemies except the righteous (muttaqeen) → taqwa. Direct address 'O My servants' to believers → believers. Entry into the Garden with spouses, golden trays → paradise. The Day described → day-of-judgment.

43:74.notes: Sinners in eternal torment of Hell → hell, disbelievers. 'We did them no injustice' → justice. They cry to Malek (angel-keeper of Hell) → reckoning (accounting for deeds). God's justice asserted explicitly.

43:79.notes: Scheming countered by God's counter-plan → plotting. God hears their secrets, messengers record → knowledge. 'Say: If the Most Gracious had a son…' → qul-statements, tawhid (refuting the claim), shirk. 'Glorified be the Lord of the heavens and the earth' (Subhana) → praise. Leave them until their promised Day → day-of-judgment.

43:84.notes: God is Allah in heaven and earth → tawhid. 'The Wise, the Knower' → wisdom, knowledge. 'Blessed is He' (Tabaraka) → praise. Sovereignty over heavens, earth, and what is between → sovereignty. Knowledge of the Hour belongs to Him alone → signs-of-the-hour, knowledge.

43:86.notes: Idols incapable of intercession → intercession, shirk. Only those with truth and knowledge may intercede → tawhid. They admit God created them → creation. Verse 88 'My Lord, these are a people who do not believe' — attributed to the Prophet addressing God → muhammad (Prophet's lament). Disbelievers as subject throughout.

43:89.notes: Direct command to the Prophet: 'Pardon them, and say, Peace' → muhammad (direct address), qul-statements ('say'). Directed at the disbelievers → disbelievers. Very short single-verse section.

44:1.notes: Section opens with Ḥā-Mīm → disjoined-letters. The Blessed Night revelation → the-quran + divine-decree. 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' → knowledge. 'As mercy from your Lord' → mercy. 'No god but He, He gives life and causes death' → tawhid + death-and-dying. 'Lord of the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty + creation-of-heavens-earth. 'We have been sending messages' → prophethood-general. 'They play around in doubt' → disbelief. 11 labels — within ceiling.

44:10.notes: 'The sky produces a visible smoke enveloping mankind' → mankind + signs-of-the-hour. 'Painful punishment' and 'the Day when We launch the Great Assault' → day-of-judgment + punishment-of-past-nations. 'Our Lord, lift the torment from us, we are believers' — uttered supplication in distress → dua-distress. 'An enlightening messenger has already come to them' → muhammad (direct contextual reference to the Prophet). 'Educated, but crazy!' → denial-of-revelation. 'You will revert' → disbelievers. The dua at v.12 is a voiced supplication even if put in the mouths of those who will revert — it counts as uttered.

44:17.notes: 'People of Pharaoh' → pharaoh. 'A noble messenger came to them' is Moses per context (handing over Allah's servants, clear authority) → moses + prophethood-general. 'I have taken refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me' — uttered refuge-seeking → dua-protection. 'Do not exalt yourselves above Allah' → arrogance. 'Allah's servants' refers to Children of Israel → children-of-israel. The testing and the threat of destruction situate this in the punishment-of-past-nations pattern → punishment-of-past-nations.

44:22.notes: Moses appeals to his Lord ('He appealed to his Lord: These are a sinful people') — uttered appeal in distress → dua-distress. God's commands to cross the sea → moses + miracles (splitting/crossing of sea). Pharaoh's army drowned → pharaoh + punishment-of-past-nations. 'We delivered the Children of Israel' → children-of-israel. 'We chose them knowingly' → knowledge. The gardens and fountains left behind reinforce the punishment narrative.

44:34.notes: 'There is nothing but our first death, and we will not be resurrected' → denial of resurrection → disbelievers + resurrection + denial-of-revelation. 'People of Tubba and those before them — We annihilated them' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'We did not create the heavens and the earth … to play / only for a specific purpose' → creation-of-heavens-earth. The overall thrust is refutation of those who deny the Day → day-of-judgment.

44:40.notes: 'The Day of Sorting Out' → day-of-judgment. 'No friend will avail a friend' → intercession (its absence/limitation). 'Except for him upon whom Allah has mercy; He is the Mighty, the Merciful' → mercy. The Zaqqum tree, boiling bellies, dragged into Hell → hell. 'The righteous … in gardens and springs, dressed in silk … wed to lovely companions … every kind of fruit' → paradise + taqwa (the muttaqun explicitly named at v.51). 'They will not taste death beyond the first death' → death-and-dying. The accounting and sorting → reckoning. 8 labels — within ceiling.

44:58.notes: 'We made it easy in your language' — direct second-person address to the Prophet about the Qur'an → the-quran + muhammad. 'So that they may remember' → guidance (God as source of guidance through the revealed word).

44:59.notes: 'So wait and watch. They too are waiting and watching.' — brief closing verse. 'Wait' contextually refers to the Day of Sorting Out mentioned throughout the surah → day-of-judgment. Direct second-person address ('So wait') to the Prophet → muhammad. Confidence medium because the verse is very short and the eschatological referent is implied from context rather than explicit.

45:1.notes: Ha-Meem opens the section → disjoined-letters. Verse 2 names the Book's revelation → the-quran; attributes 'Exalted in Might, Wise' → power + wisdom. Verses 3–5 enumerate heavenly/earthly proofs for believers → natural-signs, cosmic-bodies (alternation of night/day), human-creation (your own creation), provision (sustenance from sky reviving earth). Addressed to believers explicitly in v3.

45:6.notes: V6 asks what message they will believe after Allah's revelations → denial-of-revelation, the-quran. V8 describes persisting arrogantly → arrogance (istakbara explicitly). V9 taking revelations in mockery → mockery. V10 Hell awaits them → hell. V11 'this is guidance' → guidance. Disbelievers as collective subject throughout.

45:12.notes: V12 sea tamed by God's command → natural-signs, power. 'Seek of His bounty' → provision. 'That you may give thanks' — shukr is explicitly named → gratitude. V13 everything in heavens and earth placed at service → creation-of-heavens-earth. Address is universal (lakum) → mankind.

45:14.notes: V14 opens with 'Tell (qul) those who believe' → qul-statements, believers. Disbelievers implied as the group being forgiven. 'He will fully recompense people' → justice. 'Days of Allah' anticipates judgment → day-of-judgment. V15 'whoever does a good deed / commits evil' — righteous conduct vs. its opposite explicitly framed as the subject → righteous-conduct.

45:16.notes: V16 names Children of Israel as recipients of Book, wisdom, prophecy → children-of-israel, previous-scriptures, prophethood-general, provision. V17 Day of Resurrection will judge their disputes → day-of-judgment. V18 direct second-person address to the Prophet ('We set you upon a pathway') → muhammad. V19 'Allah is the Protector of the righteous (muttaqin)' → taqwa. V20 'illumination for mankind, guidance, and mercy' → mankind, guidance, mercy.

45:21.notes: V21 contrasts evil-doers with believers and those who do righteous deeds → believers, disbelievers. V22 'Allah created the heavens and the earth with justice, so every soul will be repaid' → creation-of-heavens-earth, justice. V23 one who takes his desire as his god → shirk (substituting desire for God); God seals his hearing/heart → divine-decree (God's knowing decree of misguidance as consequence). Disbelief implicit throughout.

45:24.notes: V24 materialist denial of afterlife → denial-of-revelation, death-and-dying. V25 rejecting revelations → denial-of-revelation. V26 'Say (qul), Allah gives you life then makes you die then gathers you for the Day of Resurrection' → qul-statements, death-and-dying, resurrection, day-of-judgment, power. 'Most people do not know' → knowledge (God's knowledge contrasted with human ignorance).

45:27.notes: V27 'To Allah belongs the kingship of the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. Hour/falsifiers → day-of-judgment. V28 every community called to its Book → reckoning. V29 Book speaks in truth → reckoning. V30 believers admitted into His mercy → paradise, mercy, believers. V31 disbelievers rebuked: 'you turned arrogant' → arrogance, disbelievers, disbelief, hell (implied by context of punishment). V32 denial of the Hour → denial-of-revelation fits but section already has it implicitly — tagging day-of-judgment covers it.

45:33.notes: V33 'the very thing they ridiculed will haunt them' → mockery. V34 'Today We forget you … your abode is the Fire' → hell, day-of-judgment. V35 'you took Allah's revelations for a joke' → mockery, denial-of-revelation. No escape, no repentance → reckoning. Disbelievers as subject throughout.

45:36.notes: V36 'Fali-llahi-l-hamd' — explicit utterance of al-hamd → praise. 'Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth' → sovereignty, creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Lord of humanity' → mankind.

45:37.notes: V37 'To Him belongs all supremacy in the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. 'He is the Majestic' (al-Aziz) → power. 'the Wise' (al-Hakim) → wisdom. Short closing verse; three divine attribute labels are appropriate.

46:1.notes: Section opens with Ḥā-Mīm → disjoined-letters. 'The Honorable, the Wise' → wisdom (and implicitly sovereignty/power). Creation of heavens and earth invoked to challenge idols. Qul in v.4.

46:7.notes: v.7 — 'this is obviously magic' → denial-of-revelation + sorcery. v.8 — 'He is the Forgiver, the Merciful' → mercy. v.9 — 'I am not different from the other messengers' → prophethood-general. v.10 — a witness from Children of Israel mentioned; 'you turned arrogant' → arrogance. Multiple Qul commands present.

46:11.notes: v.12 — 'the Book of Moses' explicitly named → moses + previous-scriptures. v.14 — 'inhabitants of Paradise' → paradise. Guidance theme in v.12 ('to warn... and good news') makes guidance a concrete subject. No uttered du'a.

46:15.notes: v.15 contains an uttered supplication: 'Lord, enable me to appreciate the blessings... and to act with righteousness... and improve my children for me. I have sincerely repented to You.' This covers dua-gratitude (thanking for blessings on self and parents), dua-family-offspring (asking for children's improvement), and repentance (explicitly stated). Righteousness is the explicit subject of the request → righteous-conduct trigger met. v.15–16 addresses mankind generically re: parents. v.16 — paradise promised to these.

46:17.notes: v.17 — son rejects parents and resurrection → disbelief + arrogance (explicit: 'unjust arrogance' in v.20). v.18 — communities of jinn and humans doomed → jinn. v.19 — degrees of reckoning → reckoning. v.20 — paraded before Fire → hell + day-of-judgment. Marriage-and-family: the parent-child relationship is the explicit setting. 'Arrogance' is explicitly named in v.20.

46:21.notes: v.21 — 'brother of Aad' = Hud → hud + ad. Warning of a 'tremendous Day' → day-of-judgment. v.22 — people challenge to bring the punishment. v.23 — 'knowledge is only with Allah' → knowledge. v.24–25 — the wind destroying everything → natural-signs (wind as punishment) + punishment-of-past-nations. Shirk: their worship of gods is the explicit issue.

46:26.notes: Continuation of the 'Ad narrative contextually, now generalizing to all destroyed townships. v.26 — 'they disregarded the revelations of Allah' → denial-of-revelation; 'what they used to ridicule' → mockery. v.27 — destroyed townships around you → previous-creations-destroyed + punishment-of-past-nations. v.28 — idols abandoned them → shirk. The ad label applies as the 'Ad narrative directly continues from 46:21.

46:29.notes: v.29 — jinn listen to the Quran → jinn + the-quran. v.30 — 'sent down after Moses, confirming what came before' → moses + prophethood-general. 'Guides to the truth and to a straight path' → guidance. v.31 — 'He will forgive you your sins' → mercy (forgiveness). v.32 — those who do not answer are in error → disbelief.

46:33.notes: v.33 — creation of heavens and earth as argument for power to resurrect → creation-of-heavens-earth + power + resurrection. 'He is Capable of everything' → power. v.34 — disbelievers presented to the Fire → hell + day-of-judgment implicitly; disbelief explicitly named as the cause of punishment.

46:35.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('So be patient... and do not be hasty regarding them') → muhammad. 'Be patient as the messengers with resolve were patient' — patience is the explicit subject and command → patience. 'Messengers with resolve' → prophethood-general. Day when they see what they are promised → day-of-judgment. 'Will any be destroyed except the sinful people' → disbelievers.

47:1.notes: Muhammad is named explicitly in verse 2 ('sent down to Muhammad') — this triggers the people label per rule 3. 'Guidance' is invoked as the content of what was revealed (the truth from their Lord) and as the basis of contrast between the two groups — concrete trigger met.

47:4.notes: 'Patience'/'steadfast' not named here; removing. War conduct explicitly legislated (strike, bind, release/ransom) → war-and-treaties and manumission-and-captives. Paradise promised to the slain. Divine testing → divine-decree. 'Those who are killed in the way of Allah… admitted into Paradise' — believers and paradise clearly present.

47:8.notes: Verse 13 references 'your town which evicted you' — direct address to the Prophet, justifying the muhammad tag. Verse 10 invokes the ruins-of-past-nations motif → punishment-of-past-nations and previous-creations-destroyed. Verse 12: gardens with rivers → paradise; fire → hell. Verse 9: hated what Allah revealed → denial-of-revelation.

47:14.notes: Verse 15 describes paradise in detail for the muttaqun → paradise and taqwa (explicitly named). Contrasted with those in the Fire → hell. The opening contrast between one on evidence from his Lord vs. one following desires → believers vs. disbelievers.

47:16.notes: Verse 16 describes those listening to the Prophet then feigning ignorance → hypocrites and muhammad (direct second-person address implied). Verse 17: 'He increases them in guidance' → guidance; 'granted them their taqwa' → taqwa (explicitly named). Verse 18: the Hour coming suddenly, its tokens → signs-of-the-hour. Verse 19: 'no god but Allah' → tawhid; 'Allah knows your movements' → knowledge. Verse 19 also contains the command 'ask forgiveness for your sin' — addressed to the Prophet, direct second-person → muhammad confirmed.

47:20.notes: Verse 20: those with sickness in hearts (hypocrites) recoil at fighting commands in a surah → the-quran and war-and-treaties. Verse 22: 'make mischief on earth' explicitly names fasad → corruption-on-earth. Verse 24: 'will they not ponder the Quran?' → the-quran. Verse 25: Satan has enticed them → iblis. Verse 26: 'Allah knows their secret thoughts' → knowledge.

47:27.notes: Angels taking the souls of the hypocrites at death, striking them → angels and death-and-dying. The cause is their pursuit of what displeases Allah → disbelief. Short section (2 verses) — 4 labels appropriate.

47:29.notes: Verse 29: Allah exposing the malice of those with sick hearts (hypocrites). Verse 30: 'you would recognize them' — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad. Verse 31: 'those who strive and those who are steadfast (al-sabireen)' — patience (sabr) explicitly named. Verse 32: disbelievers opposing the Messenger → disbelievers. Verse 33: direct address 'O you who believe' → believers. Verse 30: 'Allah knows your actions' → knowledge.

47:35.notes: Verse 35: instruction not to call for peace from weakness during war → war-and-treaties; addressed to believers. Verse 36: 'if you have faith and lead a righteous life' (taqwa explicitly invoked) → taqwa. The worldly life described as play and pastime — disbelief in prioritizing it is the contrast. Short section.

47:38.notes: Verse 38: call to spend in Allah's cause; some withhold — greed-and-miserliness explicitly triggered ('whoever withholds'). Spending in God's cause → zakat-and-charity. 'Allah is the Rich (al-Ghani) while you are the needy' → provision (God as self-sufficient provider). Direct address to believers.

48:1.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: 'praise' (the morning/evening glorification in v.9 is commanded rather than uttered, borderline — weakest claim); 'prophethood-general' (could be seen as subsumed by the direct address to Muhammad). Section opens with the Fath announcement addressed directly to the Prophet, covers believers entering paradise, hypocrites/polytheists punished in hell, and closes with the prophetic role as witness/bearer of good news/warner.

48:10.notes: The bay'ah (pledge of allegiance) passage; hypocrites exposed by saying with tongues what is not in hearts; closing formula 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy; 'To Allah belongs the kingdom' → sovereignty; 'Allah is Informed' → knowledge.

48:15.notes: The laggards wanting to join for spoils; 'they want to change the Word of Allah' → denial-of-revelation; 'you are jealous of us' → envy (explicitly named); contains 'Say' (qul) → qul-statements.

48:16.notes: Direct 'Say' command to Desert-Arabs who lagged behind about future fighting; reward/punishment contrast with paradise (gardens) and painful punishment.

48:18.notes: Bay'ah under the tree (Ridwan); Allah pleased with believers, sent serenity, rewarded with imminent conquest; 'Allah is Capable of everything' → power; 'guide you on a straight path' → guidance; 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' → wisdom; knowledge invoked ('He knew what was in their hearts', 'Allah has encompassed them').

48:22.notes: Covers Hudaybiyyah restraint, the Sacred Mosque being barred, Allah's pattern (sunna) never changing, serenity sent down, and 'the words of righteousness (taqwa)' explicitly named in v.26 → taqwa trigger met; 'Allah admits into His mercy whomever He wills' → mercy; 'Allah is aware of everything' → knowledge.

48:27.notes: The vision of entering the Sacred Mosque fulfilled; shaving/cutting of hair → hajj-and-pilgrimage context; 'He knew what you did not know' → knowledge; 'sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth' → guidance + prophethood-general; 'imminent victory' is divine decree fulfillment → divine-decree.

48:29.notes: Opens with 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah' — explicit naming → muhammad; describes companions in prostration/ruku → prayer; 'compassionate amongst themselves' → mercy attribute of believers; their description in the Torah and Gospel → previous-scriptures; 'believe and do good deeds' → righteous-conduct (explicitly named as a category here); prophethood affirmed.

49:1.notes: Direct address to believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū) multiple times. The Prophet is addressed in verse 4 ('those who call you from behind the chambers') — direct second-person address to Muhammad. Taqwa explicitly named ('fear Allah', 'tested for piety'). Closing formula 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge. Lowering voices before the Prophet is the explicit subject of humility-adjacent instruction; however, the section explicitly names the disposition of lowering voices as taqwa-tested, so taqwa is the stronger concept trigger here.

49:6.notes: Direct address to believers. Instruction to investigate/verify news → justice-and-witness (bearing witness, just judgment). 'Allah has given you the love of faith' → guidance (God as source of guidance). Closing 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' → knowledge and wisdom. Verse 7 mentions the Messenger of Allah among them but this is descriptive context, not direct address to Muhammad.

49:9.notes: Direct address to believers. Rules for reconciliation between fighting Muslim factions → war-and-treaties. 'Reconcile with justice, be equitable; Allah loves the equitable' → justice (divine attribute). Taqwa explicitly named ('remain conscious of Allah'). 'That you may receive mercy' → mercy.

49:11.notes: Verses 11–12 open with direct address to believers; verse 13 shifts to yā ayyuhā an-nās → mankind. Mockery explicitly prohibited → mockery. Slander and backbiting explicitly named ('slander one another', 'insult with names', 'backbite') → slander-and-backbiting. Taqwa explicitly named ('remain mindful of Allah'). Repentance explicitly named ('whoever does not repent'). Closing 'Allah is Most Relenting, Most Merciful' → mercy. 'Allah is All-Knowing, Well-Experienced' → knowledge. Verse 13 'We created you from a male and female' → human-creation.

49:14.notes: Multiple 'Say:' (qul) imperatives in verses 14, 16, 17 → qul-statements. The Desert-Arabs' superficial faith vs. true belief distinction → sincerity is explicitly the subject ('these are the sincere', 'if you are sincere'). 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. 'Allah knows everything in the heavens and earth' → knowledge. 'Allah has done you a favor by guiding you to the faith' → guidance. Disbelievers/hypocrites-adjacent — the Desert-Arabs who claim belief without it entering their hearts are addressed as a group distinct from true believers.

49:18.notes: Single verse asserting God's knowledge of the unseen in heavens and earth, and His sight over all deeds. Pure divine-attribute statement. No named figures, no addressed group, no du'a, no other themes present.

50:1.notes: 15 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: 'provision' (sustenance is mentioned but secondary to the resurrection argument); 'natural-signs' could be subsumed under 'creation-of-heavens-earth' though both genuinely apply (sky, earth, rain, palms); 'resurrection' is the core argument for which the natural signs serve as evidence. Named peoples: Noah, Thamud, 'Ad, Pharaoh, Lot's brethren, plus 'dwellers of the Woods' (Madyan/Shuayb's people) and 'people of Tubba' — tagging madyan is borderline as 'Dwellers of the Woods' is not always equated with Madyan; omitted. All five explicitly named nations/figures tagged.

50:15.notes: The two recording angels seated right and left are tagged under 'angels'. God's nearness 'closer than the jugular vein' is a direct invocation of nearness. The daze of death closing the section earns 'death-and-dying'. The opening challenge 'Were We fatigued by the first creation?' asserts 'power' (omnipotence over creation/resurrection).

50:20.notes: The Trumpet blown opens the Day of Judgment scene. Hell is described directly (v24, v30). Paradise brought near for the pious (v31). Shirk explicitly named: 'who fabricated another god with Allah' (v26). Justice asserted: 'I am not unjust to the servants' (v29). Taqwa triggered explicitly: 'Paradise will be brought closer to the pious' (v31, muttaqin). Repentance triggered explicitly: 'every careful penitent … came with a repentant heart' (v32–33).

50:36.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet throughout ('So endure what they say', 'And listen', v39–41) warrants 'muhammad'. 'Proclaim the praises of your Lord … glorify Him' is a command for prayer and glorification; 'praise' applies as the section utters the command to glorify (subbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbika). 'Creation of heavens and earth in six days' (v38) earns 'creation-of-heavens-earth'. 'We control life and death' (v43) earns 'death-and-dying'. The Day of Emergence/gathering in vv41–44 earns 'day-of-judgment' and 'resurrection'.

50:45.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('you are not a dictator over them') earns 'muhammad'. 'Remind by the Quran' makes the Quran the explicit subject. 'We are fully aware' asserts divine knowledge. 'Whoever fears My warning' invokes taqwa as explicit subject (fear/wariness of God's threat).

51:1.notes: Opening oath-series (spreading winds, cloud-bearing, sailing ships, distributing angels) invokes both natural-signs and cosmic-bodies. Verses 13–14 describe disbelievers being presented to the Fire. Verses 15–16 describe the pious (muttaqin) in gardens and springs — paradise. Verse 17 mentions night prayer, verse 18 dawn istighfar (described, not uttered, so prayer not dua-forgiveness), verse 19 charity to the beggar — zakat-and-charity. Verses 20–23 cite earthly and heavenly ayat as signs — natural-signs and provision. Taqwa triggered by explicit 'muttaqin' (v.15). 11 labels — within ceiling.

51:24.notes: Verses 24–30: Abraham's angelic guests; announcement of a knowledgeable boy (Isaac implied per tafsir); 'He is the Wise, the Knowing' — wisdom and knowledge (v.30). Verses 31–37: angels sent to Lot's people — punishment-of-past-nations; rocks of clay unleashed; believers evacuated (v.35–36) — believers and disbelievers. Lot is not named explicitly here but the referent 'people guilty of sin' and 'rocks of clay' are unmistakably Lot's people per context and tafsir; tagging lot (medium confidence on lot label alone). Isaac is not named but 'knowledgeable boy' announced to Abraham — tafsir identifies as Isaac; keeping medium on isaac tag.

51:38.notes: Verses 38–40: Moses sent to Pharaoh with clear authority; Pharaoh calls him sorcerer/madman (denial-of-revelation); Pharaoh and troops thrown into the sea — punishment-of-past-nations. Verses 41–42: 'Ad destroyed by devastating wind. Verses 43–45: Thamud defied their Lord, struck by lightning. Verse 46: people of Noah mentioned. Verses 47–48: heaven constructed with power, earth spread — creation-of-heavens-earth and power. Verse 49: all things created in pairs — natural-signs. 11 labels — within ceiling.

51:50.notes: Verse 50: 'flee towards Allah, I am a clear warner' — prophethood-general; direct first-person speech of the prophet as warner addressed to people. Verse 51: 'do not set up any other god with Allah' — explicit tawhid and shirk warning. Verse 52: past messengers called sorcerer/madman — denial-of-revelation. Verse 54: 'turn away from them; you are not to blame' — direct address to the Prophet (second person singular 'you') — muhammad. Verse 55: 'the reminder benefits the believers' — remembrance (dhikr explicitly named: 'dhikra'), believers. 8 labels.

51:56.notes: Verse 56: 'I did not create the jinn and the humans except to worship Me' — jinn and mankind (humans as category), creation. Verse 57: God needs no provision from them — provision (negated, but the attribute ar-Razzaq is the substantive claim). Verse 58: 'Allah is the Provider, the One with Power, the Strong' — explicit divine attributes provision and power. Verse 59: wrongdoers will have their turn like their counterparts — punishment-of-past-nations (reference to prior destroyed peoples) and disbelievers. 7 labels.

51:60.notes: Single verse: woe to disbelievers because of their promised Day — disbelievers and day-of-judgment. Minimal section, 2 labels appropriate.

52:1.notes: The surah opens with a series of oaths (the Mount, the inscribed Book, the frequented House, the elevated roof, the seething sea) before asserting the inevitability of punishment. The 'Book inscribed in a published scroll' is a reference to either the Quran or a heavenly record; tagged the-quran on the strength of the revealed-book oath. The deniers being shoved into Hell and the day of cosmic upheaval (heaven swaying, mountains in motion) firmly anchor day-of-judgment, hell, signs-of-the-hour, and cosmic-bodies (heaven/mountains as cosmic phenomena). The taunt 'Is this magic?' maps to denial-of-revelation.

52:17.notes: The section describes the reward of the muttaqun (explicitly named — 'the righteous') in Paradise: gardens, bliss, food, drink, spouses (hur), serving youths, reunion with believing offspring. Taqwa is explicitly triggered by 'al-muttaqin'. Mercy is anchored in 'He is the Good, the Compassionate' (closing formula, verse 28) and 'Allah blessed us'. Provision covers the food, fruit, meat, and drink supplied to them. Marriage-and-family is warranted by the coupling with spouses and the reunion of believing families/offspring (v.21). The believers' dialogue about fearing for their families and being spared also supports these tags.

52:29.notes: This section is addressed directly to the Prophet ('By the grace of your Lord, you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman'; 'Or do you demand a payment from them') — direct second-person address to him personally, warranting the muhammad label alongside qul-statements (v.31 'Say...'). The disbelievers' accusations (soothsayer, madman, poet, fabricator) map to denial-of-revelation. The challenge 'let them produce a discourse like it' maps to challenge-to-produce. The rhetorical questions about creation of heavens and earth (v.36), creation from nothing (v.35), treasuries of the Lord (v.37), and daughters vs. sons for God (v.39 — a shirk refutation) yield creation, sovereignty, knowledge, tawhid, and shirk. The closing 'Allah transcends what they associate' (Subhan Allah) explicitly anchors tawhid and shirk.

52:44.notes: The section addresses the stubbornness of disbelievers (even falling sky-lumps dismissed as clouds), their coming Day when ploys avail nothing, and a worldly punishment besides the Final one. The direct address to the Prophet in v.48 ('patiently await the decision of your Lord, for you are before Our Eyes') is substantive second-person address to him — muhammad applies. Patience is explicitly named ('patiently await'). The command 'proclaim the praises of your Lord when you arise' — though a command rather than an uttered praise — contains 'bi-hamdi rabbik' which is close to praise being uttered/named; tagged praise as the act of praising is explicitly named as the subject of the instruction.

52:49.notes: A single verse commanding glorification of God at night and at the receding of the stars. Prayer/tasbeeh at specific times (night, star-receding) maps to prayer. The stars as a temporal marker map to cosmic-bodies. The act of glorification (tasbih) maps to praise.

53:1.notes: Section covers the divine oath by the star, the defense of the Prophet's truthfulness and non-erring nature, revelation brought by Gabriel (the Extremely Powerful / the one of vigor), the two sightings — including the Sidrat al-Muntaha and the Garden of Repose — and 'the Great Signs of his Lord.' Muhammad is directly addressed in context ('your friend') and the section is substantively about him and the revelation he receives. Angels tag for Gabriel as the revealer. The Sidrat al-Muntaha/Garden of Repose reference earns `paradise`. The star oath opens the surah as a cosmic-body image. `power` for 'Extremely Powerful.' `knowledge` for the complete revelation transmitted without error.

53:19.notes: Section refutes the Meccan goddesses al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat as mere invented names — a direct shirk rebuttal. Polytheists are the addressees. `angels` because the section explicitly discusses the naming of angels as females and the limits of angelic intercession (v26–28). `intercession` for v26. `sovereignty` for 'To Allah belong the Last and the First' and 'To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and on earth.' `knowledge` for God knowing best who strayed and who is guided (v30) and 'He knows you well' (v32). `reckoning` for v31 (rewarding evil and good deeds). `guidance` explicitly named in v23 ('guidance has come to them from their Lord') and v30. `human-creation` for v32 ('He created you from the earth … embryos in your mothers' wombs').

53:33.notes: Section references the Scrolls of Moses (v36) and Abraham who fulfilled (v37) — both named figures tagged. `previous-scriptures` for the Scrolls of Moses. Core theological declarations: individual moral accountability (v38–39), deeds witnessed and rewarded (v40–41) → `reckoning`; the next existence (v47) → `resurrection`; God gives death and life (v44) → `death-and-dying` not added as section focuses on resurrection/reckoning context; human creation from sperm drop (v46) → `human-creation`; enriches and impoverishes (v48) → `provision`; Lord of Sirius (v49) → cosmic-body claim supporting `power`. Destroyed peoples: 'Ad (v50) → `ad`; Thamud (v51) → `thamud`; people of Noah (v52) → `noah`; 'the ruined cities' (v53–54, tafsir: Lot's people) → `lot`; all collectively → `punishment-of-past-nations`.

53:56.notes: V56: 'This is a warning, just like the first warnings' — `prophethood-general` (the Qur'an/Prophet as one in a line of warners). V57–58: 'The inevitable is imminent; none besides Allah can unveil it' — `signs-of-the-hour` and `day-of-judgment`. V59–61: The disbelievers marvel, laugh, and are lost in frivolity — `disbelievers` and `mockery` (laughing at the discourse / the warner).

53:62.notes: A single verse commanding prostration and worship of Allah alone. `tawhid` for the exclusive direction of worship to Allah. `praise` for the prostration-and-worship command framed as an act of glorification (this is a sajdah verse — the uttered/commanded act of bowing to God). Note: rule 5 applies — no concept labels triggered beyond what is explicitly named. The verse is brief but self-contained as a worshipful directive.

54:1.notes: The splitting of the moon is a named miracle and a sign of the approaching Hour. 'The Hour has drawn near' directly invokes eschatological imminence.

54:2.notes: Verses 2–5 describe the disbelievers calling the miracle 'continuous magic' (denial/sorcery label triggered by explicit accusation). Verses 6–8 describe the Day of Resurrection — graves opening, scrambling toward the Caller. 'Profound wisdom' in v.5 names wisdom explicitly.

54:9.notes: 'So he appealed to his Lord, I am overwhelmed, so help me' is an uttered supplication → dua-distress. The flood narrative involves God opening heavens and bursting earth with springs → natural-signs and power. 'We made the Quran easy to learn' in v.17 → the-quran. 'A purpose already destined' → divine-decree.

54:18.notes: 'Ad denied the truth; a screaming wind was unleashed — explicit punishment narrative. 'We made the Quran easy to remember' → the-quran. The wind as a natural destructive force → natural-signs.

54:23.notes: Thamud rejected warnings and called the prophet a liar → denial-of-revelation and mockery. The she-camel sent as a test → miracles (a sign given to Salih). Salih is the prophet of Thamud, so tagged even though not named by name — however, the she-camel is his specific sign and 'be patient' is addressed to him (the messenger), making his presence implicit. Confidence remains high. 'A purpose already destined' context from the broader narrative → divine-decree for the water division decree. 'We made the Quran easy to understand' → the-quran.

54:33.notes: Lot's people rejected warnings → denial-of-revelation and punishment. The family of Lot was saved as 'a blessing from Us' → mercy. 'Thus We reward the thankful' explicitly names gratitude (shukr) as the concept → gratitude label triggered. 'We made the Quran easy to memorize' → the-quran.

54:41.notes: 'The seizure of an Almighty Omnipotent' — both power and sovereignty invoked as divine attributes in the closing formula. Pharaoh's people rejected all signs → denial-of-revelation.

54:43.notes: 'Do you have immunity in the scriptures' references prior scriptures → previous-scriptures. The Hour as their appointed time → day-of-judgment. 'Dragged upon their faces into the Fire' → hell. 'Everything We created is precisely measured' → divine-decree. 'Our command is but once' → power. 'We have destroyed your likes' → punishment-of-past-nations.

54:52.notes: 'Everything they have done is in the Books / everything small or large is written down' → reckoning (the recording of deeds). 'The righteous (muttaqin) will be amidst gardens and rivers' → paradise and taqwa (the muttaqin are named explicitly as the subject).

54:55.notes: 'In an assembly of virtue, in the presence of an Omnipotent King' — paradise described; 'Omnipotent King' invokes both sovereignty and power as divine attributes.

55:1.notes: The surah opens with 'Ar-Rahman' (The Compassionate) — a direct invocation of the mercy attribute. Verses 2–4 assert God taught the Quran, created man, and taught him expression — covering revelation, human creation, and divine knowledge.

55:5.notes: Sun and moon moving by plan → cosmic-bodies. Stars and trees prostrating, sky raised → natural-signs and creation-of-heavens-earth. The balance/mizan established by God → sovereignty. The explicit command to maintain weights with justice → justice (divine attribute) and justice-and-witness (worldly injunction against violating the balance in trade/conduct).

55:10.notes: Earth spread out for creatures, fruits, palms, grains, fragrant plants — classic provision and natural-signs passage. 'For the creatures' addresses all living beings broadly, including mankind.

55:14.notes: Man created from hard clay, jinn from a fusion of fire — explicit parallel creation accounts for both human and jinn. Both groups are addressed by the refrain 'which of your Lord's marvels will you deny?' confirming jinn and mankind as dual addressees.

55:17.notes: Lord of the two Easts and Wests → sovereignty over cosmic directions. Two seas merged with a barrier between them → natural-signs / creation-of-heavens-earth. Pearls and coral emerging from the seas → provision. The refrain addresses both jinn and mankind throughout.

55:24.notes: Ships raised on the sea belonging to God → sovereignty and power over creation. 'Everyone upon it is perishing' — explicit statement of death and mortality → death-and-dying. 'The Presence of your Lord remains, Full of Majesty and Splendor' asserts divine sovereignty and permanence. Ships as provision/means of livelihood is implicit but secondary; the primary themes are God's ownership and the transience of all creatures.

55:29.notes: 'Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him; every day He is managing' → nearness-and-response and sovereignty/power. 'We will attend to you, O prominent two' (the two burdens = jinn and mankind) introduces eschatological reckoning. Direct address to 'the society of jinn and humans' — both people labels apply. The passage transitions toward the Day when God will settle accounts.

55:35.notes: Flares of fire and brass, sky splitting apart, Day when no one is questioned about sins — all eschatological. Both jinn and mankind are addressed throughout.

55:41.notes: The guilty recognized by their marks, seized by forelocks and feet → reckoning on the Day. 'This is Hell that the guilty denied' → explicit hell description. The guilty (mujrimun) who denied are disbelievers. Both jinn and mankind are implicitly addressed per the sustained dual refrain of the surah.

55:46.notes: 'For him who feared the standing of his Lord' → taqwa as the explicit qualifier for paradise. Two gardens with varieties, flowing springs, fruits of every kind → paradise description. The dual addressees (jinn and mankind) continue. Those who feared their Lord → believers/taqwa-possessors.

55:54.notes: Reclining on brocade-lined furnishings, fruits near at hand, maidens restrained in gaze untouched by man or jinn → detailed paradise description. 'Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?' (v.60) — the word ihsan (goodness/righteous conduct) is explicitly named as the basis for reward, triggering righteous-conduct. Confidence medium on righteous-conduct since ihsan can be read as a general rhetorical statement rather than an instruction, but the explicit naming of the concept meets rule 5's concrete trigger test.

55:62.notes: Two additional gardens below the first pair — deep green, gushing springs, fruits/date-palms/pomegranates, good and beautiful companions untouched by human or jinn. Extended paradise description for the second tier of gardens. Dual addressees (jinn and mankind) maintained by the refrain throughout.

55:76.notes: Reclining on green cushions and exquisite carpets — continuation of paradise description, closing the garden passages before the final doxology.

55:78.notes: 'Tabāraka-smu rabbika dhī al-jalāli wa-l-ikrām' — 'Blessed be the name of your Lord, Full of Majesty and Splendor.' This is an explicit tabaraka formula → praise (uttered praise). 'Full of Majesty and Splendor' asserts sovereignty. Closing doxology of the surah.

56:1.notes: Section covers the cosmic shock of the Day, the division of humanity into three groups, and the rewards of the forerunners in Paradise. 'Those on the Right' and 'those on the Left' are introduced but elaborated in subsequent sections; forerunners' paradise is described in detail here.

56:27.notes: Describes the rewards of the People of the Right: lush gardens, food, water, shade, and specially created companions. 'We have created them of special creation' triggers human-creation. Provision applies to the abundance of fruit, water, and sustenance described.

56:41.notes: Describes the fate of the People of the Left: hellfire, boiling water, bitter tree of Zaqqum. Verse 47–48 quotes their denial of resurrection; verse 49 has 'Say,' triggering qul-statements. Day of Retribution named explicitly in v56.

56:57.notes: Series of rhetorical questions about human reproduction, agriculture, water, and fire as divine signs. v57 addresses 'you' universally (mankind). 'We have decreed death' triggers death-and-dying. v70 'Will you not be thankful?' names gratitude explicitly as the expected response. v74 'glorify the Name of your Great Lord' is a command to glorify, not an uttered praise, so praise label withheld. Power and creation both apply as God asserts Himself as the true Creator/Grower/Sender.

56:75.notes: Opens with an oath by the positions of the stars (cosmic-bodies). Asserts the noble Quran and its divine origin (the-quran). v81–82 addresses those who deny it (denial-of-revelation, disbelievers). v83–87 describes the moment of death and God's nearness (death-and-dying, nearness-and-response). v88–94 reiterates the three-group destiny — forerunners/paradise, right/paradise, deniers/hell — tying back to section-opening themes.

56:95.notes: Two-verse closing affirmation: 'This is the certain truth' confirms the Quran's truthfulness. 'Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Magnificent' — though a command, the formula subḥān/glorify is uttered as a closing declaration in the text itself, paralleling the same closing in v74. Borderline on praise; tagged because the glorification formula is present as a direct utterance-command framing the close of the surah.

57:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'Glorifying Allah' (sabbaha) — an uttered/asserted glorification formula, warranting 'praise'. Attributes named: Almighty/Wise (wisdom), power over all things (power), sovereignty (mulk), knowledge of all things (knowledge), created heavens and earth in six days (creation-of-heavens-earth). Merging of night and day (v6) adds cosmic-bodies. No named figures, no du'a, no eschatology.

57:7.notes: Verse 7 addresses believers directly (implicit). V8 mentions the pledge/covenant God took. V9 describes sending clear revelations to bring out of darkness into light — guidance. Closing formula 'Gentle, Most Compassionate' → mercy; 'Well Experienced' → knowledge. V10 mentions those who contributed and fought before the conquest vs. after — war-and-treaties and migration are borderline; the verse contrasts pre- and post-Fath contributors, implying both fighting and migration context. Guidance triggered by 'bring you out of darkness into the light' (v9). Covenant triggered by 'He has received a pledge from you' (v8). Migration is medium confidence — referenced implicitly through the conquest/pre-conquest distinction rather than named explicitly.

57:11.notes: V11 invites charitable spending (zakat-and-charity). V12 describes believing men and women on the Day with their light and gardens (paradise, day-of-judgment, believers). V13 depicts hypocrites on the Day separated from believers by a wall (hypocrites, day-of-judgment). V14 recounts the hypocrites' self-deception and 'arrogance deceived you' — the word arrogance appears in translation ('arrogance deceived you regarding Allah') but it is attributed to the Deceiver/Satan deceiving them rather than as their named character trait; not tagging arrogance as a label for the hypocrites. V15 says no ransom accepted, the Fire is their refuge (hell, disbelievers, disbelief). Mercy not directly named in closing formula but 'within it is mercy' (v13) — tag mercy.

57:16.notes: V16 addresses believers, exhorts their hearts to soften to dhikr (remembrance), and warns against being like those given the Book before (people-of-the-book). V17 natural rain/revival of earth metaphor (natural-signs). V18 charitable men and women — zakat-and-charity. V19 sincere believers and witnesses contrasted with disbelievers who deny (sincerity, disbelievers, disbelief, hell). V20 worldly life as vanity; hereafter has agony and forgiveness (mercy, hell). V21 race to forgiveness and paradise (paradise, mercy). 11 labels — within ceiling.

57:22.notes: V22–23 address divine decree — everything written before it happens (divine-decree); God's knowledge underlies this (knowledge). V23 warns against pride/boasting but 'proud snob' is a passing descriptor, not the section's explicit subject — not tagging arrogance. V24 explicitly names stinginess and those who induce others to be stingy — greed-and-miserliness. Closing of v24 'Allah is the Independent, the Praiseworthy' — no separate attribute label fits precisely; 'the Praiseworthy' is a divine name but maps closest to sovereignty/praise; not forcing. V25 sent messengers with proofs, Book and Balance for justice among people (prophethood-general, justice); 'humanity' (an-nas) named as the beneficiary (mankind); 'Allah is Strong and Powerful' → power. Previous-scriptures borderline for V25 'sent down the Book' but prophethood-general covers the sending of messengers with scripture adequately.

57:26.notes: V26 names Noah and Abraham and establishes prophethood and scripture in their line (noah, abraham, prophethood-general, previous-scriptures). V27 names Jesus son of Mary explicitly (jesus, mary), gives the Gospel (previous-scriptures), instills compassion and mercy in followers' hearts (mercy). V28 opens 'O you who believe' (believers) with explicit command to fear Allah — taqwa is explicitly named ('fear Allah', ittaqu — the taqwa root). Closing formula 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy already tagged.

57:29.notes: Single verse. Explicitly addresses People of the Book (people-of-the-book). States that all grace/fadl is in Allah's hand and He gives it to whom He wills — sovereignty. 'Allah is Possessor of Great Grace' — grace/fadl maps to mercy/provision; sovereignty covers the 'in His hand' claim; mercy covers the grace attribute. Provision also applicable ('He gives it to whomever He wills') but sovereignty and mercy together capture the substance adequately.

58:1.notes: Section covers the zihar divorce formula and its expiation (freeing slave, fasting, feeding needy), followed by warning to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, closing with the Day of Resurrection and reckoning. Allah's attributes: Hearing/Seeing (knowledge), Pardoning/Forgiving (mercy), Knower/Aware (knowledge). 'Muhammad' tagged because verse 1 directly addresses him ('she who argued with you'). Verse 4 mentions 'unbelievers will have a painful punishment' -> disbelievers.

58:7.notes: Verse 7 asserts Allah's omniscience — He is with every secret gathering wherever they are, and will inform them on the Day of Resurrection. Verse 8 describes those who were prohibited from secret conspiracy but reverted to it, conspiring in sin and defiance of the Messenger, greeting the Prophet with a subversive greeting — characteristic of the hypocrites. Hell is mentioned as their destination.

58:9.notes: Direct address to believers ('O you who believe') instructing them not to converse in sin and aggression but in virtue and piety (taqwa explicitly named). Verse 10 names Satan as the source of secret conspiracy and instructs believers to put their trust in Allah (tawakkul explicitly invoked: 'let the believers put their trust in Allah').

58:11.notes: Verse 11 addresses believers about conduct in gatherings; Allah elevates those of knowledge. Verse 12 instructs believers to offer charity before private consultation with the Messenger — direct address involving Muhammad. Closing formula 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' -> mercy. Allah's attribute 'Aware' -> knowledge. Charity (sadaqah) explicitly commanded -> zakat-and-charity. Righteous-conduct tagged because the section is structured as an explicit instruction in social/ethical conduct.

58:13.notes: Single verse abrogating the prior charity-before-consultation requirement; instructs believers to establish prayer and give zakat and obey Allah and His Messenger. Repentance tagged because 'Allah pardons you' (taba Allahu 'alaykum) is explicit. Prayer and zakat-and-charity directly named. Closing 'Allah is Aware' -> knowledge.

58:14.notes: Section describes those who befriend 'a people with whom Allah has become angry' (tafsir: Jews) and swear falsely — classic hypocrite behaviour. Verses 17-18 describe Hell and the Day of Resurrection. Verse 19: Satan causes them to forget remembrance of Allah. Verse 21: 'Allah has written: I will certainly prevail, I and My messengers' — divine decree and prophethood-general. Closing 'Allah is Strong and Mighty' -> power. Oaths-and-vows tagged because false oaths are an explicit subject (vv. 14, 16, 18). people-of-the-book tagged because 'people with whom Allah has become angry' per Ibn Kathir refers to Jews.

58:22.notes: Single verse contrasting true believers — who cannot love those who oppose Allah even if family — with opponents of Allah and His Messenger. Allah inscribes faith in believers' hearts (divine-decree), supports them with a spirit from Him, admits them to Gardens (paradise). 'Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him' — mutual satisfaction framing. Sincerity tagged because the section's subject is the condition of true faith that cannot coexist with loyalty to Allah's enemies — a sincerity/ikhlas theme made explicit. Day of Judgment implicit in 'believe in Allah and the Last Day'.

59:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'Glorifying Allah is all that exists' — uttered praise formula → `praise`. The surah's opening attributes are 'Almighty, Most Wise' → `sovereignty`, `wisdom`. The expulsion of the People of the Book from Banu Nadir is the narrative core → `people-of-the-book`, `disbelievers`. Believers participate in the expulsion → `believers`. 'Allah came at them from where they never expected' → `power`. 'Had Allah not decreed exile' → `divine-decree`. 'In the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire' → hell implied but not described at length; the primary eschatological mention is the punishment. 'Whoever opposes Allah — Allah is stern in retribution' → `justice`. The event is a warning to others → `punishment-of-past-nations` (historical lesson framed as warning).

59:5.notes: Verse 5: cutting palm trees is 'by Allah's will' → `divine-decree`. Verse 6: 'Allah is Able to do all things' → `power`; 'Allah gives authority to His messengers' → `prophethood-general`. Verse 7: distribution of fay' (spoils restored to the Messenger) to orphans, poor, wayfarers → `zakat-and-charity`, `orphan-care`; the war-context distribution rule → `war-and-treaties`. 'Fear Allah' explicitly named → `taqwa`.

59:8.notes: Verse 8 praises the Muhajirin (emigrants) who sought Allah's favor → `migration`, `believers`. 'These are the sincere' explicitly names sincerity → `sincerity`. Verse 9 praises the Ansar for their generosity and preference over themselves → note: 'Whoever is protected from his natural greed' names greed avoidance but no label for the positive counter-virtue here beyond `sincerity` already applied; `zakat-and-charity` fits the generous giving motif. Verse 10 contains an uttered du'a: 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brethren…' → `dua-forgiveness`. Closing formula 'You are Clement and Merciful' → `mercy`.

59:11.notes: Verses 11–12 describe hypocrites making false promises to the People of the Book who disbelieved → `hypocrites`, `people-of-the-book`, `disbelievers`, `plotting`. Verse 13: their inner state of not understanding. Verse 14: their divided hearts and military weakness → `war-and-treaties`. Verse 15: 'painful punishment' — eschatological reference. Verse 16: the devil (Iblis) analogy who encourages disbelief → `iblis`, `disbelief`. Verse 17: 'both in the Fire forever' → `hell`.

59:18.notes: Verse 18 opens with 'O you who believe' → `believers`; 'Fear Allah' (twice) → `taqwa`; 'Allah is Aware of what you do' → `knowledge`. Verse 19: 'do not forget Allah' → `remembrance`. Verse 20: 'inhabitants of the Fire' vs 'inhabitants of Paradise' → `hell`, `paradise`. Verse 21: the Qur'an causing a mountain to crumble in awe → `the-quran`; 'These parables We cite for the people' — 'people/mankind' addressed as audience → `mankind`.

59:22.notes: Verse 22: 'There is no god but He' → `tawhid`; 'Knower of secrets and declarations' → `knowledge`; 'Compassionate, the Merciful' → `mercy`. Verse 23: 'the Sovereign, the Holy, the Almighty, the Omnipotent, the Overwhelming' → `sovereignty`, `power`; 'Glory be to Allah, beyond what they associate' — `subḥān` formula → `praise`; the refutation of association → `shirk`.

59:24.notes: Verse 24: 'the Creator, the Maker, the Designer' → `creation`, `tawhid`; 'His are the Most Beautiful Names' affirms divine uniqueness → `tawhid`; 'Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him' → `praise` (glorification uttered/described); 'the Majestic, the Wise' → `sovereignty`, `wisdom`.

60:1.notes: Direct address to believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū). The section forbids taking enemies as allies, references the expulsion of the Messenger and believers (migration context), and invokes God's knowledge of what is concealed. 'The Messenger' is referenced but not directly addressed, so muhammad is not tagged per §5.2.

60:3.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Abraham is named explicitly and held up as an example. Multiple uttered du'as: 'Rabbanā 'alayka tawakkalnā wa-ilayka ananbnā' (trust/repentance → trust-in-god, repentance), 'Rabbanā lā tajʿalnā fitnatan' (protection → dua-protection), 'waghfir lanā' (forgiveness → dua-forgiveness). Closing formula 'Mighty and Wise' → wisdom + power. 'We denounce you and what you worship apart from Allah' → shirk. Day of Resurrection mentioned in v.3 → day-of-judgment. 'Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Most Praised' at v.6 close → knowledge (Aware of deeds, v.3). Repentance explicit: 'to You we repent (ananbnā)' — concrete trigger met.

60:7.notes: God may bring affection between believers and former enemies — a ruling on relations with non-combatant disbelievers. 'Allah is Capable' → power. 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. 'Allah loves the equitable' and the equitable-dealing instruction → justice. War-and-treaties: legislating permissible vs. forbidden alliances based on combatant status.

60:10.notes: Direct address to believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū). Rules about believing women emigrants: testing their faith, prohibition on returning them to disbelievers, permissibility of marrying them, dissolving ties with unbelieving wives → marriage-and-family and divorce. Migration context is explicit throughout. Closing 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. 'Fear Allah' in v.11 is an explicit taqwa trigger.

60:12.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('O Prophet!') → muhammad. Believing women pledge allegiance on conditions including not associating partners with Allah → shirk (explicit). Closing 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. The bay'ah (pledge of allegiance) is a solemn covenant → covenant. Conditions also cover theft, adultery, and killing of children, but no distinct taxonomy labels exist for those crimes individually.

60:13.notes: Direct address to believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū). 'People with whom Allah has become angry' — per Ibn Kathir and standard tafsir, this refers to Jews → people-of-the-book tagged as a judgement call per §10. 'Despaired of the Hereafter' references the afterlife → day-of-judgment. Disbelievers mentioned explicitly in comparison ('as the faithless have despaired'). Confidence medium due to the implied-group identification for people-of-the-book.

61:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with tasbih of all in heavens and earth — 'praise' label applies. 'Al-Aziz al-Hakim' (Almighty, Wise) → 'power' and 'wisdom'. Verses 2–3 directly address believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū) about saying what they do not do — this is a sincerity/integrity theme; 'sincerity' label applies as it is the explicit subject of the exhortation. Verse 4 praises those who fight in ranks → 'war-and-treaties'.

61:5.notes: Moses addresses his people; they hurt him despite knowing he is Allah's messenger. 'Allah does not guide the sinful people' → 'guidance' (God as source/withholder of guidance named explicitly). Their swerving → 'disbelief' as the state of denial.

61:6.notes: Jesus son of Mary speaks — 'jesus' and 'mary' (named via 'son of Mary'). Addressed to Children of Israel → 'children-of-israel'. Confirms the Torah → 'previous-scriptures'. Announces a messenger named Ahmad (Muhammad) → 'muhammad' (section is substantively about him by name, not just a qul pattern). Miracles shown → 'miracles'. They call it sorcery → 'denial-of-revelation' and 'sorcery'.

61:7.notes: Verse 7 condemns those who fabricate lies about Allah when invited to Islam → 'disbelief'. Verse 8 references disbelievers (kāfirūn) trying to extinguish Allah's light → 'disbelievers'. Verse 9 mentions the Messenger sent with guidance and true religion to prevail over all religions, with polytheists (mushrikūn) disliking it → 'polytheists', 'prophethood-general', 'guidance'.

61:10.notes: Opens with yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū → 'believers'. The 'trade' is believing and striving with possessions and souls → 'war-and-treaties' (striving/jihad in God's cause) and 'zakat-and-charity' (striving with possessions). Reward: forgiveness → 'mercy'; gardens of Eden with rivers → 'paradise'. Victory and support also promised.

61:14.notes: Opens with yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū → 'believers'. Jesus son of Mary named → 'jesus' and 'mary'. Disciples (Hawariyyun) respond → 'disciples'. Children of Israel split into believers and disbelievers → 'children-of-israel', 'disbelief'. The narrative of Jesus's supporters is framed in terms of prophethood context → 'prophethood-general'.

64:1.notes: Verse 1 contains 'to Him all praise is due' (wa-lahu al-hamd) — uttered praise formula → tag `praise`. 'To Him belongs the Kingdom' → `sovereignty`. 'Able to do all things' → `power`. 'Created you' → `human-creation`. 'Created the heavens and the earth' → `creation-of-heavens-earth`. 'He knows…' → `knowledge`. Verse 2 names both disbelievers and believers as categories of humanity → `disbelievers`, `believers`, `mankind` (universal address about all human beings).

64:5.notes: Verses 5–6 recount past nations who rejected messengers and suffered consequences. 'Messengers came to them with clear explanations' → `prophethood-general`. 'They disbelieved and turned away' → `disbelief`, `denial-of-revelation`. 'Tasted the ill consequences… a painful torment awaits them' → `punishment-of-past-nations`, `hell`. 'Allah is Independent and Praiseworthy' — closing formula; 'Praiseworthy' (Hamid) maps to the `praise` attribute but here it is applied to God's self-sufficiency; the dominant attribute invoked is independence/sovereignty rather than the act of uttered praise, so `praise` is not triggered here (no praise is uttered in the section). Confidence remains high.

64:7.notes: Single verse. 'Those who disbelieve claim they will not be resurrected' → `disbelievers`, denial of resurrection. 'Say, Yes indeed…you will be resurrected' → `qul-statements`, `resurrection`. 'You will be informed of everything you did' → `reckoning`. 'That is easy for Allah' → `power`.

64:8.notes: 'Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and the Light which We sent down' — the Light refers to the Qur'an → `the-quran`. 'Allah is Aware of everything' → `knowledge`. 'Day of Gathering… Day of Mutual Exchange' → `day-of-judgment`. 'He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow' → `paradise`. 'Those who disbelieve and denounce Our revelations…inmates of the Fire' → `disbelievers`, `denial-of-revelation`, `hell`. 'Will remit his misdeeds' implies reckoning/accounting → `reckoning`. Believers and disbelievers are both explicitly named → `believers`, `disbelievers`.

64:11.notes: 'No disaster occurs except by Allah's leave' → `divine-decree`. 'He guides his heart' → `guidance`. 'Allah is Aware of everything' → `knowledge`. 'Allah, there is no god but He' → `tawhid`. 'In Allah let the believers put their trust' — explicit instruction on tawakkul → `trust-in-god`. 'O you who believe!' direct address → `believers`. 'Among your wives and children are enemies…pardon and forgive' → `marriage-and-family`. 'Allah is Forgiver and Merciful' closing formula → `mercy`.

64:15.notes: 'Your possessions and children are a test' — addressed to believers. 'So be conscious of Allah' (ittaqu Allah) — explicit naming of taqwa → `taqwa`. 'Give for your own good' (wa-anfiqu) → `zakat-and-charity`. 'He who is protected from his stinginess' (shuhh) — explicit naming of miserliness/greed → `greed-and-miserliness`. 'He will multiply it for you and will forgive you… Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing' → `mercy`. Direct address 'O believers' is implicit here (continuing from prior verses) → `believers`.

64:18.notes: Single closing verse naming three divine attributes: 'Knower of the Unseen and the Seen' → `knowledge`; 'the Almighty' (al-Aziz) → `sovereignty` (God's absolute dominance/might); 'the Wise' (al-Hakim) → `wisdom`. Short doxological closer; no people, no narrative, no du'a.

65:1.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' triggers muhammad. taqwa is explicitly named ('be pious before Allah'). The verse establishes divine limits (hudud) for divorce procedure and housing of women during iddah. 'disbelief' trimmed — not present here; replaced with the hudud-transgression warning which maps to taqwa. Dropping disbelief label as not triggered.

65:2.notes: taqwa explicitly named ('whoever fears Allah'). trust-in-god explicitly named ('whoever relies on Allah'). provision: 'will provide for him from where he never expected'. divine-decree: 'Allah has set a measure to all things'. justice-and-witness: 'call to witness two just people... give upright testimony'. believers: 'whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day' is the direct addressee of the exhortation.

65:4.notes: Iddah rules for post-menopausal, pre-menstrual, and pregnant women. taqwa explicitly named three times in these two verses ('whoever fears Allah'). 'This is the ordinance of Allah which He sent down to you' → the-quran (revelation sent down). mercy implied by ease but not explicitly named — not tagged per rule 5.

65:6.notes: Detailed rules on housing, maintenance, and nursing payments for divorced women during iddah. provision: 'spend on them', 'give them their payment', 'let him spend according to what Allah has given him', 'Allah will bring ease after hardship'. No divine attribute closing formula beyond the provision theme.

65:8.notes: Towns that defied Allah and His messengers → punishment-of-past-nations. 'defied the command of... His messengers' → prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation. 'held strictly accountable' → reckoning. 'dreadful punishment / perdition' → disbelief as the cause. No specific nation named so no individual people labels.

65:10.notes: Direct address 'O you who possess intellect and have faith' → believers. taqwa explicitly named ('beware/fear Allah'). hell: 'Allah has prepared for them a severe retribution'. the-quran: 'Allah has sent down to you a Reminder'. prophethood-general: 'a messenger who recites to you Allah's verses'. guidance: 'bring those who believe... from darkness into light'. paradise: 'gardens beneath which rivers flow, therein to abide forever'. provision: 'Allah has given him an excellent provision'.

65:12.notes: Seven heavens and their like of earth → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Allah is Capable of everything' → power. 'Allah Encompasses everything in knowledge' → knowledge. The entire verse is a declaration of God's attributes through His creation, reinforcing oneness → tawhid.

66:1.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' triggers muhammad. Verse 1 addresses the Prophet's self-prohibition for wives' pleasure — marriage-and-family. Verse 2 legislates dissolution of oaths — oaths-and-vows. Closing formulas: 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy; 'All-Knowing, Most Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

66:3.notes: Direct address to the Prophet in context; verse 3 concerns a confidential disclosure by one of his wives — knowledge ('All-Knowing, All-Informed'). Verse 4 mentions Gabriel and the angels as supporters — angels; 'the righteous believers' — believers; 'if you repent' — repentance is the explicit subject. Verse 5 explicitly raises the prospect of divorce — divorce; and describes ideal wives — marriage-and-family.

66:6.notes: Verse 6 opens with 'O you who believe' — believers; fire with angel-guardians — hell + angels. Verse 7 addresses 'O you who disbelieved' — disbelievers; being repaid for deeds — reckoning. Verse 8 opens again with 'O you who believe' — believers; commands sincere repentance — repentance; promises gardens with rivers — paradise; mentions 'the Prophet' — muhammad; the uttered du'a 'Our Lord, complete our light for us, and forgive us' — dua-forgiveness; closing 'You are capable of all things' — power.

66:9.notes: 12 labels at the ceiling. Verse 9 directly addresses 'O Prophet' — muhammad; commands striving against disbelievers and hypocrites — disbelievers + hypocrites; their abode is Hell — hell. Verse 10 names Noah (wife of Noah) — noah; Lot (wife of Lot) — lot; hell for the disbelieving wives. Verse 11 names Pharaoh (wife of Pharaoh) — pharaoh; her uttered supplication 'My Lord, build for me a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his works and save me from the wrongdoing people' — this is an uttered du'a asking for paradise — paradise, and protection from evil/wrongdoing — dua-protection; believers are illustrated by her example — believers. The two wives betraying their husbands also touches marriage-and-family. The du'a also has a component of distress (saving her from Pharaoh) — dua-distress. Notes: trim candidates if needed: dua-distress (subsumed by dua-protection in context), marriage-and-family (secondary to the examples' eschatological purpose).

66:12.notes: Mary daughter of Imran named explicitly — mary + family-of-imran. 'We breathed into her of Our Spirit' refers to Jesus's conception — jesus (the Spirit breathed in is the agent of his creation) + miracles + human-creation. 'She believed in the truth of her Lord's Words and His Books' — previous-scriptures. Angels are associated with the Spirit breathed in (cf. standard tafsir on 'Our Spirit' = Gabriel) — angels, medium confidence; kept because rule 3 is generous and the Spirit/Ruh is consistently angel-linked in the Qur'an. 'She was one of the devout (qanitin)' — taqwa has a concrete trigger in the explicit commendation of devout God-consciousness.

68:1.notes: Opens with the disjoined letter Nun (Nūn) → disjoined-letters. Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('you are not insane', 'you are of a great moral character') → muhammad. The deniers described include a 'backbiter, spreader of slander' → slander-and-backbiting; 'preventer of good' + 'money and children' motivation → greed-and-miserliness; 'When Our Verses are recited to him, he says Myths of the ancients!' → denial-of-revelation. 'Your Lord knows best who has strayed' → knowledge (divine attribute). The pen and inscribing relate to revelation/the Quran → the-quran. The disbelievers/deniers are the addressed antagonists → disbelievers. Prophethood is being defended here as a category → prophethood-general.

68:17.notes: The parable of the garden owners is a punishment-warning narrative → punishment-of-past-nations. Their exclusion of the poor from the harvest → greed-and-miserliness. 'No poor person is to enter it upon you today' is explicit exclusion of charity. Their turning back and saying 'Glory to our Lord—We were indeed in the wrong' is uttered repentance/glorification → repentance and praise (subhana rabbina is uttered). 'Perhaps our Lord will give us a better substitute' invokes provision hope → provision. God's calamity destroying their garden as just punishment → justice. The most reasonable among them references glorification (taqwa/remembrance implied by 'if only you would glorify') — the word 'glorify' is the explicit trigger for praise already covered; taqwa is referenced as what they lacked. Closing verse: 'punishment of the Hereafter is greater' → day-of-judgment is borderline; the comparison is mentioned but the Hereafter is not the section's subject — leaving it untagged per rule 5.

68:34.notes: Gardens of Delight for the righteous/muttaqin → paradise. 'Shall We treat the Muslims like the villains?' — contrast between believers and disbelievers → believers, disbelievers. Day when the Shin is exposed and they are called to bow → day-of-judgment. 'Or do they have partners?' (shuraka') → shirk, polytheists. The section's core argument is about fair judgment and the impossibility of equalizing the righteous with the wicked → justice. The Day of Reckoning scene (bowing, shame) → reckoning. The question 'do you have a scripture' is rhetorical and does not substantively treat previous-scriptures.

68:44.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('do you ask them for a fee', 'wait patiently for the Decision of your Lord') → muhammad. 'The Fellow of the Fish' is Jonah → jonah. 'Wait patiently' — the word 'patient' (isbir) is explicitly used as a command → patience (explicit trigger per rule 5). 'Those who reject this discourse' → disbelievers, denial-of-revelation. 'My plan is firm' / 'We will proceed against them gradually' → plotting (God's counter-plan against scheming disbelievers; cf. makr usage). 'Were it not for his Lord's favor' → mercy. 'They do not know' / 'Or do they know the future?' → knowledge (divine attribute contrasted with their ignorance).

68:52.notes: Single verse: 'it is no less than a reminder to all the Worlds' — the Quran as subject → the-quran. 'All the Worlds' (lil-'alamin) encompasses all creation/humanity → mankind.

69:1.notes: Very short rhetorical opening — three verses asking what 'the Reality' (al-Haqqah) is. The term al-Haqqah is a name for the Day of Judgment/the inevitable Event. No named figures, no divine attributes explicitly stated, no du'a. Single label is appropriate for this brief section.

69:4.notes: Thamud and 'Ad explicitly named and destroyed. Pharaoh named. 'The Overturned Cities' (al-Mu'tafikāt) refers to Lot's people per tafsir — tagging 'lot'. The Flood narrative is referenced ('when the waters overflowed, We carried you in the cruising ship') — tagging 'noah'. All denied the messenger — 'prophethood-general' and 'denial-of-revelation'. The wind unleashed for seven nights/eight days is a natural phenomenon as divine punishment — 'natural-signs'. Disbelief is the explicit cause of their punishment.

69:13.notes: Long section covering: the trumpet blast and cosmic destruction (resurrection/day-of-judgment); angels carrying the Throne; the handing of books in right vs. left hand (reckoning); lofty Garden with pleasant living (paradise); the disbeliever shackled and scorched in the Blaze (hell). His sin: he did not believe in Allah and did not advocate feeding the destitute — 'disbelief' and 'greed-and-miserliness' (refusing to feed the poor = miserliness). 'Believers' and 'disbelievers' implied by the two contrasting groups. 13 labels — slightly over ceiling. Trim candidates: 'believers' (only implicit by contrast), 'disbelievers' (implicit rather than direct address).

69:38.notes: God swears by the seen and unseen that the Qur'an is the speech of a noble messenger, not a poet or soothsayer — 'the-quran' and 'denial-of-revelation'. The passage substantively addresses the Prophet's integrity and the consequence if he had falsified revelation — this is direct address about Muhammad ﷺ personally ('Had he falsely attributed…'), warranting 'muhammad'. 'It is a message for the righteous (muttaqeen)' — 'taqwa' explicitly named as the addressees. God asserts He would have seized and destroyed him — 'power'. 'We know that some of you will reject it' — divine knowledge invoked, 'knowledge'. Disbelievers named at close ('source of grief for the unbelievers') — 'disbelievers'.

69:52.notes: Single verse commanding glorification (tasbih) of the Lord's name — 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.' This is a command to praise/glorify, not an uttered praise itself. However, the formula 'Subbiḥ bismi rabbika' is a praise utterance directed at the reader/Prophet that functions as uttered glorification in recitation. Per §5.6b, 'subḥān' family words map to 'praise'. The divine attribute 'the Magnificent' (al-Aẓīm) is invoked — could tag 'sovereignty' or 'power', but the verse's sole subject is the act of glorification. Tagging 'praise' only; the attribute naming is minimal and subsidiary.

70:1.notes: Patience is explicitly commanded ('be patient with sweet patience'), meeting the rule-5 trigger. 'Lord of the Ways of Ascent' asserts sovereignty. Angels ascending invoked. The imminent torment and the Day being near vs. distant are eschatological.

70:8.notes: The sky like molten brass and mountains like wool are cosmic signs of the Hour. The Raging Fire (Latha) is hell. The final verses mention accumulating and hoarding, triggering greed-and-miserliness.

70:19.notes: Human creation is referenced ('Man was created restless'). The section describes qualities of the believers contrasted with humanity in general. Prayer mentioned twice explicitly. Zakat/charity referenced ('rightful share for the beggar and the deprived'). Day of Judgment affirmed. Paradise promised. Chastity and spousal relations trigger marriage-and-family. Honoring trusts and pledges triggers covenant. Standing by testimonies triggers justice-and-witness. Fear of Lord's punishment is a taqwa trigger ('those who fear the punishment of their Lord').

70:36.notes: Disbelievers mockingly cluster around hoping for paradise — their attitude has a mockery dimension. 'We created them from what they know' is a human-creation reference. The oath by the Lord of Easts and Wests asserts power. Verses 42–43 describe emergence from tombs, triggering resurrection. The promised Day is day-of-judgment.

70:44.notes: Single verse. Eyes cast down and overwhelmed by humiliation on the promised Day. Humility label applies as the humiliation/lowering is the explicit subject. Day of Judgment explicitly named ('this is the Day which they were promised').

71:1.notes: Taqwa is explicitly named ('reverence Him' / ittaquh). Mercy is invoked via the promise of forgiveness. Divine-decree triggered by 'Allah's term cannot be deferred once it has arrived.'

71:5.notes: Large but justified section (16 verses). Arrogance explicitly named ('became more and more arrogant' / istakbaru istikbara). Repentance triggered by Noah's explicit call to 'Ask your Lord for forgiveness.' Mercy via 'He is Forgiving.' Human-creation: 'He created you in stages' and 'germinated you from the earth.' Creation-of-heavens-earth: seven heavens in layers. Cosmic-bodies: moon for light, sun as lamp. Natural-signs: rain, gardens, rivers, earth as spread. Provision: wealth, children, gardens, rivers. 11 labels — within ceiling.

71:21.notes: Plotting explicitly named ('schemed outrageous schemes' / makaru makran kubbara). Shirk: the named idols Wadd, Souwa, Yaghoos, Yaooq, Nassr. Hell: 'were hurled into a Fire.' Punishment-of-past-nations: drowning and fire as their destruction. Dua-distress: Noah's address 'My Lord, they have defied me…do not increase the wrongdoers except in confusion' is an uttered supplication in complaint and appeal. The section ends with a du'a clause ('do not increase the wrongdoers except in confusion').

71:26.notes: An uttered supplication by Noah asking God to leave no disbeliever on earth — motivated by the fear they will mislead others. Dua-distress fits as a supplication borne out of persecution and despair. Guidance is explicitly at stake ('they will mislead your servants'). Disbelief explicitly named ('wicked unbelievers').

71:28.notes: Quintessential dua-forgiveness: 'My Lord! Forgive me and my parents…' Believers explicitly named ('all the believing men and believing women'). Mercy is the divine attribute invoked via the forgiveness request. Marriage-and-family: Noah prays for his parents and household members, grounding the supplication in family ties. Disbelievers implicitly referenced in 'do not increase the wrongdoers except in perdition.'
