72:1.notes: Jinn's testimony opens the surah: they heard the Quran, believed, affirmed tawhid (no mate, no child), and noted past denial of resurrection. 'Say' at verse 1 triggers qul-statements. Shirk is explicitly rejected ('we will never associate anyone with our Lord'). 'Fools among us used to say nonsense about Allah' covers disbelief/denial patterns. Seeking power through jinn (v6) is a form of shirk-adjacent practice — covered under shirk.

72:8.notes: Jinn describe probing the heavens and finding it guarded by stern angels and shooting stars/projectiles. Cosmic-bodies applies to the shooting stars (shuhub). Angels appear as the guards. The change in heavenly arrangement reflects divine decree about what information is now withheld.

72:11.notes: Jinn acknowledge internal diversity — righteous and less-than-righteous paths. They affirm they cannot escape Allah's power (v12). The compromisers are destined for Hell (v15). Guidance is explicitly mentioned as the thing they heard and believed (v13). Power of God affirmed in 'we cannot defeat Allah nor escape Him.'

72:16.notes: Had they kept to the Path, God would have given them abundant water (provision). Whoever turns away from remembrance of their Lord faces mounting torment. Taqwa is borderline — the section frames steadfastness on the Path as the condition for blessing, which is the taqwa concept, but the word is not used explicitly. Marked medium due to taqwa borderline call. Punishment here is future/conditional rather than historical, so punishment-of-past-nations is a weak fit — removed in favour of the clearer labels.

72:18.notes: Mosques are for Allah alone — do not call on anyone besides Him (tawhid, anti-shirk, prayer context). Multiple 'Say:' (qul) commands in vv20–22 trigger qul-statements. The Prophet's role in conveying messages is prophethood-general. Hell mentioned explicitly for those who defy Allah and His Messenger (v23). 'The servant of Allah' in v19 is understood as Muhammad ﷺ in tafsir, but since this is descriptive rather than direct address, muhammad label is not added; qul-statements covers the Say: pattern.

72:24.notes: Disbelievers will see what they were promised on the Day (day-of-judgment). 'Say: I do not know whether it is near' triggers qul-statements. 'The Knower of the Invisible' — God's exclusive knowledge of the unseen is the dominant divine attribute (knowledge). Messengers receive guarded disclosure of revelation (prophethood-general). Divine decree covers God's timing of the promised event. Disbelievers are the addressed party in v24.

72:28.notes: God ensures messengers have conveyed their Lord's messages (prophethood-general). 'He encompasses what they have and has tallied everything by number' — comprehensive divine knowledge (knowledge). Guards dispatched around messengers (angels, continuing from v27). 'Tallied everything by number' also reflects divine decree/omniscience. Short single-verse section; 4 labels appropriate.

74:1.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('O you Enrobed one', 'your Lord') qualifies this for `muhammad`. 'Magnify your Lord' is an uttered-praise command but since it is commanded rather than uttered in the section itself, `praise` is borderline; however 'And magnify your Lord' (فَكَبِّرْ) is a direct command to glorify God and the formula Allāhu akbar is closely implied — included at medium sub-confidence. 'Be constant' (patience/sabr) is explicitly named as a virtue to practice. Trumpet + difficult day for disbelievers → `day-of-judgment` and `disbelievers`.

74:11.notes: The unnamed individual (per tafsir, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah) was given vast wealth and children (provision) yet turned arrogant and stubborn toward revelations. He called the Qur'an 'magic from the past' → `denial-of-revelation` and `sorcery`. His desire for more despite ingratitude → `greed-and-miserliness`. Threatened with Saqar (Hell) → `hell`. Arrogance explicitly named: 'turned back and was proud' (istakbara) → `arrogance`.

74:31.notes: Angels appointed as wardens of the Fire → `angels` and `hell`. 'Those given the Scripture' (People of the Book) mentioned twice → `people-of-the-book`. Believers mentioned → `believers`. Those with sickness in their hearts and the unbelievers → `hypocrites` and `disbelievers`. 'Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills' → `guidance`. 'A reminder for the mortals' describing the Qur'an → `the-quran`.

74:32.notes: Oath by the moon, night, and morning → `cosmic-bodies`. 'A warning to the mortals' (al-bashar) is a universal address to humanity → `mankind`. The great warning refers to Saqar/Hell established in prior section, functioning here as an eschatological reminder → `day-of-judgment`. 'It is a reminder' points to the Qur'an as a reminder → `the-quran`.

74:38.notes: Every soul hostage to its deeds → `reckoning`. Those on the Right in Gardens → `paradise`. Dialogue about what drove them to Saqar → `hell` and `day-of-judgment`. 'We were not of those who prayed' → `prayer`. 'Nor did we feed the destitute' → `zakat-and-charity`. 'We used to deny the Day of Judgment' → `disbelief`. 'Intercession of intercessors will not help them' → `intercession`.

74:49.notes: Rebuke of those turning away from the Reminder → `denial-of-revelation` and `the-quran`. 'They do not fear the Hereafter' → `day-of-judgment`. The panicked-donkeys simile is directed at those fleeing the message — they are the disbelievers → `disbelievers`. 'Whoever wills shall remember it' is a universal address → `mankind`.

74:56.notes: 'They will not remember unless Allah wills' → `divine-decree`. 'He is the Source of Righteousness (taqwa) and the Source of Forgiveness' → `taqwa` is explicitly named as God's attribute here, and forgiveness → `mercy`. The verse continues the address to humanity from the prior section → `mankind`.

75:1.notes: The divine oath by the Day of Resurrection and the blaming soul opens the surah. Man's skepticism about bone-reassembly is directly rebutted with God's power ('We are Able'). Man's desire to deny what is ahead and his mocking question 'When is the Day?' are denial/disbelief triggers.

75:7.notes: The eclipse of the moon, joining of sun and moon are cosmic signs of the Hour (cosmic-bodies + signs-of-the-hour). Man's accounting of all he put forward and left behind is the reckoning. 'To your Lord is the settlement' asserts sovereignty. Mankind is the addressee throughout.

75:16.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('Do not wag your tongue with it') about receiving revelation — this is substantively about Muhammad personally and about the Qur'an's collection, recitation, and explanation. 'Upon Us is its collection' reflects divine decree/guarantee. Muhammad tagged because of direct personal address, not a qul-statement.

75:20.notes: 'You love the fleeting life and disregard the Hereafter' is direct address to mankind. Radiant faces looking toward their Lord = paradise/reward; gloomy faces = hell/punishment. Disbelief is implied by the preference for the fleeting over the eternal, though it reads as a general human tendency — tagged because the section's contrast maps to believer/disbeliever eschatological fates. Hell not named explicitly but the 'back-breaker' befalling gloomy faces is a clear punishment reference.

75:26.notes: Verses 26–30 vividly describe the moment of death (breast-bones, leg entwined with leg — agony of dying). Verses 31–35 describe the disbeliever's failure: 'he neither believed nor prayed' (disbelief + prayer), 'denied and turned away' (disbelief), 'went to his family full of pride' (arrogance — 'yatamatta' connotes strutting arrogance). The woe-refrain closes. Mankind is the implied subject.

75:36.notes: The rhetorical question 'Does man think he will be left without purpose?' leads into the stages of human creation — drop of semen, clot, proportioned form, two sexes. This directly invokes human-creation. 'He created and proportioned' tags creation. The implied argument is toward resurrection/accountability (day-of-judgment). Power is implicit in the creative act ('He created and proportioned'). Mankind is the subject.

75:40.notes: Single verse: 'Is He not Able to revive the dead?' — a direct rhetorical affirmation of God's power to resurrect. Both resurrection and power are the explicit subject.

76:1.notes: Verse 1 invokes mankind's pre-existence (human-creation). Verse 2 describes creation from a mixed fluid and the granting of hearing/sight. Verse 3 frames the two paths — appreciative (taqwa) or unappreciative (disbelief) — as the test. Guidance is explicitly stated ('We guided him to the way').

76:4.notes: Verse 4: hell prepared for disbelievers. Verses 5–6: paradise drinks for the righteous. Verses 7–10: the righteous described — fulfilling vows (oaths-and-vows), fearing the Day (day-of-judgment), feeding the poor/orphan (zakat-and-charity, orphan-care) and the captive (manumission-and-captives), acting for Allah's sake alone (sincerity). Verse 12: rewarded for their patience (sabr explicitly triggered by the word 'patience'). This section has 11 labels, within ceiling.

76:13.notes: Detailed description of paradise's physical comforts — thrones, shade, fruit, silver vessels, cups, silk, bracelets, a pure drink — and the divine declaration that this is their reward. Provision is tagged because the sustained imagery of food, drink, and sustenance in paradise is God's provision. Believers are the implicit addressees throughout ('for you', 'your efforts').

76:23.notes: Verse 23: the Qur'an's revelation is the explicit subject (the-quran). Verse 24: direct second-person address to the Prophet with an instruction to be patient (patience explicitly named) and not obey sinners/blasphemers — this is direct address to Muhammad (muhammad). Verse 25: 'mention the Name of your Lord morning and evening' — remembrance (dhikr) explicitly commanded. Verse 26: 'prostrate yourself… glorify Him long into the night' — prayer. No qul-statement present.

76:27.notes: Verse 27: the disbelievers love the fleeting life and ignore the Heavy Day (day-of-judgment). Verse 28: 'We created them and strengthened their frame' (human-creation) and 'whenever We will, We can replace them' (power — divine omnipotence asserted directly).

76:29.notes: Verse 29: 'whoever wills, let him take a path to his Lord' — guidance explicitly offered. Verse 30: 'you cannot will unless Allah wills' — divine-decree asserted. Closing formula 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' — knowledge and wisdom (rule 4, closing attributes).

76:31.notes: God admits into His mercy whom He wills (mercy). The wrongdoers face a painful punishment prepared for them (hell, justice). Short single-verse section; 4 labels appropriate.

77:1.notes: The oaths by 'those unleashed in succession…delivering a message…excusing or warning' are interpreted by many commentators (including Ibn Kathir) as referring to angels, winds, or Qur'anic verses. The most supported reading is angels carrying revelation, hence 'angels' and 'prophethood-general'. The closing promise that what is foretold will occur points to 'day-of-judgment' and 'divine-decree'. Confidence medium because the referent of the oaths is inherently ambiguous from the surface text alone.

77:8.notes: Stars obliterated, sky fractured, mountains blown away — classic signs of the Hour; 'cosmic-bodies' applies for the stars. Messengers 'alerted' for the Day of Decision invokes 'prophethood-general'. 'Woe to the liars/rejecters' invokes 'disbelief' and 'reckoning'.

77:16.notes: Destruction of the ancients followed by the later generations as a pattern of divine punishment for the guilty/rejecters. 'Woe on that Day to the rejecters' ties to the Day of Judgment frame running through the surah.

77:20.notes: Creation from fluid in a secure lodging = 'human-creation'; earth as homestead, lofty mountains, pure water = 'natural-signs' and 'creation-of-heavens-earth'; 'We measured precisely' = 'divine-decree' and 'power'; pure water provision = 'provision'. Recurring 'Woe on that Day' refrain links to 'day-of-judgment' and 'disbelief'.

77:29.notes: Verses 29–40 describe Hell's shadow of three masses, sparks, flames — 'hell'. Verses 41–44 describe the muttaqun in shades, fountains, and fruits — 'paradise' and 'taqwa' (the muttaqun are explicitly named as the subject). 'Day of Separation, We have gathered you' = 'day-of-judgment'. 'Woe to the falsifiers/rejecters' throughout = 'disbelief' and 'reckoning'.

77:46.notes: 'Eat and enjoy a little; you are criminals' — address to the disbelievers. 'When it is said to them, kneel, they do not kneel' — explicit refusal of prayer/prostration, hence 'prayer' (the institution being defied) and 'disbelievers'. Recurring 'Woe on that Day' = 'day-of-judgment'.

77:50.notes: Closing rhetorical challenge: 'In what message beyond this will they believe?' — the Qur'an is the subject ('the-quran'), and the verse expresses exasperation at persistent rejection ('denial-of-revelation', 'disbelief').

78:1.notes: The 'Great Event' (al-naba' al-'azim) is understood by Ibn Kathir as referring to the Resurrection/Day of Judgment, about which the disbelievers were disputing. The section opens as a challenge to those who deny or debate this truth, hence denial-of-revelation is also apt. No named figures, no du'a, no divine attributes explicitly invoked.

78:6.notes: A series of rhetorical questions cataloguing God's creative acts: earth as cradle (natural-signs, creation-of-heavens-earth), mountains as pegs (natural-signs), creation of humans in pairs (human-creation, mankind), sleep, night/day (cosmic-bodies), seven heavens (creation-of-heavens-earth), blazing lamp/sun (cosmic-bodies), rain, vegetation, gardens (natural-signs, provision). 'Power' is warranted by the cumulative assertion of God's capacity over all these acts.

78:17.notes: The Day of Sorting (yawm al-fasl), the blowing of the Trumpet, coming in droves, the sky opened up, mountains set in motion — classic resurrection and Day-of-Judgment imagery with signs-of-the-hour features.

78:21.notes: Hell described in detail as destination for the oppressors/transgressors. Explicit reason: they did not anticipate the reckoning (reckoning label) and denied God's signs (denial-of-revelation, disbelief). 'A fitting requital' invokes divine justice. 'We have enumerated everything in writing' adds the justice/reckoning dimension.

78:31.notes: 'For the righteous (muttaqin) there is triumph' — explicit mention of taqwa/God-consciousness as the qualifying trait. Gardens, vineyards, spouses, drinks — standard paradise description. Believers implied as the muttaqin who receive this reward.

78:37.notes: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth… The Most Merciful' — sovereignty and mercy explicitly named. Angels and the Spirit standing in rows on the Day — angels label. 'None can argue with Him' and 'only one permitted by the Most Merciful may speak' — intercession theme on the Day of Judgment. Day of Reality framing confirms day-of-judgment.

78:40.notes: Warning of a near punishment; the Day when a person sees what his hands have wrought (reckoning); the faithless (al-kafir) wishing to be dust — disbelievers and disbelief labels apply. Single verse section; 4 labels appropriate.

79:1.notes: The five oaths refer to entities that snatch, remove, glide, race, and regulate. Majority tafsir (Ibn Kathir) identifies these as angels performing various duties including seizing souls and managing divine affairs. 'Those who regulate events' points to divine-decree administration. No concrete trigger for any concept label beyond these two identifications.

79:6.notes: The quake and its successor describe the blasts of the Day; hearts pounding and sights downcast depict the scene of judgment. Verses 10–12 quote the disbelievers mocking resurrection ('Are we to be restored?'), earning both disbelievers and resurrection tags. The single nudge bringing them awake confirms resurrection.

79:15.notes: Moses called at the sacred valley, sent to Pharaoh — both figures named. 'Greatest Miracle' shown = miracles. Pharaoh denied, defied, and declared himself 'Lord most high' = arrogance (explicit istakbara-equivalent: 'I am your Lord, the most high'). Allah seized him with exemplary punishment = punishment-of-past-nations. 'Guide you to your Lord and you will turn reverent' invokes guidance and taqwa (reverence/fear of God) explicitly as the goal of Moses's mission. 'A lesson for whoever fears' reinforces taqwa as explicit subject.

79:27.notes: Verses 27–32 describe the construction of the heaven, night/day cycle (cosmic-bodies), spreading of the earth, water and pasture (natural-signs), and anchored mountains. 'A source of enjoyment for you and your animals' = provision. The rhetorical challenge 'Are you more difficult to create?' addresses humanity implicitly = mankind. The description of God building and proportioning asserts His power.

79:34.notes: The Great Cataclysm arrives; man remembers his deeds (reckoning); Hell displayed; defiant one who preferred worldly life goes to Hell (disbelievers); one who feared the Standing of his Lord and restrained desires goes to Paradise (believers). 'Feared the Standing of his Lord' is an explicit taqwa trigger. Both Hell and Paradise are named destinations.

79:42.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('They ask you', 'You have no knowledge', 'You are just a warner') = muhammad. The Hour's knowledge belongs to God alone = knowledge (divine attribute). The question about the Hour = signs-of-the-hour / day-of-judgment. 'You are just a warner' affirms prophetic role = prophethood-general.

79:46.notes: Single verse describing how, on the Day they witness it, the disbelievers will feel as though their worldly life was only an evening or a morning — a closing reflection on the brevity of the dunya relative to the Day. Disbelievers is the implied subject ('they' who were heedless).

80:1.notes: The section addresses the Prophet directly ('you frowned', 'you gave him attention', 'you were inattentive') — this is direct second-person address to Muhammad, so `muhammad` applies. The blind man seeking purification (tazkiya) and reminder (dhikr) triggers `taqwa` and `remembrance` — both are explicitly named concepts ('seeking to purify himself', 'be reminded'). The honorable pages/scribes in verses 13-16 describe the Qur'an's preserved form, warranting `the-quran` and `angels` (the scribes are understood as angelic by tafsir; marked medium for this). The man who is 'indifferent' and does not pursue purification maps to `disbelievers` per context.

80:17.notes: Mankind addressed as a category ('perish man'). Human creation from sperm drop — `human-creation`. Death and burial — `death-and-dying`. Resurrection ('when He wills, He will resurrect him') — `resurrection`. The closing condemnation ('he did not fulfill what He has commanded him') reflects `disbelief`. 'He eased the way for him' is an allusion to guidance (`guidance`) and provision. `provision` is borderline here since it's implicit — included because it fits the pattern of God enabling man.

80:24.notes: Explicit invitation to 'let man consider his food' — addresses mankind. Rain, cracked soil, grains, grapes, olives, dates, gardens, fruits as signs of God's creative provision — `natural-signs` and `provision` both clearly apply. God as Creator of these phenomena — `creation`.

80:33.notes: The 'Deafening Noise' (al-saakhkhah) is a sign/event of the Last Day — `signs-of-the-hour` and `day-of-judgment`. The fleeing from family members on that day is a vivid eschatological image; `marriage-and-family` is tagged because spouses, children, parents, and siblings are all explicitly named as those fled from — this is a pointed inversion of family bonds. `resurrection` is implied by 'that Day' but is captured here as the gathering context.

80:38.notes: Contrasting faces on the Day of Judgment — radiant/rejoicing (paradise-bound believers) vs. misery-covered (hell-bound disbelievers). Both `paradise` and `hell` are implicitly present through the contrasting fates. `believers` and `disbelievers` are the two groups depicted.

80:42.notes: Single verse identifying 'the faithless, the vicious' — explicitly names the disbelievers as the subject of the prior miserable faces. `disbelievers` (people facet) and `disbelief` (negative-attributes facet) both apply.

82:1.notes: Verses 1–4 describe cosmic and earthly upheaval at the Hour (sky breaking, planets scattered, oceans exploded, tombs overturned) — classic signs-of-the-hour imagery with cosmic-bodies and natural-signs both present. Verse 5 introduces the reckoning motif (each soul knowing what it advanced or deferred).

82:6.notes: Direct address 'O man!' → mankind. Verses 7–8 describe God creating, forming, proportioning, and assembling the human in whatever shape He willed → human-creation and creation. 'Most Generous' is an attribute but maps closest to no single attribute label cleanly; the section's emphasis on God's shaping power supports power. 'In whatever shape He willed' implies divine omnipotence and knowledge of each form.

82:9.notes: Verse 9: 'you reject the religion' → disbelief and denial-of-revelation. Verses 10–12: the noble recording angels (kiraman katibin) who know all deeds → angels and knowledge (they know everything you do).

82:13.notes: Classic eschatological contrast: the virtuous in bliss (paradise) vs. the wicked in Hell (hell), entering it on the Day of Justice (day-of-judgment). The outcome-based framing implies reckoning has occurred.

82:17.notes: Both verses are a rhetorical double-question emphasising the incomprehensibility of the Day of Justice. Short two-verse section; single label is appropriate per the rules.

82:19.notes: No soul will avail another → no intercession motif, though intercession is not the section's explicit subject. 'The decision on that Day is Allah's' → sovereignty (God holds all dominion and command). Day of Judgment is the explicit setting.

83:1.notes: The section opens with a condemnation of defrauders in trade (short-measuring), then pivots to the eschatological warning of the Great Day when mankind stands before God. 'Mankind will stand' triggers both mankind and day-of-judgment. Trade fraud is an explicit legal-ethical subject warranting trade-and-debt and corruption-on-earth.

83:7.notes: Sijjeen is the record of the wicked; woe to the deniers of the Day of Reckoning; they call revelations 'legends of the ancients' (denial-of-revelation trigger); their hearts are corroded; they are screened from God and will roast in Hell. Denial-of-revelation is explicitly triggered by 'legends of the ancients.' No uttered du'a; no named figures.

83:18.notes: Elliyyeen is the record of the righteous (abraar); they are amid bliss, on thrones, given sealed wine from Tasneem, a spring drunk by 'those brought near' (al-muqarrabun — the angels or favoured ones near God). Paradise descriptions are vivid. 'Those brought near' as witnesses and drinkers from the spring could be angels or the highest class of the righteous; tagging angels generously per rule 3 is appropriate since al-muqarrabun is a standard designation for angels in Qur'anic usage. Reckoning is implied by the contrast of records of righteous vs. wicked.

83:29.notes: The criminals (disbelievers) used to laugh at, wink at, and slander the believers — explicit mockery trigger. On the Day, the believers will laugh at the unbelievers from their thrones — paradise imagery. Day-of-judgment is the reversing frame. Both believers and disbelievers are named as groups.

83:36.notes: A single rhetorical verse: 'Have the unbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?' — affirming divine justice and the completeness of reckoning. Justice is invoked substantively as the closing claim of the surah. Reckoning is the explicit subject of the question.

10:1.notes: Alif-Lam-Ra opening triggers disjoined-letters. 'Wise Book' triggers wisdom and the-quran. Disbelievers call the Prophet a sorcerer — denial-of-revelation and sorcery. Universal address to mankind implied in 'warn mankind'.

10:3.notes: Creation in six days, settling on the Throne — creation-of-heavens-earth and sovereignty. No intercessor except by His permission — intercession. Originating and repeating creation, rewarding with equity — justice. Boiling drink and painful torment for disbelievers — hell and disbelief.

10:5.notes: Sun and moon as light with phases — cosmic-bodies. Alternation of night and day as signs — natural-signs. Signs for 'people who are aware' (taqwa-flavored address). Rivers beneath believers in Gardens — paradise. Fire for those who ignore signs — hell. 'Subhanaka Allahumma' and 'al-hamdu lillahi' uttered by inhabitants of paradise — praise. Believers and disbelievers as groups addressed.

10:11.notes: God's patient deferral of punishment — divine-decree. Past generations destroyed when they wronged and rejected messengers — punishment-of-past-nations and prophethood-general. Successors made on earth — mankind addressed implicitly. Disbelievers as group warned.

10:15.notes: Demand to change or replace the Quran — denial-of-revelation and the-quran. Two explicit Qul commands. Fear of 'torment of a terrible Day' — day-of-judgment. Prophet follows only revelation — prophethood-general.

10:17.notes: Fabricating lies about Allah and denying revelations — denial-of-revelation. Worship of false intercessors alongside Allah — shirk and intercession. 'Subhanahu wa ta'ala' uttered — praise. Qul command present. Mankind as a single community then differing — mankind. Knowledge of heavens and earth belongs to Allah — knowledge.

10:22.notes: Storm at sea, sincere du'a in distress — dua-distress (uttered supplication 'If You save us, we will be among the appreciative'). Address 'O people' — mankind. Sea and wind as natural-signs. After rescue they transgress on earth — corruption-on-earth. Invoking Allah sincerely when in peril implies tawhid in extremis.

10:24.notes: Parable of rain, plants, beautified earth then God's command destroying it overnight — natural-signs, provision, divine-decree. Addressed to 'people who reflect' — mankind implied.

10:25.notes: Allah invites to the Home of Peace (paradise) and guides whom He wills — paradise and guidance. Paradise described for those who do good; Fire for those who earned evil — paradise, hell. Judgment with equity — justice. Believers and disbelievers as groups.

10:28.notes: Gathering all on the Day, separating polytheists from their false partners — day-of-judgment, shirk, polytheists. False partners disown their worshippers — reckoning. Every soul experiences what it sent forward — reckoning. Allah as true master — tawhid.

10:31.notes: Multiple Qul commands. Who provides, who governs — provision, tawhid. Creation repeated by Allah alone — creation. Allah guides to the truth; idols cannot — guidance vs shirk. Allah fully aware — knowledge. Most follow only assumptions — disbelievers.

10:37.notes: Quran as confirmation of prior scriptures — the-quran and previous-scriptures. Challenge to produce a chapter like it — challenge-to-produce. Accusation of forgery — denial-of-revelation. Consequences for the wrongdoers of the past — punishment-of-past-nations. Qul command present.

10:40.notes: Division between those who believe and those who don't — believers, disbelievers. Lord fully aware of mischief-makers — knowledge. 'Say: I have my deeds, you have yours' — qul-statements and prophethood-general (prophetic distancing from disbelievers). Allah does not wrong people — justice implicit but not the explicit subject.

10:45.notes: Gathering on the Day — day-of-judgment, resurrection. Losers who denied meeting Allah — disbelievers, hell. Judgment between communities with fairness — justice. To every nation an appointed time — divine-decree. Multiple Qul commands. Reckoning for every soul.

10:53.notes: 'Say, yes by my Lord it is true' — qul-statements. Day of judgment affirmed as certain. Promise of Allah is true — sovereignty. He gives life and causes death — death-and-dying. Judgment with equity — justice. Disbelievers who wronged would give everything to escape punishment — reckoning.

10:57.notes: 'O people' address — mankind. Quran as advice, healing, guidance, mercy — the-quran, guidance, mercy. 'Say: In Allah's grace and mercy let them rejoice' — qul-statements. Provision from Allah made unlawful/lawful by fabricators — provision. Day of Resurrection for those who fabricate lies — day-of-judgment. Believers named as recipients of mercy.

10:61.notes: Not even atom's weight escapes Allah's knowledge — knowledge. Allah's friends (awliya) who believe and have taqwa — believers, taqwa. Good news in this life and hereafter — paradise. Power and hearing/knowledge belong to Allah — sovereignty. Those invoking others follow only guesswork — shirk. Night for rest, day for visibility as signs — natural-signs and cosmic-bodies. The Quran being recited — the-quran.

10:68.notes: 'Allah has taken a son' — shirk. 'Subhanahu' uttered — praise. He is Self-Sufficient, owns everything — tawhid, sovereignty. Those fabricating lies will not succeed and face severe punishment — disbelief, hell. Qul command present.

10:71.notes: Noah's story — noah. 'In Allah I put my trust' — trust-in-god explicitly stated. Noah's da'wah and rejection — prophethood-general. Saved in the Ark, disbelievers drowned — punishment-of-past-nations, disbelievers.

10:74.notes: After Noah, messengers sent — prophethood-general. Moses and Aaron sent to Pharaoh — moses, aaron, pharaoh. Pharaoh's court acted arrogantly — arrogance (explicitly stated: 'istakbaru'). Called Moses's signs sorcery — sorcery, denial-of-revelation. Contest with sorcerers — miracles. Children of Israel few believers — children-of-israel. Hearts sealed — disbelievers.

10:84.notes: Moses urges his people to trust in Allah — trust-in-god explicitly stated. 'In Allah we put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us victims...' — uttered supplication: dua-protection and dua-distress. 'Deliver us by Your mercy' — dua-distress. Divine instruction to Moses and Aaron to make homes places of worship and establish prayer — prayer. Moses, Aaron, children-of-Israel, pharaoh all named.

10:90.notes: Crossing of the sea, Pharaoh's drowning — moses, pharaoh, children-of-israel, punishment-of-past-nations. Pharaoh's deathbed declaration of tawhid — tawhid. His preserved body as a sign — miracles. Children of Israel settled and provided good things — provision. Their disputes to be judged on Day of Resurrection — day-of-judgment. Pharaoh's prior disbelief and corruption — disbelief.

10:94.notes: Ask those who read prior scripture — previous-scriptures, people-of-the-book. Truth from your Lord — the-quran. People of Jonah as unique example of beneficial belief — jonah. Had Allah willed all would believe — divine-decree. 'Say, look at what is in the heavens' — qul-statements. Saving messengers and believers — prophethood-general. Guidance for whoever accepts, detriment for whoever strays — guidance. Mankind addressed implicitly throughout.

10:104.notes: 'Say, O people' (twice) — qul-statements, mankind. Rejection of false gods, worship of Allah alone — tawhid, shirk. Commanded to be of believers and monotheists, not polytheists — believers, polytheists. None removes harm except Allah — power. 'He is the Forgiver, the Merciful' — mercy. Truth has come; whoever is guided benefits themselves — guidance.

10:109.notes: Follow what is revealed — the-quran, prophethood-general. 'Be patient until Allah issues His judgment' — patience explicitly commanded. 'He is the Best of judges' — justice, divine-decree.

84:1.notes: The sky rupturing and earth being leveled are classic eschatological signs preceding the Hour. The sky and earth hearkening to their Lord asserts God's sovereignty over creation.

84:6.notes: Opens with 'O man' (ya ayyuha al-insan) — universal address to mankind. Contrasts the righteous given their book in the right hand (easy reckoning, paradise implied) with the wicked given it behind their back (hell/blaze). Verse 15 closes with God watching him — the Knowledge attribute. Disbelief is implicit in the wicked man's assumption he would never return (denial of resurrection/reckoning).

84:16.notes: God swears by twilight, night, and the full moon — cosmic-bodies and natural-signs. The section then challenges why they do not believe and do not bow when the Quran is recited — tagging the-quran and denial-of-revelation. Disbelievers addressed implicitly ('they do not believe', 'they do not bow down').

84:22.notes: Verse 22 names those who disbelieve and are in denial. Verse 23 asserts Allah's complete knowledge of what they conceal. Verse 24 contains 'inform them' (bashshirhum) — a command to the Prophet similar to a qul-statement pattern, though the imperative here is 'fabashshirhum' not 'qul'; tagging qul-statements is borderline. Punishment threatened — tagged under hell/punishment. Removed punishment-of-past-nations as this is a forward threat, not a historical example. Confidence medium on qul-statements.

84:25.notes: Short closing verse contrasting believers who do good deeds with the disbelievers of the previous section. 'Do good deeds' explicitly names righteous conduct. 'Undiminished reward' points to paradise.
